category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The transcription factor common to somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages, often retained as a diagnostic marker in their respective adenomas, is [___].
back:
• PIT-1 (Pituitary-specific positive transcription factor 1)
• Regulates differentiation of these three cell types
• Used to classify plurihormonal adenomas

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 35-year-old male presents with loss of libido, impotence, and bitemporal hemianopsia. Serum testosterone is low. Which anterior pituitary hormone is most likely elevated?
back:
• Prolactin (Lactotroph Adenoma)
• High Prolactin inhibits GnRH pulsatility
• Results in decreased LH/FSH and low testosterone

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the liver in mediating the tissue-growth effects of excessive Growth Hormone (GH) in Acromegaly.
back:
• GH stimulates hepatic synthesis of IGF-1
• IGF-1 (Insulin-like Growth Factor-1) promotes soft tissue and bone growth
• Serum IGF-1 is more stable than GH for diagnosis

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the response to high-dose dexamethasone suppression in Cushing Disease versus Ectopic ACTH Syndrome.
back:
• Cushing Disease: ACTH and Cortisol levels suppress
• Ectopic ACTH: No suppression of ACTH or Cortisol
• Pituitary tumors remain partially sensitive to feedback; ectopic sources are autonomous

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the physiological consequence of Gonadotroph (FSH/LH) deficiency in premenopausal females.
back:
• Amenorrhea (absence of menses)
• Infertility due to anovulation
• Atrophy of secondary sexual characteristics

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The most sensitive clinical screening test to distinguish primary thyroid failure from secondary (pituitary-related) hypothyroidism is measuring serum [___].
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• High in primary (loss of feedback)
• Low or inappropriately normal in secondary

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: An 8-year-old boy presents with height significantly above the 97th percentile and coarse facial features. Name the condition and the status of his epiphyseal plates.
back:
• Gigantism
• Epiphyseal plates are open (unfused)
• Caused by somatotroph adenoma secreting excess GH

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain why acute pituitary apoplexy results in life-threatening cardiovascular collapse.
back:
• Sudden loss of ACTH leads to acute adrenal crisis
• Causes profound glucocorticoid deficiency
• Associated with rapid increase in intracranial pressure

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the diagnostic hormone profiles of Pituitary Cushing's vs. Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency.
back:
• Cushing's: High ACTH and High Cortisol
• Secondary Insufficiency: Low ACTH and Low Cortisol
• Both are primary pituitary pathologies

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the three hormones most commonly deficient in panhypopituitarism that require immediate clinical replacement.
back:
• ACTH (to prevent adrenal crisis)
• TSH (to maintain metabolism)
• GH (in children to allow growth)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The common transcription factor required for the differentiation of somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary is [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Essential for the development of GH, PRL, and TSH producing cells
• Retained in respective pituitary adenomas for diagnostic classification

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with enlarging shoe size, coarse facial features, and a protruding jaw. Initial screening reveals an elevated IGF-1 level. Identify the likely hormone excess and the most sensitive diagnostic test.
back:
• Hormone: Growth Hormone (GH) excess (Acromegaly)
• Diagnostic Test: Failure to suppress serum GH after an oral glucose load
• Pathophysiology: GH stimulates hepatic secretion of IGF-1

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the optic chiasm in the visual manifestations of expanding anterior pituitary macroadenomas.
back:
• Upward tumor expansion compresses the decussating fibers
• Location: Optic chiasm fibers from the nasal retinas are affected
• Clinical Result: Bitemporal hemianopsia (loss of lateral visual fields)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the response to high-dose dexamethasone suppression testing between Cushing disease and ectopic ACTH secretion.
back:
• Cushing Disease (Pituitary): High-dose dexamethasone suppresses ACTH and cortisol levels
• Ectopic ACTH (e.g., Small Cell Lung Cancer): No suppression of ACTH levels regardless of dose

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Define the cause and clinical hallmark of Nelson Syndrome in post-adrenalectomy patients.
back:
• Cause: Loss of feedback inhibition on a pre-existing corticotroph microadenoma
• Clinical Hallmark: Hyperpigmentation due to excessively high ACTH levels (MSH-like activity)
• Nature: Aggressive tumor growth causing mass effects

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Postpartum ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary following severe obstetric hemorrhage and shock is termed [___].
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome
• Mechanism: Pregnancy-induced pituitary hypertrophy outstrips its low-pressure venous blood supply
• Manifestation: Failure of lactation and secondary hypoadrenalism

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea and galactorrhea. Serum prolactin is 400 ng/mL. Identify the first-line pharmacologic treatment and its mechanism.
back:
• Treatment: Dopamine agonists (e.g., Bromocriptine or Cabergoline)
• Mechanism: Binds D2 receptors on lactotrophs to mimic hypothalamic inhibitory factors
• Result: Suppression of PRL secretion and tumor shrinkage

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the intracellular mechanism of somatic GNAS mutations in somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Mutation: Abrogates the GTPase activity of Gs-alpha subunit
• Pathway: Constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase leads to high cAMP levels
• Outcome: Persistent cellular proliferation and GH hypersecretion

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the skeletal impact of excessive Growth Hormone (GH) before versus after epiphyseal closure.
back:
• Pre-closure (Gigantism): Generalized increase in body size with disproportionately long limbs
• Post-closure (Acromegaly): Bone thickening (prognathism, hand/foot enlargement) without increased height

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: State the primary cause and defining clinical urgency of pituitary apoplexy.
back:
• Cause: Sudden hemorrhage into a pituitary adenoma
• Signs: Excruciating headache, diplopia, and cardiovascular collapse
• Nature: A neurosurgical emergency due to acute hypopituitarism and mass effect

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The anterior pituitary hormone primarily responsible for stimulating the adrenal cortex to produce glucocorticoids like cortisol is [___].
back:
• Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
• Derived from the precursor pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
• Secreted by corticotrophs

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with enlargement of the jaw (prognathism), sausage-like thickening of the fingers, and new-onset glucose intolerance. The likely underlying hormone abnormality involves an excess of [___].
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Leads to hepatic secretion of Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Diagnosis: Acromegaly (post-pubertal GH excess)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of dopamine as the primary inhibitory factor in the regulation of prolactin secretion.
back:
• Secreted by the hypothalamus
• Acts as a Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF)
• Interruption of dopamine flow (stalk effect) results in hyperprolactinemia

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical manifestations of Growth Hormone (GH) excess in prepubertal children versus post-epiphyseal adults.
back:
• Gigantism (Children): Generalized increase in body size; disproportionately long arms/legs
• Acromegaly (Adults): Enlargement of hands/feet, facial coarsening, and viscera (liver/heart) growth

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the classic visual field defect associated with a pituitary macroadenoma extending superiorly into the suprasellar region.
back:
• Bitemporal hemianopsia
• Caused by compression of decussating fibers in the optic chiasm
• Affects lateral visual fields

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The clinical condition characterized by the rapid expansion of an ACTH-secreting pituitary tumor following the surgical removal of both adrenal glands is termed [___].
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Manifests with mass effects and skin hyperpigmentation
• Due to loss of feedback inhibition by adrenal corticosteroids

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 30-year-old female presents with spontaneous milky nipple discharge (galactorrhea) and amenorrhea. Laboratory testing confirms a prolactinoma. Identify the primary physiologic hormone suppressed by this condition.
back:
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
• Suppression results in decreased LH and FSH
• Leads to infertility and sexual dysfunction

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the biological function of the transcription factor PIT-1 in anterior pituitary differentiation and adenoma classification.
back:
• Regulates differentiation of somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs
• Retained in Somatotroph, Lactotroph, and Thyrotroph adenomas
• Essential for GH, PRL, and TSH synthesis

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the typical clinical presentation of functioning pituitary adenomas with that of non-functioning (silent) adenomas.
back:
• Functioning: Endocrine syndromes (e.g., Cushing disease, Acromegaly)
• Non-functioning: Mass effects (headache, bitemporal hemianopsia) and hypopituitarism

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the most common type of hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma.
back:
• Prolactin-secreting (Lactotroph) adenoma
• Accounts for roughly 30% of clinically recognized cases
• Frequently presents as a microadenoma in women

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: IGF-1 as the primary diagnostic screen for GH excess.
front: In the diagnosis of a growth hormone-secreting somatotroph adenoma, the most reliable marker used to screen for acromegaly is [___].
back:
Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1).
• Levels are stable throughout the day compared to GH.
• IGF-1 mediates most somatic growth effects of GH.
• Failure to suppress GH after oral glucose confirms diagnosis.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Prolactinoma pathophysiology and its inhibitory effect on GnRH.
front: A 28-year-old female presents with milky nipple discharge and secondary amenorrhea. MRI reveals a 0.8 cm intrasellar mass. Identify the most likely hormone abnormality and its effect on the reproductive axis.
back:
Hyperprolactinemia (Lactotroph Adenoma).
• Hormone: Markedly elevated Prolactin.
• Effect: Prolactin inhibits GnRH release from the hypothalamus.
• Result: Low FSH and LH levels leading to infertility and amenorrhea.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Impact of epiphyseal closure on GH clinical manifestations.
front: Explain how the timing of growth hormone hypersecretion determines whether a patient develops gigantism or acromegaly.
back:
• Pre-pubertal: GH excess before epiphyseal closure leads to gigantism (increased linear height).
• Post-pubertal: GH excess after epiphyseal closure leads to acromegaly (acral and soft tissue growth; no increased height).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Biochemical differentiation of ACTH-dependent Cushing Syndrome.
front: Contrast the hormone level response to a high-dose dexamethasone suppression test in a patient with a corticotroph adenoma versus a patient with an ectopic ACTH-secreting tumor.
back:
• Corticotroph Adenoma (Cushing Disease): ACTH and Cortisol levels typically suppress with high doses.
• Ectopic ACTH (e.g., Small Cell Lung Cancer): Secretion is autonomous and fails to suppress regardless of dose.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the expected serum levels of TSH and Free T4 in a patient with a rare functioning thyrotroph adenoma.
back:
• TSH: Inappropriately elevated or normal.
• Free T4/T3: Elevated.
• Clinically: Presents with secondary hyperthyroidism, distinguished from primary hyperthyroidism where TSH is suppressed by high T4.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Local mass effects of pituitary tumors on the optic chiasm.
front: The classic visual manifestation of a large pituitary macroadenoma compressing the decussating fibers of the optic chiasm is [___].
back:
Bitemporal hemianopsia.
• Caused by pressure on fibers from the nasal retinas.
• Leads to loss of both lateral visual fields.
• Common presenting sign of non-functioning gonadotroph adenomas.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Pituitary Apoplexy as a neurosurgical and endocrine emergency.
front: A patient with a known pituitary adenoma suddenly develops an excruciating headache, diplopia, and acute cardiovascular collapse. Name the likely condition and its immediate hormonal consequence.
back:
Pituitary Apoplexy.
• Consequence: Acute panhypopituitarism (total hormone deficiency).
• Pathophysiology: Sudden hemorrhage or infarction into a pre-existing adenoma causing rapid enlargement and tissue destruction.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Hormonal feedback loops and POMC derivatives.
front: Explain why patients with Nelson Syndrome develop intense skin hyperpigmentation following bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing Disease.
back:
• Mechanism: Loss of cortisol feedback causes massive ACTH secretion from the existing pituitary tumor.
• Hyperpigmentation: ACTH is derived from POMC, which also produces Melanocyte-Stimulating Hormone (MSH).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Functional vs. non-functional adenoma clinical presentation.
front: Contrast the typical clinical presentation of a gonadotroph adenoma with that of a somatotroph adenoma.
back:
• Gonadotroph: Usually non-functional (silent); presents with mass effects (vision loss, headache) or hypopituitarism.
• Somatotroph: Functional; presents with GH-excess syndromes (gigantism/acromegaly) and metabolic disorders (diabetes).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Threshold and sequence of hormone loss in hypopituitarism.
front: State the minimum percentage of anterior pituitary parenchyma that must typically be lost before clinical hypopituitarism manifests.
back:
Approximately 75%.
• Sequence of loss: GH usually first, followed by FSH/LH, TSH, and finally ACTH.
• Causes: Non-functional macroadenomas, Sheehan syndrome, or surgical ablation.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Local Mass Effects of Pituitary Tumors
front: An expanding anterior pituitary macroadenoma that compresses the decussating fibers at the optic chiasm classically results in [___].
back:
• Bitemporal hemianopsia
• Loss of lateral (temporal) visual fields
• Signs of increased intracranial pressure (headache, nausea)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with prognathism, sausage-like fingers, and a failing glucose tolerance test. Which hormone and downstream mediator are most likely elevated?
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Result of a functioning somatotroph adenoma

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which hyperprolactinemia results in amenorrhea and infertility in females.
back:
• Elevated Prolactin (PRL) inhibits hypothalamic GnRH release
• Decreased GnRH leads to low FSH and LH levels
• Disruption of the LH surge prevents ovulation

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Differential Diagnosis of ACTH-Dependent Cushing Syndrome
front: Contrast the diagnostic response to a high-dose dexamethasone suppression test in Pituitary Cushing Disease versus Ectopic ACTH Syndrome.
back:
• Cushing Disease: ACTH levels are suppressed; pituitary adenomas retain partial feedback sensitivity
• Ectopic ACTH: No suppression; nonpituitary tumors (e.g., small-cell lung cancer) are completely autonomous

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the pharmacological mechanism used to treat lactotroph adenomas without surgical intervention.
back:
• Dopamine receptor agonists (e.g., Bromocriptine)
• Mimic the hypothalamic Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF)
• Inhibit prolactin secretion and induce tumor shrinkage

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The most common form of anterior pituitary ischemic necrosis, occurring due to obstetric hemorrhage and hypovolemia, is termed [___].
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome
• Clinical features: Failure of postpartum lactation, amenorrhea, and loss of pubic/axillary hair

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A patient with prior bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing Syndrome presents with skin hyperpigmentation and an enlarging sella turcica. What is the diagnosis and hormone status?
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Elevated ACTH and Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
• Loss of adrenal corticosteroid feedback on a corticotroph microadenoma

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain how somatotroph adenomas induce metabolic disturbances such as secondary diabetes mellitus.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH) exerts anti-insulin effects on peripheral tissues
• GH stimulates hepatic gluconeogenesis
• Persistent GH excess leads to impaired glucose tolerance

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical manifestations of excessive Growth Hormone (GH) based on the status of epiphyseal plates.
back:
• Children (Pre-closure): Gigantism (generalized increase in body size, long limbs)
• Adults (Post-closure): Acromegaly (growth of face, hands, feet; viscera enlargement)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the hormones synthesized from the Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) precursor by pituitary corticotrophs.
back:
• Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
• Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH)
• POMC is a glycosylated polypeptide precursor

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In the anterior pituitary, somatotrophs produce [___], which stimulates the hepatic secretion of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1).
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Responsible for linear growth in children
• Regulates carbohydrate and lipid metabolism in adults
• Overproduction leads to gigantism or acromegaly

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 35-year-old female presents with milky nipple discharge and secondary amenorrhea. Serum pregnancy test is negative. Identify the likely hormone involved and the associated clinical manifestation name.
back:
• Hormone: Prolactin (hyperprolactinemia)
• Manifestation: Galactorrhea and amenorrhea
• Common in lactotroph adenomas
• Results in interference with the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the optic chiasm in the visual manifestations of an expanding anterior pituitary macroadenoma.
back:
• Upward growth compresses the optic chiasm
• Specifically damages decussating nasal retinal fibers
• Results in bitemporal hemianopsia (loss of lateral visual fields)
• Often accompanied by headache and increased intracranial pressure

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the hormonal effects of Growth Hormone (GH) excess in prepubertal patients versus postpubertal adults.
back:
• Prepubertal: Gigantism; increased linear growth due to open epiphyses
• Postpubertal: Acromegaly; soft tissue overgrowth and bone thickening (hands/feet/jaw)
• Both show elevated IGF-1 and failure of GH suppression by glucose

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Specify the laboratory hallmark of Cushing Disease in terms of ACTH and cortisol levels.
back:
• Elevated serum ACTH (pituitary origin)
• Elevated serum cortisol (adrenal response)
• Cortisol suppresses with high-dose dexamethasone
• Differentiates from ACTH-independent adrenal tumors where ACTH is low

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The condition characterized by failure of postpartum lactation and loss of pubic hair due to ischemic infarction of the anterior pituitary is [___].
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome
• Caused by obstetric hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock
• Results in panhypopituitarism
• Pituitary is susceptible due to physiological hypertrophy during pregnancy

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with decreased libido, impotence, and low testosterone. LH and FSH are inappropriately low. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism
• Secondary to gonadotroph cell deficiency or pituitary mass effect
• Manifests as loss of secondary sexual characteristics
• Requires differentiation from primary testicular failure (where LH/FSH would be high)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the 'Stalk Effect' mechanism that leads to hyperprolactinemia in patients with non-functional pituitary macroadenomas.
back:
• Tumor compresses the pituitary stalk
• Interrupts dopamine (Prolactin Inhibitory Factor) delivery from hypothalamus
• Causes disinhibition of normal lactotrophs
• Results in modest prolactin elevation despite no tumor secretion

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the response of pituitary-sourced ACTH versus ectopic ACTH (e.g., small cell lung cancer) to a high-dose dexamethasone suppression test.
back:
• Pituitary (Cushing Disease): ACTH and cortisol levels are suppressed
• Ectopic ACTH: No suppression occurs; levels remain high
• Ectopic sources are autonomous of pituitary feedback mechanisms

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: State the most common cell-type lineage transcription factor expressed by somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph cells.
back:
• PIT-1
• Regulates development of GH, Prolactin, and TSH secreting cells
• Mutations lead to combined pituitary hormone deficiency
• Used as an immunohistochemical marker in pituitary adenoma classification

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The lineage-specific transcription factor required for the differentiation of somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary is [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Essential for growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), and TSH production
• Retained in corresponding pituitary adenomas.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 35-year-old male presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and enlarged hands and feet. He fails to suppress serum growth hormone levels after an oral glucose load. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Somatotroph adenoma (Acromegaly)
• Characterized by IGF-1 excess
• Features include prognathism, sausage-like fingers, and organomegaly.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain why patients with Nelson syndrome (ACTH-secreting tumors following bilateral adrenalectomy) exhibit skin hyperpigmentation.
back:
• ACTH is synthesized from pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
• POMC is also a precursor for melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH)
• Excess ACTH production involves high MSH levels, stimulating melanocytes.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical manifestations of growth hormone (GH) excess before versus after the closure of epiphyseal plates.
back:
• Before: Gigantism (generalized increase in body size; disproportionately long limbs)
• After: Acromegaly (enlarged facial bones/mandible, soft tissue thickening, visceral enlargement).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Name the classic visual field defect associated with a pituitary macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm.
back:
• Bitemporal hemianopsia
• Caused by compression of decussating nasal retinal fibers
• Loss of both lateral (temporal) visual fields.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The primary inhibitory hypothalamic factor responsible for regulating the secretion of prolactin from the anterior pituitary is [___].
back:
• Dopamine (Prolactin Inhibitory Factor)
• Interruption of the pituitary stalk causes hyperprolactinemia due to loss of this inhibition.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 28-year-old female presents with failure to lactate and secondary amenorrhea following a pregnancy complicated by massive obstetric hemorrhage. Identify the underlying condition.
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome (Postpartum Ischemic Necrosis)
• Physiological pituitary enlargement in pregnancy leads to relative hypoxia
• Hemorrhagic shock causes infarction of the anterior lobe.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: How do functioning lactotroph adenomas typically manifest in premenopausal women compared to men?
back:
• Women: Amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility (early diagnosis)
• Men: Loss of libido, erectile dysfunction, and late-stage mass effects (e.g., headache, visual defects).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the hormone levels and skin appearance of primary (adrenal) versus secondary (pituitary) hypoadrenalism.
back:
• Primary (Addison): High ACTH; hyperpigmentation of skin/creases
• Secondary (Pituitary): Low ACTH; skin pallor (deficiency of melanotropins).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Define the clinical hallmarks of 'Pituitary Apoplexy'.
back:
• Sudden excruciating headache
• Diplopia (oculomotor nerve pressure)
• Acute hypopituitarism and cardiovascular collapse
• Neurosurgical emergency often involving hemorrhage into an adenoma.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Anterior pituitary somatotrophs are responsible for the synthesis of [___], the primary driver of tissue overgrowth in acromegaly.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Stimulates hepatic secretion of IGF-1
• Leads to soft tissue and bone enlargement

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 32-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility. Laboratory evaluation reveals high serum prolactin. Identify the most likely underlying lesion and its hormonal interaction.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary tumor
• High prolactin inhibits GnRH release, disrupting the menstrual cycle

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the diagnostic utility of the oral glucose load test in a patient suspected of having a somatotroph adenoma.
back:
• Failure to suppress GH levels is diagnostic
• Normally, glucose suppresses GH production
• Confirms autonomous hormone secretion regardless of pituitary size

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical manifestations of Growth Hormone (GH) excess in a prepubertal child versus a 50-year-old male.
back:
• Prepubertal: Gigantism (increased body size, long arms/legs due to open epiphyses)
• Adult: Acromegaly (prognathism, enlarged hands/feet, thickened fingers, and visceral enlargement)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the pharmacological step used to medically manage a lactotroph adenoma causing hyperprolactinemia.
back:
• Administration of dopamine receptor agonists (e.g., bromocriptine)
• Mimics hypothalamic PIF (Prolactin Inhibitory Factor)
• Results in tumor shrinkage and normalization of serum prolactin

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The characteristic visual field abnormality produced by an expanding pituitary macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm is [___].
back:
• Bitemporal hemianopsia
• Caused by compression of decussating fibers
• Associated with signs of elevated intracranial pressure (headache, nausea)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A patient presents with weight gain, truncal obesity, and abdominal striae. Lab tests show elevated ACTH and hypercortisolism. Describe the specific condition and a common non-endocrine skin finding.
back:
• Cushing Disease (pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma)
• Hyperpigmentation (due to MSH activity in ACTH precursors)
• Differentiated from Cushing Syndrome (general hypercortisolism)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A patient with a known pituitary adenoma suddenly develops an excruciating headache, diplopia, and acute hypotension. Distinguish this event from a standard enlarging mass.
back:
• Pituitary Apoplexy (acute hemorrhage into an adenoma)
• Neurosurgical emergency; causes rapid enlargement
• Can lead to sudden death or acute panhypopituitarism

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the serum Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) and T4 levels in primary hypothyroidism versus central (secondary) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH, Low T4 (loss of feedback inhibition)
• Central: Low/Normal TSH, Low T4 (pituitary/hypothalamic failure)
• Central hypothyroidism is usually part of panhypopituitarism

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the most frequent hormone deficiencies encountered in a patient with total anterior pituitary destruction.
back:
• GH (growth failure in children)
• Gonadotropins (amenorrhea, loss of libido)
• TSH (hypothyroidism)
• ACTH (hypoadrenalism/pallor)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In a female patient presenting with amenorrhea and galactorrhea due to a pituitary microadenoma, the high-yield diagnostic hormone to measure in serum is [___].
back:
• Prolactin (PRL)
• Elevated levels (>200 ng/mL) typically indicate a lactotroph adenoma
• Inhibits GnRH, leading to decreased FSH and LH

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A middle-aged man presents with progressive enlargement of hands, feet, and jaw (prognathism). Identify the likely hormone excess and its primary secondary hepatic mediator.
back:
• Hormone: Growth Hormone (GH)
• Mediator: Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Pathology: Somatotroph Adenoma (Acromegaly)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the mechanism by which a large, non-secretory suprasellar mass causes mild elevations in serum prolactin levels despite not being a prolactinoma.
back:
• Stalk Effect: Mass compresses the pituitary stalk
• Interruption: Blocks delivery of hypothalamic dopamine (Prolactin-Inhibiting Factor) to the anterior lobe
• Result: Loss of normal inhibitory tone leads to hyperprolactinemia

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical presentation of somatotroph adenomas in prepubertal children versus postpubertal adults regarding skeletal growth.
back:
• Prepubertal: Gigantism; generalized increase in body size and long limbs due to open epiphyses
• Postpubertal: Acromegaly; growth of small bones (hands/feet), facial bones, and viscera due to closed epiphyses

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Specify the first-line pharmacological agent used to manage hyperprolactinemia and its specific receptor target.
back:
• Agent: Bromocriptine (or Cabergoline)
• Target: Dopamine D2 receptor agonist
• Effect: Directly inhibits prolactin secretion and induces tumor shrinkage

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary occurring as a complication of severe postpartum hemorrhage and hypotension is clinically known as [___].
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome
• Caused by relative hypoxia of the physiologically enlarged gestational pituitary
• Manifests as failure of lactation and loss of pubic hair

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A patient with a known pituitary macroadenoma suddenly develops an excruciating headache, visual loss, and acute cardiovascular collapse. Identify the most likely pathophysiology.
back:
• Pituitary Apoplexy
• Sudden hemorrhage into a pituitary tumor
• Causes rapid expansion, mass effect, and acute panhypopituitarism

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the pathophysiology of Nelson syndrome following bilateral adrenalectomy in a patient previously treated for Cushing disease.
back:
• Loss of negative feedback inhibition by adrenal corticosteroids
• Rapid growth of a pre-existing ACTH-secreting pituitary microadenoma
• Manifestations: Hyperpigmentation (due to MSH/POMC) and local mass effects

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the skin manifestations and ACTH levels in primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) versus secondary hypopituitarism.
back:
• Addison: Hyperpigmentation present; ACTH levels high (cross-reactivity with MSH)
• Secondary: Skin pallor/no pigment changes; ACTH levels low
• Aldosterone: Deficient in primary; normal in secondary

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Name the classic visual field defect produced by an enlarging pituitary adenoma and the specific neuro-anatomic structure it compresses.
back:
• Defect: Bitemporal hemianopsia
• Structure: Optic chiasm (compression of decussating nasal retinal fibers)
• Clinical Significance: Most common local mass effect of macroadenomas

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In adults with somatotroph adenomas, the persistent elevation of [___] stimulates hepatic secretion of IGF-1, leading to the clinical manifestations of acromegaly.
back:
● Growth Hormone (GH)
● Leads to soft tissue overgrowth
● Causes visceral enlargement (liver/heart)
● Increases bone density in spine/hips

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, infertility, and milky nipple discharge (galactorrhea). If a pituitary lesion is present, the most likely underlying pathophysiology is [___].
back:
● Hyperprolactinemia (Lactotroph Adenoma)
● Prolactin inhibits GnRH pulsatility
● Leads to decreased LH/FSH
● Serum PRL levels typically correlate with tumor size

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the oral glucose loading test in diagnosing GH-secreting somatotroph adenomas.
back:
● Mechanism: Oral glucose normally suppresses GH
● Positive Result: Failure to suppress GH levels
● Significance: Most sensitive standard test for acromegaly

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the physical manifestations of GH excess in a 10-year-old child versus a 45-year-old adult based on their skeletal development status.
back:
● Child (Pre-epiphyseal closure): Gigantism; generalized increase in body size with long limbs
● Adult (Post-epiphyseal closure): Acromegaly; enlarged jaw (prognathism), broadened face, and sausage-like fingers

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the expected hormonal response to the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test in a patient with a pituitary corticotroph microadenoma (Cushing Disease).
back:
● Serum ACTH: Elevated at baseline
● Response: ACTH secretion is suppressed by high doses
● Outcome: Significant reduction in urinary steroid excretion

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The classic visual field abnormality caused by an expanding pituitary macroadenoma compressing the decussating fibers in the optic chiasm is [___].
back:
● Bitemporal hemianopsia
● Loss of both lateral (temporal) fields
● Often associated with headache, nausea, and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A woman experiences massive obstetric hemorrhage followed by failure to lactate and persistent amenorrhea. Identify the likely diagnosis and the state of the posterior pituitary.
back:
● Diagnosis: Sheehan Syndrome (Postpartum Necrosis)
● Pathophysiology: Ischemic infarction of the enlarged anterior lobe
● Posterior Pituitary: Usually unaffected due to independent arterial blood supply

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: How does skin pigmentation differentiate Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's) from Secondary Pituitary Hypofunction?
back:
● Primary: Hyperpigmentation occurs (high ACTH/MSH precursor POMC)
● Secondary: No hyperpigmentation (low ACTH)
● Appearance: Secondary disease often presents with characteristic pallor

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the TSH levels found in Primary Hypothyroidism versus Central (Pituitary) Hypothyroidism in a patient with low T3/T4.
back:
● Primary: TSH is increased (loss of feedback inhibition)
● Central: TSH is low or inappropriately normal
● central indicates failure of the pituitary-thyroid axis

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the clinical manifestations resulting specifically from LH and FSH deficiency in a male patient with a non-functional pituitary macroadenoma.
back:
● Decreased libido
● Impotence (erectile dysfunction)
● Loss of pubic and axillary hair
● Testicular atrophy due to reduced testosterone

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary are all derived from a common precursor that expresses the transcription factor [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Required for the terminal differentiation of these three specific cell lineages.
• Mutations in this factor result in combined pituitary hormone deficiency (GH, PRL, and TSH).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male notes a gradual increase in shoe size and develops a protruding lower jaw (prognathism). Identify the primary elevated hormone and its hepatic mediator.
back:
• Hormone: Growth Hormone (GH).
• Mediator: Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1).
• Condition: Acromegaly (GH excess occurring after epiphyseal closure).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain how a non-functioning suprasellar mass can lead to hyperprolactinemia despite not secreting the hormone itself.
back:
• Pituitary stalk effect.
• Compression interrupts the delivery of hypothalamic dopamine.
• Dopamine is the primary Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF); its loss allows unchecked PRL release.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the effects on skin appearance in functioning corticotroph adenomas versus secondary adrenocortical insufficiency.
back:
• Corticotroph Adenoma: Hyperpigmentation due to high ACTH/POMC levels stimulating melanocytes.
• Secondary Insufficiency: Skin pallor due to deficient ACTH and melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) production.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the specific biochemical response to an oral glucose load used to confirm a diagnosis of suspected GH-secreting adenoma.
back:
• Failure to suppress GH production.
• In normal physiology, glucose loading reduces GH levels.
• This lack of suppression is a highly sensitive diagnostic test for acromegaly.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Expanding anterior pituitary macroadenomas frequently compress decussating fibers at the optic chiasm, resulting in [___].
back:
• Bitemporal hemianopsia.
• Loss of both lateral/temporal visual fields.
• Often accompanied by headache, nausea, and vomiting due to elevated intracranial pressure.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A postpartum female who suffered severe obstetric hemorrhage fails to lactate and develops loss of pubic hair. Identify the most likely underlying pathology.
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome (postpartum ischemic necrosis).
• Anterior pituitary infarction due to hemorrhage/hypotension.
• Pregnancy-induced gland enlargement lacks a corresponding increase in blood supply, creating vulnerability.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of Nelson Syndrome development following bilateral adrenalectomy for treatment of Cushing disease.
back:
• Loss of negative feedback by adrenal corticosteroids.
• Rapid expansion of a pre-existing ACTH-secreting pituitary microadenoma.
• Manifests with mass effects and intense hyperpigmentation.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the skeletal manifestations of GH excess occurring in children versus manifestations in adult patients.
back:
• Gigantism (Children): Generalized increase in body size with disproportionately long arms/legs.
• Acromegaly (Adults): Enlargement of acral bones (hands/feet), facial bones, and visceral organs.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Name the hormone deficiency responsible for growth failure in children with hypopituitarism.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH) deficiency.
• Leads to pituitary dwarfism.
• Must be distinguished from cretinism (thyroid deficiency) and constitutional growth delay.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In adults, the autonomous hypersecretion of growth hormone after epiphyseal closure leads to the clinical condition [___].
back:
• Acromegaly
• Manifestations: Enlarged hands/feet, prognathism (jaw protrusion), and hyperostosis
• Labs: Elevated GH and IGF-1

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility. A pituitary microadenoma is identified. Explain the pathophysiological mechanism causing the amenorrhea.
back:
• Hyperprolactinemia inhibits GnRH pulsatility
• Result: Decreased FSH and LH secretion
• Leads to anovulation and loss of the menstrual cycle

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: How does the Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) distinguish normal GH physiology from a somatotroph adenoma?
back:
• Normal: Hyperglycemia suppresses GH levels
• Adenoma: GH secretion is autonomous and fails to suppress after a glucose load
• Diagnostic for acromegaly

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical skin findings and ACTH levels in Cushing Disease (pituitary adenoma) versus secondary adrenal insufficiency (pituitary failure).
back:
• Cushing Disease: Hyperpigmentation (high ACTH/POMC stimulate melanocytes)
• Secondary Insufficiency: Skin pallor (low ACTH/POMC levels)
• Primary adrenal failure (Addison's) also shows hyperpigmentation

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the primary pharmacological class used to treat functioning lactotroph adenomas and its effect on hormone levels.
back:
• Dopamine Agonists (e.g., Bromocriptine)
• Mechanism: Mimics hypothalamic Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF)
• Effect: Rapidly decreases serum prolactin and reduces tumor size

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The biochemical hallmark of Cushing Disease is hypersecretion of [___] that fails to suppress with low-dose dexamethasone but usually suppresses with high-dose dexamethasone.
back:
• Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH)
• Causes bilateral adrenal cortical hyperplasia
• Leads to excess cortisol production

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 50-year-old male with a large non-functional macroadenoma presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and loss of libido. Which hormonal deficit explains the sexual dysfunction?
back:
• Secondary Hypogonadism
• Deficiency of LH and FSH (Gonadotrophs)
• Result: Low serum testosterone levels

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the mechanism of 'Stalk Effect' hyperprolactinemia in a patient with a non-secreting suprasellar tumor.
back:
• Compression of the pituitary stalk
• Interrupts dopamine flow from the hypothalamus
• Loss of Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF) leads to disinhibition and mild PRL elevation

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the effect of excess GH on the skeletal system in children (pre-pubertal) versus adults (post-pubertal).
back:
• Children (Gigantism): Increased linear growth due to open epiphyses
• Adults (Acromegaly): Bone thickening and soft tissue overgrowth (closed epiphyses)
• Both show elevated IGF-1

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the hormones synthesized by the basophil cell population of the anterior pituitary.
back:
• B-FLAT: 
• FSH (Follicle-stimulating hormone)
• LH (Luteinizing hormone)
• ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone)
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Differentiation of somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary requires the common high-yield transcription factor [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Essential for development of these specific cell lineages.
• Mutations result in combined pituitary hormone deficiency (GH, PRL, and TSH).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 40-year-old male presents with coarse facial features, enlarging hands, and a protruding jaw. Screening reveals elevated IGF-1. Identify the likely pituitary cell type involved and the expected effect on glucose metabolism.
back:
• Somatotrophs (GH-secreting adenoma).
• GH induces peripheral insulin resistance.
• Clinically manifests as impaired glucose tolerance or secondary diabetes mellitus.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the optic chiasm in the visual manifestations of expanding anterior pituitary macroadenomas.
back:
• Compression of decussating fibers at the optic chiasm.
• Results in bitemporal hemianopsia (loss of lateral visual fields).
• Often accompanied by headache and elevated intracranial pressure.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical presentation of growth hormone (GH) excess in pediatric patients versus adult patients.
back:
• Pediatric (Gigantism): Occurs before epiphyseal closure; leads to generalized increase in body size and long limbs.
• Adult (Acromegaly): Occurs after epiphyseal closure; leads to bone thickening (prognathism), visceral enlargement, and soft tissue overgrowth.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Outline why hyperprolactinemia frequently results in amenorrhea and infertility in reproductive-aged females.
back:
• Prolactin inhibits GnRH release from the hypothalamus.
• This leads to decreased secretion of FSH and LH from the anterior pituitary.
• Result is anovulation and disruption of the menstrual cycle.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In the anterior pituitary, [___] cells are the site of synthesis for Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC), the precursor to ACTH and MSH.
back:
• Corticotrophs.
• POMC is cleaved into ACTH, melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH), and endorphins.
• Excessive ACTH production results in Cushing Disease.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A woman suffers severe postpartum hemorrhage followed by failure to lactate and loss of axillary hair. Define the underlying pathophysiology of this pituitary condition.
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome (Postpartum necrosis).
• Pregnancy-induced pituitary enlargement outstrips its low-pressure venous blood supply.
• Obstetric shock causes ischemic infarction of the anterior lobe.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the mechanism behind skin hyperpigmentation in primary adrenal failure compared to its absence in secondary hypoadrenalism.
back:
• Primary: Low cortisol triggers high ACTH and POMC; POMC contains MSH sequences that stimulate melanocytes.
• Secondary: Pituitary failure results in low ACTH/POMC levels, thus no melanocyte stimulation occurs.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the hormone levels of TSH and T4 in primary versus secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: Low T4 with significantly elevated TSH (loss of negative feedback).
• Secondary: Low T4 with inappropriately low or normal TSH (pituitary/hypothalamic failure).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: List the two defining characteristics of Nelson Syndrome following bilateral adrenalectomy.
back:
• Rapid expansion of a pre-existing corticotroph microadenoma due to loss of cortisol feedback.
• Clinically manifests as hyperpigmentation and symptoms of local mass effect (headache, visual defects).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In adults, the chronic hypersecretion of growth hormone (GH) leads to the stimulation of hepatic [___], which is the primary mediator of tissue overgrowth in acromegaly.
back:
• IGF-1 (Insulin-like growth factor-1).
• Mediates bone and soft tissue thickening.
• Measured as a standard screening tool.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A postpartum female presents with failure to lactate, cold intolerance, and loss of pubic hair after an obstetric hemorrhage. Identify the pathophysiology and expected hormone levels.
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome (Ischemic necrosis of anterior pituitary).
• Low Prolactin (PRL), TSH, ACTH, and Gonadotropins (FSH/LH).
• Caused by hypovolemia in a physiologically enlarged gland.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of negative feedback inhibition in the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis when serum T3 and T4 levels are high.
back:
• Elevated T3/T4 inhibits the release of TRH from the hypothalamus.
• Inhibits TSH release from the anterior pituitary.
• Restores metabolic homeostasis.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the serum ACTH levels found in Cushing Disease versus Cushing Syndrome caused by a primary adrenal cortical adenoma.
back:
• Cushing Disease: High ACTH (pituitary source).
• Adrenal Adenoma: Low ACTH (feedback suppression by autonomous cortisol).
• High ACTH leads to hyperpigmentation in pituitary cases.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Pituitary macroadenomas frequently produce bitemporal hemianopsia. Identify the exact structure compressed and the resulting visual defect.
back:
• Structure: Optic chiasm.
• Mechanism: Compression of decussating fibers from the nasal retinas.
• Result: Loss of the temporal (lateral) visual fields.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In the anterior pituitary, Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) are both derived from the large precursor molecule [___].
back:
• Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC).
• Explains why ACTH excess causes hyperpigmentation.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 30-year-old female presents with milky nipple discharge and secondary amenorrhea. If a pituitary microadenoma is present, what are the expected levels of Prolactin and FSH?
back:
• Prolactin: Markedly elevated (>200 ng/mL).
• FSH: Low to suppressed.
• Pathophysiology: High PRL inhibits hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Discuss the clinical and hormonal emergency presented by 'Pituitary Apoplexy'.
back:
• Presentation: Sudden headache, diplopia, and collapse.
• Hormonal Status: Acute panhypopituitarism.
• Risk: Life-threatening hypocortisolism (requires immediate steroid replacement).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the clinical manifestations of GH hypersecretion in children (Gigantism) versus adults (Acromegaly).
back:
• Gigantism: Occurs before epiphyseal closure; results in increased height/long limbs.
• Acromegaly: Occurs after closure; results in enlarged jaw (prognathism), hands, and feet.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the primary hypothalamic inhibitory neurotransmitter that regulates Prolactin secretion and explain the 'stalk effect' on this hormone.
back:
• Neurotransmitter: Dopamine.
• Stalk Effect: Mass compression blocks dopamine flow.
• Result: Paradoxical mild elevation of Prolactin (Hyperprolactinemia).

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: In the laboratory diagnosis of acromegaly, the most reliable and sensitive screening biomarker to measure is [___].
back:
• Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Levels are persistently elevated due to growth hormone (GH) stimulation
• Unlike GH, IGF-1 has a long half-life and stable serum concentrations.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 30-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea and galactorrhea. Serum prolactin is 300 ng/mL. Identify the most likely underlying lesion.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary tumor
• High prolactin inhibits GnRH, leading to decreased LH/FSH and estrogen deficiency.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the mechanism of action by which an enlarging pituitary macroadenoma produces bitemporal hemianopsia.
back:
• Superior/suprasellar extension of the tumor
• Direct mechanical compression of the optic chiasm
• Damage specifically to decussating nerve fibers responsible for lateral (temporal) visual fields.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the skin findings in primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's) with those found in hypopituitarism-induced secondary adrenal insufficiency.
back:
• Primary (Addison's): Hyperpigmentation due to high ACTH/POMC (melanocyte stimulation).
• Secondary (Pituitary): Skin pallor due to ACTH and MSH deficiency.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the neurosurgical emergency characterized by sudden excruciating headache, diplopia, and cardiovascular collapse due to acute tumor hemorrhage.
back:
• Pituitary Apoplexy
• Often occurs into a pre-existing adenoma
• Causes rapid mass expansion and acute panhypopituitarism.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: The form of ischemic pituitary necrosis resulting from severe obstetric hemorrhage and systemic hypotension is known as [___].
back:
• Sheehan Syndrome
• Pregnancy causes physiologic pituitary hypertrophy without increased blood supply
• Leads to failure of postpartum lactation and loss of menses.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with increasing shoe size, coarse facial features, and spade-like hands. GH levels fail to suppress after an oral glucose load. Diagnosis?
back:
• Acromegaly (Somatotroph Adenoma)
• Failure of GH suppression by glucose is diagnostic
• GH excess occurs after epiphyseal plate closure.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: How does the removal of both adrenal glands in a patient with Cushing disease lead to the development of Nelson Syndrome?
back:
• Loss of cortisol-mediated feedback inhibition
• Causes rapid, aggressive growth of a pre-existing ACTH-producing pituitary microadenoma
• Presents with mass effects and intense hyperpigmentation.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the hormonal profiles of 'functioning' versus 'non-functioning' (silent) pituitary adenomas regarding their clinical presentation.
back:
• Functioning: Present early with hormone excess syndromes (e.g., Cushing’s, Gigantism).
• Non-functioning: Present late with mass effects (vision loss) or hypopituitarism due to gland destruction.

category: Enumerate clinical manifestations along with hormone levels of anterior pituitary
front: Name the transcription factor commonly expressed by somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages in the anterior pituitary.
back:
• PIT-1
• Required for the terminal differentiation of these three cell types
• Retained in their corresponding adenomas for diagnostic classification.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas are classified as [___] if their diameter is less than 1 cm and as macroadenomas if they exceed that threshold.
back:
• Microadenomas
• Size is the primary radiologic metric for classification
• Macroadenomas are more likely to cause symptomatic mass effect

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and headaches. Lab tests show normal hormone levels, but imaging reveals a 2.5 cm sellar mass. This tumor most likely belongs to the [___] lineage.
back:
• Gonadotroph (SF-1/GATA-2 lineage)
• Most common "silent" (non-functioning) macroadenoma
• Presents due to local mass effect rather than hormonal excess

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: How do "silent" adenomas differ from functional adenomas in their typical clinical detection and tumor stage?
back:
• Silent: Detected later via mass effect (visual defects, intracranial pressure)
• Functional: Detected earlier due to endocrine syndromes (Cushing, acromegaly)
• Silent tumors are usually macroadenomas at diagnosis

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the histological and immunohistochemical appearance of a "densely granulated" somatotroph adenoma with its "sparsely granulated" counterpart.
back:
• Densely: Acidophilic/eosinophilic; strong, diffuse GH staining
• Sparsely: Chromophobic; weak GH staining
• Sparsely Hallmark: Paranuclear "fibrous bodies" (cytokeratin inclusions)

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the specific lineage transcription factor and the auxiliary receptor used to confirm lactotroph differentiation in a biopsy.
back:
• PIT-1 (Lineage transcription factor)
• ER-alpha (Estrogen Receptor alpha)
• Combined expression confirms lactotroph origin in sparsely/densely granulated variants

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The definitive diagnostic criterion that distinguishes a pituitary carcinoma from a locally invasive aggressive adenoma is the presence of [___].
back:
• Metastases (craniospinal or systemic)
• Histological features (pleomorphism/mitoses) are insufficient for the diagnosis of carcinoma
• Carcinomas are extremely rare (<1% of cases)

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 30-year-old female with prior bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing disease presents with skin hyperpigmentation and a new, large sellar mass. Identify this condition.
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Pathophysiology: Loss of cortisol feedback inhibition on a preexisting corticotroph microadenoma
• Characterized by rapid expansion and aggressive behavior

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the mechanistic specificity of GNAS mutations in somatotroph adenomas compared to thyrotroph or gonadotroph adenomas.
back:
• GNAS encodes Gs-alpha, activating adenyl cyclase
• Somatotroph proliferation is cAMP-dependent (GHRH pathway)
• Thyrotrophs/Gonadotrophs utilize different signaling cascades unaffected by GNAS gain-of-function

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Distinguish between "plurihormonal" adenomas and "null cell" adenomas based on transcription factor expression patterns.
back:
• Plurihormonal: Usually PIT-1 lineage; express multiple hormones (GH, PRL, TSH)
• Null cell: Express no lineage-specific factors (PIT-1, TPIT, SF-1) or hormones

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the lineage-specific transcription factor required for the differentiation of corticotroph cells and their corresponding adenomas.
back:
• TPIT (T-box protein 19)
• Essential for ACTH/POMC synthesis
• Positive in both functional and silent corticotroph adenomas

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The transcription factor [___] is expressed by somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages, and is used to classify their respective pituitary adenomas.
back:
• PIT-1
• Required for differentiation of these three cell types
• Its expression is retained in neoplastic cells for lineage-specific identification

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 35-year-old male with a pituitary macroadenoma presents with visual field defects, headaches, and decreased libido. Laboratory tests show low LH and testosterone. Identify the most likely adenoma type and the mechanism of hypogonadism.
back:
• Non-functioning Gonadotroph Adenoma
• Mass effect destroys adjacent normal gonadotroph cells
• Resulting deficiency in trophic hormones leads to secondary hypogonadism

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain how the immunohistochemical detection of the transcription factor SF-1 distinguishes gonadotroph adenomas from other pituitary tumor lineages.
back:
• SF-1 is specific to gonadotroph differentiation
• It identifies "silent" adenomas that do not secrete hormones
• Distinguishes them from PIT-1 or TPIT positive lineages

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast a functioning Lactotroph Adenoma with a non-functioning Macroadenoma causing "stalk effect" regarding Prolactin levels and clinical presentation.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma: Prolactin usually exceeds 200 ng/mL; proportional to tumor size
• Stalk Effect: Mild prolactin elevation (<100 ng/mL) due to dopamine inhibition loss
• Both can present with bitemporal hemianopsia

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the molecular consequence of GNAS mutations in somatotroph adenomas and the resulting clinical syndrome.
back:
• Constitutive activation of Gs-alpha protein
• Abolished GTPase activity leads to persistent cAMP levels and cell growth
• Results in Acromegaly (adults) or Gigantism (children)

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The characteristic histologic hallmark of pituitary adenomas, which distinguishes them from normal anterior pituitary parenchyma, is the [___].
back:
• Absence of a reticulin network
• Normal pituitary has a rich, compartmentalized reticulin framework
• Neoplasm also displays cellular monomorphism

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient with Cushing Disease undergoes bilateral adrenalectomy but later develops a rapidly enlarging pituitary mass and skin hyperpigmentation. Name the condition and its pathophysiology.
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Loss of cortisol-mediated feedback inhibition on the pituitary
• Pre-existing corticotroph microadenoma undergoes aggressive expansion

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: How does a somatic mutation in the USP8 gene contribute specifically to the pathogenesis of functioning Corticotroph Adenomas?
back:
• USP8 is a deubiquitinase enzyme
• Mutations prevent Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) degradation
• Enhanced EGFR signaling drives excessive ACTH synthesis and cellular proliferation

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the treatment response and microscopic features of "sparsely granulated" versus "densely granulated" somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely Granulated: Slower growing; typically responds well to somatostatin analogues
• Sparsely Granulated: More aggressive; characterized by "fibrous bodies" (cytokeratin inclusions)
• Both cause GH excess

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Define the anatomic size criteria used to distinguish a pituitary microadenoma from a macroadenoma.
back:
• Microadenoma: Less than 1 cm in diameter
• Macroadenoma: Greater than 1 cm in diameter
• Macroadenomas are typically associated with bitemporal hemianopsia

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas are classified by size into microadenomas and macroadenomas based on a diameter threshold of [___].
back:
• Threshold is 1 cm.
• Microadenomas are less than 1 cm.
• Macroadenomas are greater than 1 cm and more likely to produce mass effects.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 28-year-old female presents with cessation of menses and spontaneous milky nipple discharge. MRI reveals a 0.7 cm intrasellar lesion. Identify the most likely adenoma subtype.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma).
• Causes hyperprolactinemia leading to amenorrhea and galactorrhea.
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain how the transcription factor PIT-1 determines the classification of specific pituitary adenoma lineages.
back:
• PIT-1 is required for the differentiation of somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs.
• Adenomas expressing PIT-1 include somatotroph, lactotroph, mammosomatotroph, and thyrotroph adenomas.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the histologic and staining characteristics of Densely Granulated versus Sparsely Granulated somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely Granulated: Eosinophilic, strong/diffuse cytoplasmic GH staining.
• Sparsely Granulated: Chromophobic, weak staining, and characteristic paranuclear "fibrous bodies" (cytokeratin inclusions).
• Sparsely granulated types often behave more aggressively.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the most common subtype of hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma based on hormonal secretion.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma).
• Accounts for approximately 30% of all clinically recognized cases.
• Often presents earlier in females due to menstrual disturbances.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The primary histologic feature distinguishing a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary tissue is the loss of the [___] network.
back:
• Reticulin network.
• Adenomas show cellular monomorphism and lack the supporting connective tissue framework seen in normal parenchyma.
• Results in a soft, gelatinous tumor consistency.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with broadening of facial features, thickening of fingers, and a protruding jaw. Failure to suppress growth hormone after an oral glucose load confirms the diagnosis of [___].
back:
• Acromegaly (Somatotroph Adenoma).
• Occurs after epiphyseal closure.
• Characterized by soft tissue overgrowth and viscero-megaly.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which GNAS mutations lead to cellular proliferation in somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• GNAS encodes the alpha subunit of stimulatory G-protein (Gsα).
• Mutations abrogate GTPase activity, preventing GTP hydrolysis.
• Results in constitutive cAMP generation and unchecked mitogenic signaling.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Distinguish between Cushing Disease and Nelson Syndrome regarding their classification and pathophysiology.
back:
• Cushing Disease: Hypercortisolism caused by an ACTH-secreting pituitary microadenoma.
• Nelson Syndrome: Development of a large, aggressive ACTH-secreting adenoma after surgical removal of adrenals for Cushing treatment.
• Nelson lacks feedback inhibition from adrenal steroids.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the mandatory clinical or pathologic requirement for the definitive diagnosis of pituitary carcinoma.
back:
• Presence of metastases.
• Requires documentation of craniospinal or systemic spread.
• Cytologic features alone are insufficient to distinguish from adenoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Differentiation of somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages from a common precursor cell in the anterior pituitary is regulated by the transcription factor [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Essential for the development of GH, Prolactin, and TSH-secreting cells
• Retention of this factor is used to classify these specific adenoma subtypes

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with coarse facial features, broadening of the lower face, and sausage-like thickening of the fingers. What is the most likely diagnosis and its primary biochemical mediator?
back:
• Somatotroph Adenoma (Acromegaly)
• Excess Growth Hormone (GH) stimulates hepatic secretion of Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
• IGF-1 mediates the characteristic soft tissue and visceral overgrowth

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of the GNAS gene mutation in the development of somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Leads to abrogation of GTPase activity in the Gs-alpha subunit
• Results in constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase
• Causes persistent elevation of cyclic AMP (cAMP)
• cAMP serves as a potent mitogenic stimulus for somatotroph proliferation

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast pituitary microadenomas with macroadenomas based on size thresholds and typical clinical presentations.
back:
• Microadenoma: <1 cm diameter; usually presents with hormonal excess syndromes (e.g., Cushing disease)
• Macroadenoma: >1 cm diameter; often presents with mass effects (e.g., bitemporal hemianopsia) or hypopituitarism

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the primary hypothalamic inhibitory influence on lactotrophs and the pharmacological class used for clinical management.
back:
• Inhibited by Dopamine (Prolactin-Inhibitory Factor)
• Managed with Dopamine receptor agonists (e.g., Bromocriptine)
• These agents effectively shrink tumors and resolve hyperprolactinemia symptoms

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: On light microscopy, the neoplastic cells of a pituitary adenoma typically demonstrate cellular monomorphism and the [___].
back:
• Absence of a significant reticulin network
• Normal pituitary has a delicate reticulin framework surrounding cell nests
• Loss of this framework is a key histological feature of adenomas

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient previously treated with bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing syndrome develops hyperpigmentation and a large, invasive pituitary mass. Identify the condition.
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Caused by loss of inhibitory feedback from adrenal corticosteroids on a corticotroph microadenoma
• Hyperpigmentation results from elevated ACTH precursors (pro-opiomelanocortin)

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain why gonadotroph adenomas usually present with mass effects rather than a specific endocrine syndrome.
back:
• Secretion of FSH and LH is usually inefficient and minimal
• Termed "silent" or non-functioning adenomas
• Tumor expansion leads to bitemporal hemianopsia and hypopituitarism via compression

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast functioning corticotroph adenomas with "silent" corticotroph adenomas regarding biochemical and clinical features.
back:
• Functioning: ACTH-secreting; presents with Cushing disease (hypercortisolism)
• Silent: Expresses ACTH and TPIT immunohistochemically but lacks clinical hypercortisolism; typically larger at diagnosis with mass effects

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the specific transcription factor used to define the corticotroph lineage in the current classification of pituitary tumors.
back:
• TPIT (T-box protein 19)
• Essential for differentiation of corticotroph cells
• Used to identify corticotroph lineage in both functioning and silent adenomas

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The primary histological feature used to distinguish a pituitary adenoma from normal pituitary parenchyma is the absence of a [___] network.
back:
• Reticulin network
• Normal pituitary has a distinct reticulin framework surrounding nests of cells
• Adenomas show complete breakdown of this network

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 35-year-old female presents with amenorrhea and galactorrhea. MRI reveals a 0.7 cm sellar mass. Identify the most likely adenoma subtype and its specific transcription factor.
back:
• Lactotroph adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Transcription factor: PIT-1 (and ER-alpha)
• Most common functioning pituitary adenoma subtype

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of the GNAS gene mutation in the pathogenesis of somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Encodes Gs-alpha subunit
• Mutation inhibits GTPase activity
• Leads to constitutive cAMP generation
• Drives persistent somatotroph proliferation and GH secretion

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the histological and clinical features of "densely granulated" vs. "sparsely granulated" somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely: Acidophilic; strong/diffuse GH staining
• Sparsely: Chromophobic; characteristic paranuclear 'fibrous bodies' (cytokeratin)
• Sparsely granulated variants tend to be more clinically aggressive

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: List the three hormonal products associated with the PIT-1 lineage in pituitary adenoma classification.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Prolactin (PRL)
• Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH)
