category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas derived from the [___] lineage are identified by the expression of Steroidogenic Factor-1 (SF-1) and GATA-2.
back:
• Gonadotroph
• Most are clinically non-functioning (silent)
• Typically present with mass effects rather than hormonal syndromes

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient previously treated with bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing disease now presents with skin hyperpigmentation and a large, invasive sellar mass. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Caused by loss of inhibitory effect of adrenal corticosteroids
• Results in aggressive growth of a corticotroph adenoma

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the physiological sequence that leads to the clinical emergency known as 'pituitary apoplexy.'
back:
• Acute hemorrhage into an existing adenoma
• Rapid lesion expansion
• Compression of adjacent optic chiasm/nerves
• Resultant acute hypopituitarism and potential cardiovascular collapse

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the cellular features of a pituitary adenoma with the normal anterior pituitary gland in routine H&E sections.
back:
• Normal: Polymorphic (mixture of acidophils, basophils, chromophobes)
• Adenoma: Monomorphic (single uniform cell type throughout)
• Adenomas lack the varied staining of a functioning gland

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Define the specific size threshold used to distinguish a pituitary microadenoma from a macroadenoma.
back:
• 1 cm in diameter
• Microadenoma: < 1 cm
• Macroadenoma: > 1 cm

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Lineage-specific transcription factors in pituitary adenoma classification
front: The common progenitor transcription factor expressed in somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages of pituitary adenomas is [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Retained in lineage-specific differentiation
• Essential for identifying sub-types in immunohistochemistry

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 30-year-old female presents with amenorrhea and galactorrhea. MRI reveals an 8 mm intrasellar lesion. Identify the most likely diagnosis and its classification by size.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Classified as a microadenoma (< 1 cm diameter)
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the signal transduction defect caused by somatic GNAS mutations in somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Abolished GTPase activity of Gsα protein
• Constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase
• Persistent cyclic AMP (cAMP) generation
• Leads to unchecked somatotroph proliferation

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the microscopic hallmarks of densely granulated vs. sparsely granulated somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely: Acidophilic cytoplasm, diffuse GH staining
• Sparsely: Chromophobic cells, weak GH staining
• Sparsely feature: Perinuclear 'fibrous bodies' (cytokeratin inclusions)

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Define the anatomical criteria distinguishing a pituitary microadenoma from a macroadenoma.
back:
• Microadenoma: Diameter < 1 cm
• Macroadenoma: Diameter > 1 cm
• Macroadenomas are more likely nonfunctional and present with mass effects

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas derived from the corticotroph lineage are specifically defined by the expression of the transcription factor [___].
back:
• TPIT (T-box protein 19)
• Associated with ACTH, POMC, and MSH production
• Positive in both functional and silent corticotroph adenomas

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient presents with prognathism, sausage-like fingers, and bitemporal hemianopsia. Identify the most likely hormone excess and its transcription factor profile.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH) excess
• Associated with Somatotroph Adenoma
• Transcription factor: PIT-1 positive

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Pituitary apoplexy as a complication of macroadenomas
front: Describe the clinical dynamics and immediate risks of pituitary apoplexy.
back:
• Acute hemorrhage into an existing adenoma
• Rapid tumor expansion causes sudden headache and diplopia
• Risk: Acute hypopituitarism and cardiovascular collapse
• Neurosurgical emergency

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast gonadotroph adenomas with most functioning adenomas regarding their clinical presentation.
back:
• Gonadotroph: Usually nonfunctional (silent); presents with mass effects/hypopituitarism
• Functioning: Presents with specific hormonal syndromes (e.g., Cushing, Acromegaly)
• Gonadotroph markers: SF-1 and GATA-2

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the two histological features that differentiate a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary tissue.
back:
• Cellular monomorphism (uniform cell population)
• Absence of a significant reticulin network
• Normal pituitary shows a diverse mixture of acidophils/basophils/chromophobes

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A pituitary adenoma is clinically designated as a [___] if its diameter exceeds 1 cm.
back:
• Macroadenoma
• Note: Lesions <1 cm are microadenomas
• Size correlates with likelihood of mass effects (e.g., bitemporal hemianopsia).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility. MRI reveals a 0.6 cm sellar lesion. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma
• Often associated with PIT-1 and ERα transcription factor expression.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of the transcription factor PIT-1 in the classification of anterior pituitary lineages.
back:
• PIT-1 expression defines the development of three cell types:
• Somatotrophs (GH)
• Lactotrophs (Prolactin)
• Thyrotrophs (TSH).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast sparsely granulated somatotroph adenomas with the densely granulated variant.
back:
• Sparsely: Chromophobic cells, weak GH staining, contains 'fibrous bodies' (cytokeratin inclusions), more aggressive
• Densely: Eosinophilic cells, strong diffuse GH staining, slower growing.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the specific G-protein subunit mutation found in approximately 40% of somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• GNAS mutation (encoding Gsα)
• Mechanism: Abolishes GTPase activity, leading to constitutive cAMP activation and unchecked cellular proliferation.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Gonadotroph adenomas are typically identified by the immunohistochemical expression of [___] and GATA-2.
back:
• Steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1)
• Most are clinically 'silent' (nonfunctional)
• Usually present as macroadenomas with mass effects.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with prognathism, sausage-like fingers, and new-onset diabetes. Failure to suppress GH during an oral glucose load confirms the diagnosis. The clinical symptoms are primarily mediated by [___].
back:
• Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Secreted by the liver in response to excess Growth Hormone (GH)
• Responsible for soft tissue and bone overgrowth in Acromegaly.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the mechanism by which USP8 mutations contribute to the development of corticotroph adenomas.
back:
• USP8 is a deubiquitinase
• Mutation prevents degradation of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR)
• Result: Enhanced EGFR signaling and increased ACTH production.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast 'silent' pituitary adenomas with true null cell adenomas.
back:
• Silent: Express lineage-specific transcription factors or hormones on IHC but lack clinical symptoms
• Null Cell: Lack any markers of hormonal or lineage differentiation (no PIT-1, TPIT, or SF-1).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the most common combination of hormones secreted by bihormonal (plurihormonal) pituitary adenomas.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH) and Prolactin
• Derived from the common PIT-1 progenitor lineage
• Often associated with mammosomatotroph adenomas.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The most common genetic alteration in approximately 40% of somatotroph adenomas is a somatic activating mutation in the [___] gene, leading to constitutive cAMP activation.
back:
• GNAS gene
• Encodes the α-subunit of the stimulatory G-protein (Gsα)
• Abrogates GTPase activity, preventing the "off" switch for signaling

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with widening fingers, jaw protrusion (prognathism), and new-onset diabetes. Elevated levels of which hepatic-derived factor primarily mediate these clinical findings?
back:
• Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Secreted by the liver in response to excess Growth Hormone (GH)
• Responsible for most acromegalic soft tissue and bone overgrowth

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the two primary histological features that distinguish a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary tissue.
back:
• Cellular monomorphism: All cells appear identical (one hormone type)
• Absent reticulin network: Loss of the supportive connective tissue framework characteristic of normal acini

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the microscopic characteristics of "densely granulated" versus "sparsely granulated" somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely granulated: Acidophilic; strong, diffuse GH staining
• Sparsely granulated: Chromophobic; weak GH staining; contains "fibrous bodies" (paranuclear cytokeratin inclusions); often more aggressive

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Dopamine receptor agonists (e.g., bromocriptine) are first-line therapy for lactotroph adenomas because they act by [___].
back:
• Mimicking Prolactin Inhibitory Factor (PIF)
• Binding D2 receptors on lactotrophs
• Inhibiting prolactin secretion and inducing tumor shrinkage

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: By convention, a pituitary adenoma is classified as a microadenoma if its diameter is less than [___], while those exceeding this threshold are macroadenomas.
back:
• 1 cm (10 mm)
• Macroadenomas (>1 cm) are more likely to cause "mass effects" like bitemporal hemianopsia

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient with a history of bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing syndrome now presents with a large pituitary mass and intense skin hyperpigmentation. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Nelson syndrome
• Pathophysiology: Loss of inhibitory cortisol feedback allows a preexisting corticotroph microadenoma to grow aggressively

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the mechanism by which USP8 mutations promote the development of corticotroph adenomas.
back:
• Encodes a deubiquitinase enzyme
• Mutations prevent the degradation of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR)
• Results in stabilized EGFR signaling, enhancing ACTH production and cell proliferation

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the specific transcription factors required for the PIT-1 lineage versus the gonadotroph lineage adenomas.
back:
• PIT-1 lineage: Requires PIT-1 (Somatotrophs, Lactotrophs, Thyrotrophs)
• Gonadotroph lineage: Requires Steroidogenic Factor-1 (SF-1) and GATA-2

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the high-yield morphological marker for an aggressive subtype of ACTH-secreting tumors characterized by ring-like cytokeratin deposition.
back:
• Crooke hyaline change
• Diagnostic of Crooke cell adenoma
• Caused by high levels of circulating glucocorticoids

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Transcription Factor Lineage in Pituitary Adenomas
front: The transcription factor required for the differentiation of somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages, and commonly used to classify their respective adenomas, is [___].
back: PIT-1 (Pituitary-specific transcription factor 1). It serves as the primary lineage marker for somatotrophs, lactotrophs, mammosomatotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the modern classification of pituitary adenomas.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 40-year-old male presents with new-onset diabetes, thickening of facial skin, and widening of the dental spaces. Serum IGF-1 is significantly elevated. Identify the most likely underlying pituitary tumor.
back: Somatotroph adenoma (GH-secreting). It causes acromegaly in adults, characterized by bone and soft tissue overgrowth, insulin resistance, and elevated hepatic insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) production.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the diagnostic role of immunohistochemical staining for transcription factors versus hormones in identifying 'silent' pituitary adenomas.
back: Silent adenomas may not secrete measurable serum hormones but remain identifiable by their lineage-specific transcription factors (e.g., TPIT for corticotrophs or SF-1 for gonadotrophs), allowing for more precise pathological subtyping.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: An adenoma is found to have chromophobe cells with paranuclear glossy inclusions ('fibrous bodies') on histology. Contrast the clinical aggressiveness of this tumor with its 'densely granulated' counterpart.
back: This is a sparsely granulated somatotroph adenoma. It typically behaves more aggressively and is less responsive to somatostatin analogues than the densely granulated (eosinophilic) somatotroph variant.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the dopamine receptor agonist used to pharmacologically reduce the size and secretion of lactotroph adenomas.
back: Bromocriptine (or Cabergoline). These drugs mimic the natural inhibitory influence of hypothalamic dopamine on lactotroph cells, suppressing prolactin release and inducing tumor involution.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas are classified as macroadenomas when their diameter is equal to or exceeds [___] cm.
back: 1 cm. Microadenomas are defined as being less than 1 cm in diameter, while macroadenomas are 1 cm or larger.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 35-year-old female presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and galactorrhea. Explain the 'stalk effect' as a potential non-neoplastic cause of her elevated prolactin.
back: Any suprasellar mass can compress the pituitary stalk, blocking the inhibitory flow of dopamine from the hypothalamus. This 'disinhibition' causes lactotroph hyperplasia and mild hyperprolactinemia, mimicking a true prolactinoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the mechanism by which hypercortisolism leads to 'Crooke hyaline change' in the non-neoplastic pituitary.
back: High levels of endogenous or exogenous glucocorticoids cause the accumulation of intermediate keratin filaments in the cytoplasm of non-neoplastic ACTH-producing cells, resulting in a pale, homogeneous appearance.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the diagnostic feedback regulation of somatotroph adenomas versus corticotroph adenomas during hormone suppression tests.
back: Somatotrophs: Fail to suppress GH after an oral glucose load. Corticotrophs (Cushing Disease): ACTH and cortisol suppression typically occur only with high-dose dexamethasone, not low-dose.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the two hallmark histological features used to distinguish a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary parenchyma.
back:
1. Cellular monomorphism (a single cell type instead of a mixture).
2. Absence of the reticulin network (the delicate connective tissue supporting normal acini).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Histologically, the two most characteristic features distinguishing pituitary adenomas from the normal anterior pituitary parenchyma are cellular monomorphism and the absence of a significant [___].
back:
• Reticulin network
• This absence accounts for the soft, gelatinous consistency of most adenomas.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 26-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility. MRI reveals an 8mm sellar mass. Identify the most likely diagnosis and the lineage-specific transcription factor involved.
back:
• Diagnosis: Lactotroph adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Transcription factor: PIT-1 (also expresses ERα)
• Note: Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of GNAS mutations in the pathogenesis of somatotroph (Growth Hormone) adenomas.
back:
• Abrogates GTPase activity of the Gsα subunit
• Leads to constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase
• Results in persistent cAMP generation and unchecked cellular proliferation.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the microscopic features of densely granulated vs. sparsely granulated somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely: Acidophilic cytoplasm; strong/diffuse GH staining
• Sparsely: Chromophobic; weak GH staining; contains "fibrous bodies" (paranuclear cytokeratin inclusions).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Define the clinical emergency known as 'pituitary apoplexy'.
back:
• Acute hemorrhage into an adenoma
• Rapid enlargement causing sudden mass effect and hypopituitarism
• Can lead to cardiovascular collapse or sudden death.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: In the classification of pituitary adenomas, corticotroph adenomas are defined by the expression of the transcription factor [___].
back:
• TPIT (also known as Tbx19)
• These tumors typically cause Cushing Disease or Nelson Syndrome.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 50-year-old male presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and headaches. Lab tests show mild hypopituitarism but no hormone excess. Biopsy shows an adenoma expressing SF-1. Identify the tumor type.
back:
• Gonadotroph adenoma
• Usually nonfunctioning (silent)
• Diagnosed by expression of Steroidogenic Factor-1 (SF-1) and GATA-2.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: How do mutations in USP8 contribute to the development of Cushing Disease?
back:
• Encoding a deubiquitinase enzyme
• Prevents degradation of EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor)
• Upregulated EGFR signaling enhances ACTH synthesis and cell growth.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the diagnostic size criteria and typical presentations for pituitary microadenomas vs. macroadenomas.
back:
• Microadenoma: <1 cm; usually presents with hormonal syndromes
• Macroadenoma: >1 cm; usually presents with mass effects (e.g., visual defects) and hypopituitarism.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Which specific pituitary-related tumor is associated with germline DICER1 mutations in children under age 2?
back:
• Pituitary blastoma
• Composed of primitive "small round blue cells"
• Often associated with pleuropulmonary blastoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The [___] gene, encoding the α-subunit of the stimulatory G-protein (Gsα), is somatically mutated in approximately 40% of somatotroph adenomas.
back:
* GNAS
* Leads to constitutive cAMP activation
* Promotes unchecked somatotroph proliferation

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with broadening facial features, protruding lower jaw, and sausage-like thickening of the fingers. The most likely cell type of origin for this tumor is [___].
back:
* Somatotrophs
* Secrete excess Growth Hormone (GH)
* Stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of lineage-specific transcription factors in the classification of PIT-1 versus TPIT positive pituitary adenomas.
back:
* PIT-1: Defines somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages
* TPIT: Defines corticotroph lineage
* Used to classify 'silent' adenomas lacking clinical syndromes

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the microscopic and immunohistochemical features of 'Densely' versus 'Sparsely' granulated somatotroph adenomas.
back:
* Densely: Eosinophilic cells, diffuse GH staining, strong PIT-1
* Sparsely: Chromophobe cells, paranuclear fibrous bodies (cytokeratin+), weak GH staining
* Sparsely variant is often more aggressive

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the primary clinical reason that gonadotroph adenomas are usually diagnosed as macroadenomas rather than microadenomas.
back:
* They are typically 'silent'
* Inefficient hormone secretion (FSH/LH)
* Present only via mass effects (vision loss, headache) once large

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: In the pathologic staging of pituitary tumors, a lesion is defined as a 'macroadenoma' when its maximum diameter exceeds [___] cm.
back:
* 1 cm
* Lesions < 1 cm are microadenomas
* Size correlates with likelihood of sellar erosion and mass effects

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient with a history of bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing syndrome now presents with a large pituitary mass and skin hyperpigmentation. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
* Nelson Syndrome
* Loss of adrenal steroid feedback inhibition
* Aggressive ACTH-producing corticotroph macroadenoma

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the mechanism by which USP8 mutations lead to the development of Cushing disease in corticotroph adenomas.
back:
* USP8 is a deubiquitinase
* Mutated USP8 prevents EGFR degradation
* Enhanced EGFR signaling drives ACTH overproduction and cell growth

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the underlying mechanism of hyperprolactinemia in a lactotroph adenoma versus the 'stalk effect' seen in non-functional masses.
back:
* Adenoma: Autonomous PRL secretion by neoplastic cells
* Stalk Effect: Mass compresses pituitary stalk, blocking hypothalamic dopamine (prolactin-inhibiting factor) reach

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the specific transcription factor used as a diagnostic marker for gonadotroph differentiation in non-functioning pituitary tumors.
back:
* Steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1)
* Distinguishes gonadotroph tumors from null cell adenomas
* GATA-2 is also commonly expressed

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Transcription factor markers in pituitary adenoma classification
front: The common transcription factor expressed by the somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph lineages in pituitary adenomas is [___].
back: PIT-1 (Pituitary-specific transcription factor-1). It is essential for the differentiation and hormone production of Growth Hormone, Prolactin, and TSH cells.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 32-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and loss of libido. MRI reveals a 6 mm sellar mass. Identify the most likely diagnosis and its primary transcription factor marker.
back:
Diagnosis: Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma).
Lineage Marker: PIT-1 (often co-expressing ERα).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the microscopic features of 'densely granulated' vs. 'sparsely granulated' somatotroph adenomas.
back:
Densely granulated: Eosinophilic cytoplasm; diffuse, strong GH staining.
Sparsely granulated: Chromophobic; weak GH staining; contains characteristic paranuclear 'fibrous bodies' (cytokeratin inclusions).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and hypopituitarism but no clinical signs of hormone excess. Distinguish between a 'silent' gonadotroph adenoma and a 'null cell' adenoma using immunohistochemistry (IHC).
back:
Silent Gonadotroph: IHC positive for FSH/LH or transcription factors (SF-1/GATA-2).
Null Cell: IHC negative for all lineage-specific transcription factors and hormones.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Name the dopamine receptor agonist used to medically manage lactotroph adenomas by mimicking natural hypothalamic inhibition.
back: Bromocriptine (or Cabergoline). These dopamine agonists inhibit prolactin secretion and cause tumor shrinkage in most patients.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The definitive clinical criterion required to classify a pituitary neoplasm as a 'Pituitary Carcinoma' rather than an aggressive adenoma is [___].
back: The presence of craniospinal or systemic metastases. Local invasion alone is insufficient for a diagnosis of malignancy in the pituitary.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male with acromegaly shows elevated serum Growth Hormone (GH). Explain the most sensitive biochemical test to confirm autonomous GH secretion.
back: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT). Failure to suppress GH levels to below 1 ng/mL after a glucose load indicates autonomous secretion by a somatotroph adenoma.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Compare the clinical behavior and lineage markers of Corticotroph adenomas associated with Cushing Disease vs. Nelson Syndrome.
back:
Cushing Disease: ACTH excess leads to hypercortisolism.
Nelson Syndrome: Large, aggressive ACTH-secreting tumor develops post-adrenalectomy due to loss of cortisol feedback.
Lineage Marker: Both express TPIT.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the physiological feedback mechanism of Prolactin with that of ACTH.
back:
Prolactin: Primary control is inhibitory via hypothalamic Dopamine.
ACTH: Controlled by negative feedback from circulating adrenal Cortisol.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the two hallmark histologic features that distinguish any pituitary adenoma from the normal anterior pituitary parenchyma.
back:
1. Cellular monomorphism (uniform cell population).
2. Absence of the reticulin network (sparse supporting connective tissue).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary are all derived from a common progenitor cell lineage expressing the transcription factor [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• Essential for the differentiation of GH, PRL, and TSH secreting cells

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 28-year-old female presents with amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and infertility. Histological examination of a pituitary biopsy shows cellular monomorphism and loss of the reticulin network. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Most common hyperfunctioning pituitary adenoma
• Clinically identified by hyperprolactinemia

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the molecular mechanism involving the GNAS gene that leads to unchecked proliferation in approximately 40% of somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Activating mutation in the Gsα subunit
• Abrogates intrinsic GTPase activity
• Leads to constitutive cAMP generation and persistent mitogenic signaling

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the histological and staining features of densely granulated versus sparsely granulated somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Densely: Acidophilic/eosinophilic cytoplasm; strong, diffuse cytoplasmic GH staining
• Sparsely: Chromophobic cells; weak GH staining; characterized by paranuclear "fibrous bodies"

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Define the size-based classification used to distinguish pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas.
back:
• Microadenoma: Less than 1 cm in diameter
• Macroadenoma: Greater than 1 cm in diameter

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Gonadotroph adenomas, which often present as non-functioning macroadenomas, typically express the lineage-specific transcription factors [___] and GATA-2.
back:
• Steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1)
• Expresses β-FSH and β-LH subunits
• Typically presents with mass effects rather than hormonal syndromes

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient develops a large, destructive ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma and hyperpigmentation following bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing syndrome. This clinical entity is known as [___].
back:
• Nelson Syndrome
• Caused by loss of inhibitory feedback from adrenal corticosteroids
• Characterized by mass effects and skin darkening via MSH

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Local Mass Effects of Pituitary Tumors
front: Describe the anatomical mechanism by which a pituitary macroadenoma produces the classic visual field defect of bitemporal hemianopsia.
back:
• Superior expansion through the diaphragma sella
• Direct compression of decussating fibers at the optic chiasm
• Interrupts impulses from the nasal retinas

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
coreConcept: Hormonally Silent vs. Null Cell Adenomas
front: Distinguish between "silent" pituitary adenomas and true null cell adenomas regarding their cellular differentiation markers.
back:
• Silent: Express hormones or transcription factors (e.g., TPIT) by IHC but lack clinical excess symptoms
• Null Cell: Demonstrate no evidence of hormone production or lineage-specific transcription factors

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the specific transcription factor that serves as a diagnostic marker for corticotroph adenomas.
back:
• TPIT (T-box protein 19)
• Required for the differentiation of the POMC/ACTH cell lineage

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Pituitary adenomas are classically designated as macroadenomas if their maximum diameter is greater than [___].
back:
• 1 cm
• Lesions less than 1 cm are termed microadenomas.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with progressive enlargement of the hands and feet, a protruding lower jaw (prognathism), and new-onset hypertension. Identify the most likely underlying pituitary cell lineage tumor.
back:
• Somatotroph adenoma
• Clinical syndrome: Acromegaly
• Mediated by hepatic Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1) secretion.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the role of the transcription factor PIT-1 in the classification of pituitary adenomas.
back:
• Defines the acidophil lineage
• Expressed in Somatotroph, Lactotroph, and Thyrotroph adenomas
• Used for lineage-specific immunohistochemical classification.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient with growth hormone excess shows weak GH staining on biopsy and characteristic juxtanuclear 'fibrous bodies' on microscopy. Contrast this with the classic 'densely granulated' variant.
back:
• Sparsely granulated (this case): Chromophobe cells, cytokeratin fibrous bodies, more aggressive.
• Densely granulated: Eosinophilic cells, strong diffuse GH staining, slower growth.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the primary pharmacological step used to medically shrink a lactotroph adenoma.
back:
• Dopamine receptor agonists (e.g., Bromocriptine or Cabergoline)
• Mechanism: Mimics dopamine-mediated inhibition of prolactin secretion.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The two cardinal histological features used to distinguish a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary parenchyma are cellular monomorphism and the absence of a [___].
back:
• Reticulin network
• Normal pituitary has a distinct reticulin meshwork around cell nests (acini).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea and galactorrhea. MRI reveals a 0.6 cm intrasellar mass. Identify the most likely diagnosis and the specific immunohistochemical markers expected.
back:
• Lactotroph Adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Markers: Prolactin, PIT-1, and Estrogen Receptor alpha (ERα).

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: How does the GNAS mutation specifically drive the development of approximately 40% of somatotroph adenomas?
back:
• Mutation inactivates the intrinsic GTPase activity of Gsα subunit
• Leads to constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase
• Results in persistent high levels of intracellular cAMP and unchecked proliferation.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the metabolic feedback loop response to dexamethasone suppression in Cushing disease (pituitary adenoma) versus Ectopic ACTH syndrome.
back:
• Cushing Disease: ACTH secretion is suppressed only by high-dose dexamethasone.
• Ectopic ACTH: ACTH secretion is completely resistant to both low and high-dose dexamethasone.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Which transcription factors are the high-yield diagnostic markers for the gonadotroph adenoma lineage?
back:
• Steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1)
• GATA-2
• Note: These tumors are typically nonfunctioning (silent).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) is synthesized in the cell bodies of the [___] and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus.
back:
• Supraoptic 
 • Hormones travel via the hypothalamic-hypophyseal tract for storage in the posterior pituitary.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient with small-cell lung carcinoma presents with confusion and serum sodium of 118 mEq/L, while appearing euvolemic. Identify the likely pathophysiology.
back:
• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH) 
 • Ectopic ADH secretion leads to excessive renal water resorption and dilutional hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of the V2 receptor upon ADH binding in the renal collecting ducts.
back:
• Activates cAMP-dependent protein kinase 
 • Triggers insertion of Aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane 
 • Increases free water reabsorption into the interstitium.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the response to a water deprivation test followed by desmopressin in Central versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus (DI).
back:
• Central DI: Significant increase in urine osmolality (>50%) after desmopressin.
 • Nephrogenic DI: Minimal or no increase in urine osmolality (ADH resistance).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Which tetracycline antibiotic acts as an ADH antagonist and is used to treat SIADH?
back:
• Demeclocycline 
 • It induces a state of functional nephrogenic DI by inhibiting ADH-induced cAMP production.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The diagnostic hallmark of Diabetes Insipidus is the excretion of large volumes of dilute urine with a specific gravity typically below [___].
back:
• 1.005 
 • This reflects the kidney's inability to concentrate urine due to ADH deficiency or resistance.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 30-year-old male develops massive polyuria (10L/day) 48 hours after a severe head injury. Specify the likely posterior pituitary complication.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus 
 • Trauma disrupts the hypothalamic-hypophyseal axons, causing an absolute deficiency of ADH release.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain how SIADH leads to neurologic dysfunction without inducing peripheral edema.
back:
• Excessive water causes hyponatremia and cerebral edema (cellular swelling) 
 • Natriuretic peptides (ANP/BNP) are released to excrete sodium/water 
 • This "pressure natriuresis" maintains euvolemia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the urine osmolality and serum sodium levels in SIADH versus Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• SIADH: High urine osmolality (concentrated); Low serum sodium (diluted) 
 • DI: Low urine osmolality (dilute); High serum sodium (concentrated).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the specialized modified glial cells that comprise the bulk of the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).
back:
• Pituicytes 
 • They provide structural and metabolic support to the axon terminals of hypothalamic neurons.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
coreConcept: ADH Site of Synthesis vs Release
front: Central diabetes insipidus is characterized by an absolute deficiency of the hormone [___], which is synthesized in the hypothalamus.
back:
• ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone / Arginine Vasopressin)
• Synthesized in supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
• Stored and released from the posterior pituitary

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 50-year-old smoker with a lung mass presents with confusion, a serum sodium of 118 mEq/L, and low serum osmolality. He is euvolemic without edema. Diagnosis?
back:
• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
• Likely ectopic ADH from small-cell lung carcinoma
• Causes excessive free water resorption

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of V2 receptors in the renal collecting duct upon binding with circulating ADH.
back:
• Activates G-proteins and increases intracellular cAMP
• Triggers translocation of Aquaporin-2 channels to apical membrane
• Facilitates free water reabsorption into the medullary interstitium

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the response to an exogenous vasopressin challenge in Central Diabetes Insipidus (DI) versus Nephrogenic DI.
back:
• Central DI: Rapid, significant rise in urine osmolality (>50%)
• Nephrogenic DI: Minimal or no response in urine osmolality
• Distinguishes hormone deficiency from renal end-organ resistance

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary urinary and serum laboratory findings that define the metabolic state in Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Polyuria (excessive dilute urine)
• Low urine specific gravity (<1.005)
• Hypernatremia and high serum osmolality (>295 mOsm/kg)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the setting of SIADH, the resulting dilutional hyponatremia frequently leads to [___] due to the movement of water into the intracellular compartment of the CNS.
back:
• Cerebral edema
• Presents with headache, nausea, and seizures
• Result of acute osmotic shift into brain cells

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient with chronic lithium use for bipolar disorder presents with polyuria and polydipsia. Desmopressin administration fails to concentrate the urine. Identify the specific disorder.
back:
• Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus
• Induced by lithium-mediated renal tubular unresponsiveness
• Inability of kidneys to respond to circulating ADH

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe why peripheral edema is rarely observed in patients with SIADH despite total body water expansion.
back:
• Total body water increases, but blood volume remains near normal
• Secondary natriuresis occurs (due to ANP release and pressure natriuresis)
• Compensatory sodium loss maintains euvolemic state

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
coreConcept: Etiological Contrast of Posterior Pituitary Disorders
front: Contrast the typical etiology of Central Diabetes Insipidus with the etiology of SIADH.
back:
• Central DI: Head trauma, tumors, or surgery affecting the hypothalamus/stalk
• SIADH: Ectopic secretion (small-cell lung cancer), CNS infections, or certain drugs

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the non-secretory, modified glial cells that support axonal processes in the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Pituicytes
• Provide structural support to hypothalamic-hypophyseal tract axons
• Posterior lobe is primarily a storage/release site, not a synthesis site

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The peptide hormone synthesized in the hypothalamus but stored and secreted by the posterior pituitary to restrict diuresis is [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)
• Also known as Arginine Vasopressin (AVP)
• Targets renal collecting ducts to increase water reabsorption.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 45-year-old male presents with polyuria and intense thirst following a head injury. Labs show high serum sodium and dilute urine. Exogenous ADH administration corrects the urine concentration. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Caused by ADH deficiency due to hypothalamic or pituitary stalk damage
• Characterized by inability to concentrate urine.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of plasma osmolality and blood pressure in the physiological regulation of ADH release.
back:
• High plasma osmotic pressure: Sensed by osmoreceptors, triggering ADH release to conserve water
• Low blood pressure: Sensed by baroreceptors, stimulating ADH to restore volume.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the serum sodium levels and urine specific gravity expected in Diabetes Insipidus versus Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH).
back:
• Diabetes Insipidus: Hypernatremia (high Na+) and low urine specific gravity (<1.005)
• SIADH: Hyponatremia (low Na+) and high urine specific gravity.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the typical volume status and the presence or absence of peripheral edema in a patient with SIADH.
back:
• Euvolemic hyponatremia
• Total body water is increased, but blood volume remains near normal
• Peripheral edema is characteristically absent.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus, the underlying defect is [___] rather than a lack of hormone production.
back:
• Renal tubular unresponsiveness to circulating ADH
• Often caused by drugs (lithium), genetic mutations (AVPR2), or hypercalcemia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 60-year-old heavy smoker presents with confusion, seizures, and a serum sodium of 118 mEq/L. Chest imaging shows a central hilar mass. What is the most likely paraneoplastic mechanism?
back:
• Ectopic secretion of ADH by Small-cell carcinoma of the lung
• Leads to excessive water resorption and dilutional hyponatremia (SIADH)
• Neurological symptoms result from cerebral edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: How does the administration of desmopressin (ADH analog) help distinguish Central from Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus?
back:
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases significantly (>50%) after administration
• Nephrogenic DI: Minimal or no increase in urine osmolality occurs due to end-organ resistance.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the metabolic consequences of ADH deficiency in a bedridden patient versus a patient with an intact thirst mechanism.
back:
• Intact thirst: Polydipsia compensates for polyuria; serum sodium may remain normal
• Bedridden/Obtunded: Rapid development of life-threatening dehydration and severe hypernatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: List three common causes of SIADH involving the Central Nervous System.
back:
• Head trauma
• Brain infections (meningitis/encephalitis)
• Intracranial tumors or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Central diabetes insipidus is characterized by an absolute deficiency of [___] resulting from damage to the hypothalamus or posterior pituitary.
back:
• ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone/Vasopressin)
• Results in inability to resorb free water
• Causes excretion of large volumes of dilute urine

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 68-year-old smoker presents with confusion and serum sodium of 118 mEq/L. Imaging reveals a 4 cm hilar mass. Identify the most likely posterior pituitary syndrome.
back:
• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
• Caused by ectopic ADH secretion from Small Cell Lung Cancer
• Results in severe dilutional hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of the Arginine Vasopressin Receptor 2 (AVPR2) in the pathogenesis of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
back:
• AVPR2 mutations cause renal unresponsiveness to ADH
• Impairs aquaporin-2 channel insertion in collecting ducts
• Prevents water resorption despite high hormone levels

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient with polyuria fails to concentrate urine during water deprivation. Administration of exogenous desmopressin leads to a 75% rise in urine osmolality. Contrast this with the expected result in a nephrogenic etiology.
back:
• Central DI: Significant increase in urine osmolality with desmopressin
• Nephrogenic DI: No or minimal increase in urine osmolality
• Indicates primary ADH lack versus renal resistance

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the volume status and the presence or absence of peripheral edema in a patient with SIADH.
back:
• Euvolemic hyponatremia
• Total body water is increased, but clinical edema is absent
• Natriuresis occurs to compensate for volume expansion

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In both central and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, the hallmark laboratory finding is a urine specific gravity typically below [___].
back:
• 1.005
• Corresponds to low urine osmolality
• Accompanied by increased serum sodium and osmolality

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient presents with a sudden 'thunderclap' headache and visual field defects, followed by massive polyuria. Identify the likely underlying clinical event and the resulting syndrome.
back:
• Pituitary Apoplexy (hemorrhage)
• Resulting in Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Acute loss of ADH release due to infarction

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: How does the hyper-resorption of free water in SIADH lead to neurologic symptoms like seizures and coma?
back:
• Leads to hypotonic dilutional hyponatremia
• Causes fluid shift from extracellular to intracellular space
• Results in cerebral edema and increased intracranial pressure

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the primary anatomic site of synthesis for ADH versus its primary site of renal physiological action.
back:
• Synthesis: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus
• Action: V2 receptors in the medullary collecting ducts of the kidney

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the two specific hypothalamic nuclei where ADH is produced before being stored in the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Supraoptic nucleus
• Paraventricular nucleus
• Hormones travel via axons down the pituitary stalk

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The posterior pituitary hormone primarily responsible for water conservation by increasing renal resorption of free water is [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Arginine Vasopressin (AVP)
• Synthesized in the hypothalamus
• Acts on kidney collecting ducts

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 40-year-old male with a history of head trauma presents with extreme thirst and the excretion of 12L of dilute urine daily. What is the likely underlying condition?
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Pathophysiology: ADH deficiency
• Key findings: Polyuria, low urine specific gravity, and polydipsia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of osmoreceptors in the regulation of ADH release during states of dehydration.
back:
• High plasma osmotic pressure is sensed by osmoreceptors
• Signals are sent to the hypothalamus
• Triggers ADH release from posterior pituitary axon terminals to conserve water

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast Central Diabetes Insipidus with Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus regarding ADH levels and response to exogenous vasopressin.
back:
• Central: Low circulating ADH; responds to exogenous vasopressin (urine concentrates)
• Nephrogenic: Normal/high ADH; no response to vasopressin (kidney resistance)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary metabolic hallmark and the typical fluid volume status observed in Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH).
back:
• Hallmark: Hyponatremia (low serum sodium)
• Volume status: Euvolemic (increased total body water without peripheral edema)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The most common non-pituitary malignancy associated with the ectopic secretion of ADH, leading to SIADH, is [___] carcinoma of the lung.
back:
• Small-cell carcinoma of the lung
• Results in over-resorption of water
• Causes dilutional hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient presents with confusion, seizures, and severe hyponatremia following CNS trauma. Lab results show inappropriately concentrated urine. Diagnosis?
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Pathophysiology: ADH excess causing water retention
• Risk: Cerebral edema due to hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the cellular mechanism of ADH action within the renal collecting duct to facilitate water resorption.
back:
• ADH binds V2 receptors
• Increases intracellular cAMP
• Stimulates insertion of Aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the urinary specific gravity and serum osmolality findings in Diabetes Insipidus versus SIADH.
back:
• DI: Low urine specific gravity; high serum osmolality
• SIADH: Inappropriately high urine specific gravity; low serum osmolality

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the specific hypothalamic nuclei where ADH is synthesized before transport to the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Supraoptic nuclei
• Paraventricular nuclei
• Transported via axons through the pituitary stalk

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Somatotroph, lactotroph, and thyrotroph adenomas are all derived from a common precursor cell expressing the transcription factor [___].
back:
• PIT-1
• This factor is essential for the differentiation of these three acidophilic and chromophobic cell lineages in the anterior pituitary.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 28-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, milky nipple discharge, and infertility. High-resolution MRI reveals a 6mm intrasellar lesion. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Lactotroph adenoma (Prolactinoma)
• Most common functioning pituitary tumor
• Causes hyperprolactinemia, which inhibits GnRH, leading to menstrual dysfunction.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the mechanism by which GNAS mutations lead to autonomous hormone secretion in somatotroph adenomas.
back:
• Activating mutations in the α-subunit of Gs (Gsα) abrogate its intrinsic GTPase activity.
• Results in constitutive activation of adenyl cyclase.
• Persistent cAMP generation drives unchecked somatotroph proliferation and Growth Hormone release.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A patient presents with bitemporal hemianopsia and hypopituitarism; contrast this with the typical clinical presentation of a 5mm lactotroph microadenoma.
back:
• Macroadenomas (>1cm): Present with mass effects, including visual field defects (optic chiasm compression) and headache.
• Microadenomas (<1cm): Present primarily with endocrine disturbances like galactorrhea, without neurological deficits.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Describe the pharmacological utility of somatostatin analogues in the management of Growth Hormone-secreting tumors.
back:
• Somatostatin normally inhibits pituitary GH secretion.
• Synthetic analogues bind to somatostatin receptors on the adenoma, effectively inhibiting GH release and often reducing tumor volume.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: The lineage-specific transcription factor required for the differentiation of corticotroph-lineage adenomas (ACTH-secreting) is [___].
back:
• TPIT (T-box protein 19)
• It is used immunohistochemically to identify corticotroph adenomas, including those that are clinically silent.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: A 45-year-old male presents with coarse facial features, increased glove size, and prognathism. Failure to suppress Growth Hormone levels during an oral glucose load confirms the diagnosis of [___].
back:
• Somatotroph adenoma (Acromegaly)
• GH stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production, causing tissue and bone overgrowth after epiphyseal closure.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Explain the physiological mechanism behind the development of Nelson syndrome following surgical adrenalectomy.
back:
• Removal of adrenals eliminates cortisol-mediated negative feedback on the pituitary.
• This triggers the rapid expansion of a pre-existing ACTH-secreting microadenoma.
• Results in hyperpigmentation and severe mass effects.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Contrast the biochemical profile of hyperthyroidism caused by Graves disease with that caused by a thyrotroph adenoma.
back:
• Graves Disease: Elevated T3/T4 with suppressed (low) TSH.
• Thyrotroph Adenoma: Elevated T3/T4 with inappropriately normal or elevated TSH levels.

category: Classification of pituitary adenomas
front: Identify the specific histological hallmark that distinguishes a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary parenchyma.
back:
• Cellular monomorphism (single cell type) and the absence of a reticulin network.
• Normal gland shows a mixture of cell types supported by a delicate reticulin framework.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the pathogenesis of Central Diabetes Insipidus, the primary hormonal defect involves a deficiency of [___], resulting in an inability of the kidneys to concentrate urine.
back:
• ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) or Vasopressin
• Synthesis occurs in the hypothalamus
• Storage and release happen in the posterior pituitary
• Deficiency causes massive excretion of dilute urine

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 60-year-old smoker presents with confusion and serum sodium of 118 mEq/L. Chest X-ray reveals a hilar mass. Identify the most likely posterior pituitary syndrome.
back:
• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
• Caused by ectopic ADH production from small-cell lung carcinoma
• Leads to excessive water resorption
• Results in severe dilutional hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of the V2 receptor and Aquaporin-2 channels in response to ADH secretion.
back:
• ADH binds V2 receptors on renal collecting duct cells
• Triggers cAMP-mediated insertion of Aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane
• Facilitates free water reabsorption into the systemic circulation

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the diagnostic outcomes of a Water Deprivation Test followed by Desmopressin administration in Central versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases significantly (>50%) after Desmopressin
• Nephrogenic DI: No response to Desmopressin; urine remains dilute
• Differentiates primary hormone deficiency from end-organ resistance

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the specific nuclei in the hypothalamus where ADH and Oxytocin are synthesized before transport to the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Supraoptic nuclei (primarily ADH)
• Paraventricular nuclei (primarily Oxytocin)
• Transported via axons through the pituitary stalk
• Stored in terminal nerve endings within the neurohypophysis

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the laboratory diagnosis of Diabetes Insipidus, the urine specific gravity is characteristically [___] despite rising serum osmolality.
back:
• Low (usually < 1.005)
• Reflects failure to concentrate urine
• Serum sodium and osmolality typically rise simultaneously
• Accompanied by polyuria (>3L/day)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient with a recent head injury develops extreme thirst and voids 10 liters of dilute urine daily. If this is Central Diabetes Insipidus, describe the serum sodium status.
back:
• Hypernatremia (High serum sodium)
• Excessive free water loss in urine concentrates serum
• Leads to compensatory polydipsia (excessive thirst)
• Stimulates osmoreceptors to trigger ADH release if pathway is intact

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the mechanism of 'euvolemic hyponatremia' in SIADH and why peripheral edema is usually absent.
back:
• Excess water expands extracellular fluid volume
• Triggers Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) release
• Causes secondary natriuresis (sodium excretion in urine)
• Maintains near-normal volume but worsens hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the serum and urine osmolality findings typical of SIADH.
back:
• Serum Osmolality: Decreased (Low due to dilutional hyponatremia)
• Urine Osmolality: Inappropriately high (Concentrated urine)
• Urine sodium is usually elevated (>20 mmol/L) due to natriuresis

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the two primary physiologic stimuli that signal the hypothalamus to increase the release of ADH.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (sensed by osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood pressure/volume (sensed by baroreceptors)
• Stress, pain, and certain drugs can also trigger release

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
coreConcept: Site of ADH and Oxytocin Synthesis
front: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and oxytocin are synthesized in the [___] before being transported to the posterior pituitary for storage and release.
back:
• Hypothalamus (specifically the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei).
• Transported via axons in the pituitary stalk.
• Released directly into systemic circulation upon physiological stimulus.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 60-year-old heavy smoker presents with confusion and seizures. Labs reveal serum sodium of 115 mEq/L and high urine osmolality despite low serum osmolality. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH).
• Likely paraneoplastic (Small-cell carcinoma of the lung).
• Characterized by euvolemic hyponatremia and cerebral edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of ADH in the renal collecting ducts and the effect of its deficiency in Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• ADH normally promotes water reabsorption.
• Deficiency prevents water conservation in the collecting ducts.
• Results in polyuria (excessive urination) and compensatory polydipsia (thirst).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast Central Diabetes Insipidus with Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus regarding ADH levels and response to exogenous vasopressin administration.
back:
• Central: Decreased ADH levels; urine concentrates with vasopressin.
• Nephrogenic: Normal/high ADH levels; renal tubules fail to respond to vasopressin.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary metabolic complication that limits the survival of bedridden or obtunded patients with Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Severe, life-threatening dehydration.
• Occurs because patients cannot voluntarily compensate for free water loss through polydipsia.
• Leads to hypernatremia and vascular collapse.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In patients with Diabetes Insipidus, the hallmark of the condition is the excretion of large volumes of urine with a characteristically [___] specific gravity.
back:
• Low (dilute urine).
• Indicates the kidney's inability to concentrate urine due to absent or ineffective ADH.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient suffers a traumatic head injury and subsequently develops massive polyuria and a serum sodium of 155 mEq/L. Which posterior pituitary syndrome is most likely?
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus.
• Caused by trauma to the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, or posterior pituitary.
• Results in absolute ADH deficiency.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which SIADH leads to neurologic dysfunction without peripheral edema.
back:
• Excessive water resorption increases total body water.
• Dilutional hyponatremia causes osmotic movement of water into brain cells.
• Results in cerebral edema; euvolemic status prevents peripheral edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the serum sodium levels and serum osmolality typically seen in Diabetes Insipidus versus SIADH.
back:
• Diabetes Insipidus: Hypernatremia and high serum osmolality (water loss).
• SIADH: Hyponatremia and low serum osmolality (water retention).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Which specific modified glial cells comprise the bulk of the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis)?
back:
• Pituicytes.
• These cells support the axonal processes extending from the hypothalamus via the pituitary stalk.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The posterior pituitary hormones, oxytocin and ADH, are actually synthesized in the [___].
back:
• Hypothalamus
• Transported via axons through the pituitary stalk
• Stored in axon terminals within the neurohypophysis

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 55-year-old male with small-cell lung carcinoma presents with confusion and seizures. Labs show severe hyponatremia and inappropriately concentrated urine. Identify the likely syndrome.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Ectopic ADH secretion by the tumor
• Causes excessive resorption of free water and hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of ADH (antidiuretic hormone) in the kidneys during periods of dehydration.
back:
• Increases water resorption in renal tubules
• Restricts diuresis to conserve free water
• Stimulated by increased plasma osmolality and decreased blood pressure

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the underlying pathophysiology and ADH response in Central versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Central: ADH deficiency (trauma/tumors); responds to exogenous ADH
• Nephrogenic: Renal resistance to ADH (genetic/drugs); no response to exogenous ADH
• Both: Massive polyuria and low urine specific gravity

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the two primary stimuli that trigger the release of ADH from the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (detected by osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood pressure (detected by baroreceptors in atria and carotids)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the presence of SIADH, total body water is increased; however, [___] does not develop because blood volume remains near normal.
back:
• Peripheral edema
• Distinguishes SIADH from other hyponatremic states like heart failure
• Sodium loss in urine maintains near-normal volume

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient presents with massive polyuria (8L/day) and hypernatremia following a head injury. The urine is very dilute. Which posterior pituitary disorder is most likely?
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Result of traumatic injury to hypothalamus or pituitary stalk
• Inability to concentrate urine due to ADH lack

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the mechanism by which SIADH causes neurological symptoms like confusion and coma.
back:
• Excessive water resorption causes severe hyponatremia
• Osmotic shift of water into brain cells leads to cerebral edema
• High intracranial pressure results in neurological dysfunction

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the clinical consequences of Oxytocin deficiency versus ADH deficiency.
back:
• Oxytocin deficiency: Failure of postpartum milk ejection and lactation
• ADH deficiency: Diabetes Insipidus (polyuria, polydipsia, dehydration)
• ADH deficiency is life-threatening in obtunded patients

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: List the three components of the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary gland).
back:
• Modified glial cells (pituicytes)
• Axonal processes (from hypothalamus)
• Axon terminals (storing ADH and oxytocin)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Central diabetes insipidus results from a deficiency of the hormone [___], which is normally stored in the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Arginine Vasopressin (AVP)
• Synthesized in the hypothalamic paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei
• Stored in and released from the neurohypophysis in response to plasma osmolarity.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 55-year-old heavy smoker presents with confusion and a serum sodium of 115 mEq/L. Imaging reveals a hilar lung mass. Identify the most likely endocrine syndrome.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Pathophysiology: Paraneoplastic secretion of ectopic ADH
• Most common cause: Small-cell carcinoma of the lung.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain how the Water Deprivation Test distinguishes Central Diabetes Insipidus (DI) from Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Desmopressin (ADH analog) is administered
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases significantly (responds to exogenous ADH)
• Nephrogenic DI: Urine osmolality remains low (kidney resistance to ADH).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the volume status and physical findings of a patient with SIADH versus a patient with congestive heart failure (both presenting with hyponatremia).
back:
• SIADH: Euvolemic hyponatremia; increased total body water but normal blood volume; no peripheral edema.
• CHF: Hypervolemic hyponatremia; increased total body water and sodium; clinical edema and ascites present.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary initial management step for a patient diagnosed with SIADH who is asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic.
back:
• Fluid restriction
• Removal of the underlying cause (e.g., drug cessation)
• Induces negative water balance to gradually correct serum sodium concentration.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the diagnosis of SIADH, a key laboratory finding is a urine osmolality that is [___] relative to serum osmolality.
back:
• Inappropriately concentrated (High)
• Urine osmolality > Serum osmolality
• Reflects excessive renal water reabsorption despite low serum osmolality.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient develops polyuria (dilute urine) and polydipsia following a severe head injury. Serum sodium is 155 mEq/L. Name the condition and its specific anatomical origin.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Anatomical origin: Hypothalamic damage (supraoptic/paraventricular nuclei) or pituitary stalk disruption
• Results in absolute ADH deficiency.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe why patients with SIADH remain clinically 'euvolemic' despite significant water retention from excessive ADH.
back:
• Secondary natriuresis
• Volume expansion triggers Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) release
• Inhibits Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS)
• Sodium excretion prevents fluid overload and clinical edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the renal collecting duct pathology in SIADH versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus regarding Aquaporin-2 channels.
back:
• SIADH: Excessive ADH causes constitutive insertion of Aquaporin-2; maximal water reabsorption.
• Nephrogenic DI: Failure of Aquaporin-2 channel insertion despite high ADH; inability to concentrate urine.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: List the two primary stimuli that trigger the release of preformed ADH from the posterior pituitary into the circulation.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (detected by osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood pressure/hypovolemia (detected by baroreceptors)
• Aims to conserve free water and restore volume.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Central diabetes insipidus is characterized by a deficiency of [___] due to damage to the hypothalamus or pituitary gland.
back:
• ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) or Arginine Vasopressin (AVP)
• Results in excessive urination (polyuria)
• Leads to inability to concentrate urine
• Compensatory polydipsia (intense thirst) occurs

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 65-year-old smoker with a lung mass presents with seizures and a serum sodium of 115 mEq/L. Identify the syndrome and the likely cellular origin of the mass.
back:
• Syndrome: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
• Origin: Small-cell carcinoma of the lung
• Mechanism: Ectopic ADH secretion causing water reabsorption
• Result: Severe dilutional hyponatremia and cerebral edema

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of V2 receptors and Aquaporin-2 in the action of ADH on the kidney.
back:
• ADH binds to V2 receptors on basolateral membranes of collecting ducts
• Increases intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP)
• Triggers apical insertion of Aquaporin-2 water channels
• Facilitates free water reabsorption into the medullary interstitium

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast Central and Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus regarding ADH levels and response to exogenous desmopressin.
back:
• Central DI: Low ADH levels; urine osmolality increases >50% after desmopressin
• Nephrogenic DI: Normal/High ADH levels; minimal or no change in urine osmolality after desmopressin
• Primary defect: Synthesis/secretion (Central) vs. Renal resistance (Nephrogenic)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Justify why peripheral edema is not a standard finding in SIADH despite significant water retention.
back:
• Hypervolemia triggers release of atrial natriuretic peptides
• Promotes secondary natriuresis (sodium excretion)
• Leads to "euvolemic hyponatremia"
• Prevents interstitial fluid accumulation and visible edema

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: X-linked Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus most frequently results from a loss-of-function mutation in the [___] gene.
back:
• AVPR2 (Arginine Vasopressin Receptor 2)
• Causes renal tubular unresponsiveness to ADH
• Presents with large volumes of dilute urine
• Leads to hypernatremic dehydration if water intake is restricted
