category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient develops sudden polyuria following a basal skull fracture. Describe the expected findings in serum osmolality and urine specific gravity.
back:
• Serum Osmolality: Elevated (Hypertonic dehydration)
• Urine Specific Gravity: Low (typically <1.005)
• Result of Central Diabetes Insipidus
• High serum sodium due to excessive free water loss

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the neurologic risk associated with overly rapid correction of hyponatremia in a patient with SIADH.
back:
• Central Pontine Myelinolysis (Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome)
• Caused by sudden osmotic shift of water out of brain cells
• Leads to permanent neurologic damage or quadriparesis
• Sodium should be corrected slowly and cautiously

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
coreConcept: Volume Status in Posterior Pituitary Syndromes
front: Contrast the effects of SIADH and Diabetes Insipidus on total body water and plasma volume.
back:
• SIADH: Increased total body water; plasma volume near normal (euvolemic expansion)
• Diabetes Insipidus: Decreased total body water; plasma volume decreased (hypovolemic contraction)
• SIADH causes cellular swelling; DI causes cellular dehydration

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Enumerate three non-traumatic causes of Central Diabetes Insipidus related to the hypothalamus.
back:
• Tumors (e.g., Craniopharyngioma)
• Inflammatory/Granulomatous diseases (e.g., Sarcoidosis, Tuberculosis)
• Genetic mutations (e.g., autosomal dominant AVP gene mutations)
• Pituitary surgery (Hypophysectomy)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is synthesized primarily in the [___] of the hypothalamus before storage in the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
• Transported via axons through the pituitary stalk
• Released into systemic circulation in response to increased plasma osmolality

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 68-year-old heavy smoker presents with a lung mass, serum sodium of 118 mEq/L, and low serum osmolality. Identify the posterior pituitary syndrome and likely cause.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Likely ectopic ADH secretion from Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma
• Results in excessive water reabsorption and dilutional hyponatremia

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of V2 receptors and Aquaporin-2 channels upon ADH binding in the renal collecting ducts.
back:
• ADH binds basolateral V2 receptors (GPCRs)
• Triggers cAMP-mediated signaling
• Stimulates insertion of Aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane for water resorption

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast Central Diabetes Insipidus with Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus regarding ADH levels and the Water Deprivation Test response.
back:
• Central: Low ADH; urine osmolality increases (concentrates) with exogenous desmopressin
• Nephrogenic: Normal/High ADH; urine remains dilute despite desmopressin administration

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary clinical manifestation of SIADH on the Central Nervous System and the physiological reason for the absence of peripheral edema.
back:
• Cerebral edema and neurological dysfunction due to hyponatremia
• Absence of edema due to secondary natriuresis (euvolemic hyponatremia)
• Triggered by ANP increase and aldosterone suppression

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The hallmark laboratory finding in Diabetes Insipidus is a urine specific gravity typically [___].
back:
• Less than 1.005
• Indicates the excretion of large volumes of dilute urine
• Reflects an inability to resorb free water

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Following a severe head injury, a patient develops massive polyuria and extreme thirst. Serum sodium is 158 mEq/L. Identify the diagnosis and the likely site of injury.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Damage to the hypothalamus or the pituitary stalk
• Results in total ADH deficiency and life-threatening dehydration

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the mechanism of 'pseudohyponatremia' exclusion in suspected SIADH via serum osmolality.
back:
• SIADH must demonstrate true hypoosmolar hyponatremia
• High glucose or lipids can lower sodium while osmolality remains normal/high
• SIADH diagnosis requires low serum osmolality (<275 mOsm/kg)

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the effects of SIADH and Diabetes Insipidus on serum osmolality and volume status.
back:
• SIADH: Low serum osmolality; euvolemic/slight fluid expansion
• DI: High serum osmolality; hypovolemia/dehydration if fluid intake is inadequate

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the modified glial cells that constitute the bulk of the neurohypophysis and support hypothalamic axons.
back:
• Pituicytes
• Function as specialized glial support for axon terminals
• Do not synthesize hormones themselves

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Central diabetes insipidus is primarily characterized by a deficiency of the hormone [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Arginine Vasopressin (AVP).
• Produced in the hypothalamus and stored in the posterior pituitary.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 40-year-old male with a history of head trauma presents with massive polyuria (8L/day) and serum sodium of 152 mEq/L. Urine specific gravity is 1.002. Diagnosis?
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus.
• Caused by traumatic injury to the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk, leading to ADH deficiency.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the diagnostic significance of the desmopressin (ADH analog) response in polyuric patients.
back:
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases (>50%) as kidneys respond to exogenous ADH.
• Nephrogenic DI: No significant change due to distal tubule resistance.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
coreConcept: Differential Contrast of Posterior Pituitary Disorders
front: Contrast the urine specific gravity and serum sodium levels found in SIADH versus Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• SIADH: Low serum sodium (hyponatremia) and high urine specific gravity (concentrated).
• Diabetes Insipidus: High serum sodium (hypernatremia) and low urine specific gravity (dilute).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the specific class of pharmacological agents used to treat hyponatremia in SIADH by blocking ADH receptors.
back:
• Vaptans (e.g., Tolvaptan, Conivaptan).
• These act as V2 receptor antagonists in the renal collecting ducts.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The syndrome characterized by excessive water resorption, hyponatremia, and cerebral edema without peripheral edema is [___].
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH).
• Often presents with neurologic symptoms due to hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 65-year-old smoker presents with confusion. Labs show Serum Na+ 115 mEq/L and high urine osmolality. A chest X-ray reveals a central lung mass. What is the likely mechanism?
back:
• Ectopic ADH secretion.
• Most commonly associated with Small Cell Carcinoma of the Lung.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe why SIADH is considered a 'euvolemic' hyponatremia despite excessive water reabsorption.
back:
• Excess water expands total body water, stimulating natriuretic peptides.
• This leads to urinary sodium excretion (natriuresis).
• This prevents significant volume expansion and clinical edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the site of pathology in Central vs. Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Central DI: Hypothalamic/Pituitary failure to produce or release ADH.
• Nephrogenic DI: Renal tubular unresponsiveness to circulating ADH (V2 receptor/Aquaporin defects).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Which specific hypothalamic nuclei are responsible for synthesizing the ADH eventually stored in the posterior pituitary?
back:
• Supraoptic nuclei.
• Paraventricular nuclei.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The primary function of ADH in the kidney is to promote water resorption by inserting [___] channels into the collecting duct.
back:
• Aquaporin-2 channels
• Inserted into the apical membrane of tubular cells
• Increases water permeability
• Results in concentrated urine.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 45-year-old male with small cell carcinoma of the lung presents with confusion and a serum sodium of 115 mEq/L. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Caused by ectopic ADH secretion from the tumor
• Results in excessive water resorption
• Leads to severe dilutional hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the physiological triggers that stimulate the release of ADH from the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (detected by osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood pressure/volume (detected by baroreceptors)
• Angiotensin II stimulation
• Severe physical stress or trauma.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the results of a water deprivation test followed by ADH administration in Central vs. Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases significantly after exogenous ADH.
• Nephrogenic DI: Urine osmolality remains low/unchanged despite ADH administration.
• Central DI implies production failure; Nephrogenic implies renal resistance.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: List the hallmark laboratory findings in a patient with Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Polyuria (massive dilute urine excretion)
• Low urine specific gravity (<1.005)
• Hypernatremia
• Elevated serum osmolality.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the context of posterior pituitary dysfunction, ADH deficiency results in a clinical condition known as [___].
back:
• Diabetes Insipidus
• Can be Central (production defect) or Nephrogenic (receptor defect)
• Leads to inability to resorb water
• Characterized by extreme thirst (polydipsia).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient presents with massive polyuria and a serum sodium of 158 mEq/L following a severe head injury. Explain the likely underlying pathology.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Trauma to the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk
• Absolute deficiency of ADH secretion
• Failure of renal water conservation.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain why peripheral edema is characteristically absent in SIADH despite significant water retention.
back:
• Euvolemic hyponatremia occurs
• Transient hypervolemia triggers Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP)
• ANP increases urinary sodium loss (natriuresis)
• Prevents overt interstitial fluid accumulation.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the primary anatomical sites of synthesis and storage for posterior pituitary hormones.
back:
• Synthesis: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus.
• Storage: Axon terminals in the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).
• Release: Triggered by nerve impulses from the hypothalamus.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary clinical manifestations of oxytocin release during the postnatal period.
back:
• Milk let-down reflex (contraction of myoepithelial cells in breast)
• Uterine smooth muscle contraction (facilitates involution)
• Triggered by nipple stimulation or cervical dilation.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the posterior pituitary system, the peptide hormone primarily responsible for water conservation and restricting diuresis is [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Arginine Vasopressin (AVP)
• Synthesized in the hypothalamic supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
• Transported via axons to the neurohypophysis for storage and release.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 55-year-old smoker with a lung mass presents with lethargy and a serum sodium of 118 mEq/L. Urine osmolality is inappropriately high. Identify the syndrome.
back:
• Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
• Likely caused by ectopic ADH secretion from Small Cell Lung Carcinoma
• Results in excessive water resorption and dilutional hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which ADH restores blood pressure in response to hypovolemia.
back:
• Baroreceptors sense decreased blood pressure
• Triggers ADH release to increase water resorption in renal collecting ducts
• Increases extracellular fluid volume and cardiac output.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the diagnostic response to a Desmopressin (Vasopressin) challenge in Central versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus.
back:
• Central DI: Significant increase in urine osmolality (>50%) as the ADH deficiency is replaced.
• Nephrogenic DI: Minimal or no increase in urine osmolality due to end-organ resistance at the V2 receptor.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Identify the primary clinical danger of severe SIADH and the mechanism behind it.
back:
• Cerebral edema and neurologic dysfunction
• Mechanism: Hyponatremia creates an osmotic gradient
• Water shifts into brain cells, causing swelling, seizures, or coma.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Diabetes Insipidus is characterized by the excretion of large volumes of [___] urine.
back:
• Dilute (low specific gravity)
• Serum sodium and osmolality are typically increased
• Characterized by polyuria and polydipsia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient develops sudden polyuria and intense thirst 24 hours after neurosurgery for a pituitary adenoma. What is the likely complication?
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Cause: Surgical trauma to the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk
• Results in an absolute deficiency of ADH.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain why peripheral edema is characteristically absent in patients with SIADH despite total body water increase.
back:
• SIADH presents as 'euvolemic hyponatremia'
• Increased ADH causes water retention and volume expansion
• This triggers natriuresis (sodium excretion) to normalize blood volume, preventing edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the serum sodium levels found in Diabetes Insipidus versus those found in SIADH.
back:
• Diabetes Insipidus: Hypernatremia (high sodium) due to excessive loss of free water.
• SIADH: Hyponatremia (low sodium) due to excessive resorption of free water.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: List the two primary triggers that stimulate the hypothalamus to release ADH.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (detected by osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood pressure (detected by baroreceptors in cardiac atria and carotids).

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: The posterior pituitary hormone primarily responsible for water conservation, which is synthesized in the hypothalamus and stored in the neurohypophysis, is [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Vasopressin.
• Synthesized in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
• Transported via axons to the posterior pituitary for release.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A 30-year-old male presents with massive polyuria and extreme thirst after a head injury. Lab results show a very low urine specific gravity and hypernatremia. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Central Diabetes Insipidus (DI).
• Caused by ADH deficiency due to hypothalamic or pituitary stalk damage.
• Leads to inability to resorb water from the collecting ducts.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain the role of V2 receptors in the renal collecting ducts when activated by circulating ADH.
back:
• Stimulates cAMP-mediated signaling pathways.
• Triggers translocation of Aquaporin-2 channels to the apical membrane.
• Increases free water reabsorption into the medullary interstitium.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Contrast the response of Central versus Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus during a Desmopressin (DDAVP) challenge test.
back:
• Central DI: Urine osmolality increases (responds to exogenous ADH).
• Nephrogenic DI: Urine osmolality remains low (renal resistance to ADH).
• Used to localize the defect to the brain or kidney.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Which specific malignant neoplasm is most frequently associated with the ectopic secretion of ADH leading to SIADH?
back:
• Small-cell carcinoma of the lung.
• Represents a common paraneoplastic syndrome.
• Leads to autonomous hormone release regardless of plasma osmolality.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: In the Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH) secretion, the clinical state regarding blood volume and sodium concentration is defined as [___] hyponatremia.
back:
• Euvolemic Hyponatremia.
• Total body water increases but blood volume remains near normal.
• Peripheral edema is characteristically absent.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: A patient presents with confusion and seizures. Labs reveal a serum sodium of 115 mEq/L and a high urine osmolality despite high fluid intake. What is the underlying pathophysiology?
back:
• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH).
• Excess ADH causes over-resorption of free water.
• Results in dilutional hyponatremia and cerebral edema.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Explain why peripheral edema is absent in SIADH despite significant renal water retention.
back:
• Secondary activation of natriuretic peptides (ANP).
• Inhibition of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
• Causes "pressure natriuresis," which maintains a stable blood volume.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Distinguish between the urine osmolality findings in Diabetes Insipidus and SIADH.
back:
• Diabetes Insipidus: Low urine osmolality (dilute urine).
• SIADH: High urine osmolality (concentrated urine) relative to serum osmolality.
• Helps differentiate causes of polyuria versus hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate and describe posterior pituitary syndromes (inappropriate ADH (Anti Diuretic Hormone) secretion, diabetes insipidus)
front: Name the two primary physiological triggers that stimulate the release of preformed ADH from the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Increased plasma osmotic pressure (detected by osmoreceptors).
• Decreased blood pressure or hypovolemia (detected by baroreceptors).
• Acts to maintain fluid and electrolyte homeostasis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the follicular epithelial cells often undergo a metaplastic change into cells characterized by abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm, which are termed [___].
back: * H'u'rthle cells (oxyphil cells). * Represent a metaplastic response to chronic cellular injury. * Contain numerous mitochondria. * Characteristic histologic feature of autoimmune thyroid destruction.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with severe neck pain and a tender thyroid gland following a recent viral upper respiratory infection. Laboratory tests show transient hyperthyroidism with low radioactive iodine uptake. The likely diagnosis is [___].
back: * Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis. * Triggered by viral agents like mumps or coxsackievirus. * Characterized by multinucleate giant cells and disrupted follicles. * Typically self-limiting within 6-8 weeks.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the three primary immunological mechanisms responsible for the progressive depletion of thyroid epithelial cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell–mediated killing of thyrocytes. * Cytokine-mediated cell death via Th1-activated macrophages (IFN-gamma). * Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) involving anti-thyroid antibodies. * Resulting parenchyma replacement by mononuclear infiltrates and fibrosis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the microscopic features of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those found in subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis.
back: * Hashimoto: Features significant H'u'rthle cell metaplasia and increased interstitial fibrosis. * Subacute Lymphocytic: Lacks prominent H'u'rthle cell changes and fibrosis. * Both: Involve lymphocytic infiltration and well-developed germinal centers.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Summarize the clinical and pathological hallmarks of Riedel thyroiditis that distinguish it from other inflammatory thyroid conditions.
back: * Clinically presents as a hard, fixed thyroid mass mimicking malignancy. * Histologically characterized by extensive fibrosis extending beyond the gland capsule. * Part of the systemic IgG4-related disease spectrum. * Associated with idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A form of autoimmune thyroiditis occurring within one year of delivery, characterized by painless gland enlargement and initial thyrotoxicosis followed by possible hypothyroidism, is known as [___] thyroiditis.
back: * Postpartum thyroiditis. * A clinical subtype of subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis. * Presents with transient hyperthyroidism due to hormone leakage. * Up to one-third of cases progress to permanent hypothyroidism.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 50-year-old female with a diffuse, painless goiter presents with clinical signs of thyrotoxicosis. Scintigraphy shows low iodine uptake, and the condition later transitions to permanent hypothyroidism. This initial hyperthyroid phase is known as [___].
back: * Hashitoxicosis. * Caused by initial inflammatory disruption of follicles and hormone spillover. * Common early presentation of Hashimoto thyroiditis. * Laboratory findings include elevated free T4 and diminished TSH.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Detail the role of specific non-thyroidal genetic polymorphisms (such as CTLA4 and PTPN22) in the development of autoimmune thyroiditis.
back: * CTLA4: Polymorphisms reduce the inhibition of T-cell responses. * PTPN22: Variants affect lymphoid phosphatase signaling, promoting tolerance breakdown. * These genes are shared susceptibility loci for T1D and Graves disease.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings during the thyrotoxic phase of granulomatous thyroiditis versus Graves disease.
back: * Granulomatous Thyroiditis: Decreased uptake because follicles are damaged and cannot trap iodine. * Graves Disease: Diffusely increased uptake due to TSH-receptor stimulation by TSI. * Distinction is vital for differential diagnosis of hyperthyroidism.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary malignancy risk that requires long-term clinical monitoring in patients with chronic Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. * Arises within the chronic lymphocytic infiltrates of the thyroid gland. * Clinically suspected if a stable goiter suddenly increases in size rapidly.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The metaplastic response of thyroid follicular epithelium to chronic injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis, characterized by cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm, is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (oxyphil cells)
  • Represent a compensatory response to chronic follicular damage
  • Feature small, regular nuclei despite striking cytoplasmic expansion

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless goiter and gradual weight gain. Histology shows mononuclear inflammatory infiltrates with germinal centers and atrophic follicles. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis
  • The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas
  • Characterized by autoimmune destruction of follicles
  • Progressive thyroid failure occurs over time

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells in the tissue destruction of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Recognize thyroid autoantigens on follicular cells
  • Induce direct cell death via cytotoxic granules
  • Contributes significantly to the progressive depletion of thyroid parenchyma
  • Works alongside cytokine-mediated macrophage activation

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the microscopic features of follicle destruction in Granulomatous thyroiditis with those found in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Granulomatous: Multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid pools; neutrophils in early phases
  • Hashimoto: Prominent lymphocytic infiltrates with germinal centers; Hürthle cell metaplasia
  • Granulomatous lacks the organized lymphoid follicles seen in Hashimoto

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the suspected inciting event and clinical hallmark of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Inciting event: Viral infection (e.g., mumps, measles, adenovirus)
  • Clinical hallmark: Severe thyroid pain (most common cause)
  • Typically follows a seasonal pattern peaking in summer

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Riedel thyroiditis is characterized by extensive thyroid fibrosis and is considered a manifestation of [___].
back:
• IgG4-related disease
  • Features hard, fixed thyroid masses simulating carcinoma
  • Fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures
  • Associated with systemic fibrosis in other organs

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old woman presents with a painful neck and hyperthyroid symptoms following a respiratory illness. Radioactive iodine uptake is low. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
  • Pain distinguishes it from other common forms of thyroiditis
  • Low iodine uptake occurs despite high circulating T3/T4
  • Usually self-limiting within 2 to 6 weeks

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Detail the mechanism responsible for 'hashitoxicosis' seen during the early phases of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Follicular rupture causes sudden release of preformed thyroid hormones
  • Produces transient elevations in free T4 and T3
  • Decreases serum TSH levels
  • Eventually transitions to permanent hypothyroidism as follicles are depleted

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Distinguish Subacute Lymphocytic thyroiditis from Granulomatous thyroiditis based on clinical symptoms and microscopic findings.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Painless; often postpartum; purely lymphocytic infiltrates
  • Granulomatous: Painful; giant cell granulomas with colloid pools
  • Subacute Lymphocytic lacks the Hürthle cell change seen in Hashimoto

category: Define thyroiditis
front: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in areas where dietary iodine levels are sufficient?
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis
  • Female predominance (10:1 to 20:1)
  • Caused by a breakdown in self-tolerance to autoantigens
  • Leads to gradual, progressive thyroid failure

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The characteristic histologic hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis is an extensive mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate containing small lymphocytes and plasma cells with well-developed [___].
back:
• Germinal centers.
• These represent a breakdown in self-tolerance to thyroid autoantigens.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painful neck mass and transient hyperthyroidism following a recent viral upper respiratory infection. Microscopy shows multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid. Diagnosis?
back:
• Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis.
• It is the most common cause of thyroid pain.
• Typically follows a viral trigger.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of Hürthle cells as a morphologic marker in the context of thyroiditis.
back:
• Metaplastic response of follicular epithelium.
• Cells acquire abundant, granular eosinophilic cytoplasm.
• Occurs in response to chronic injury, specifically in Hashimoto thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the anatomical extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is confined within the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Extensive fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures, mimicking carcinoma.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the typical clinical course of subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis.
back:
• Initial mild, transient hyperthyroidism.
• Progression to euthyroidism or permanent hypothyroidism (in one-third of cases).
• Frequently occurs in the postpartum period.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In the autoimmune destruction seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis, the cytokine [___] is released by activated Th1 cells to recruit and activate macrophages.
back:
• Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ).
• This mediates cytokine-induced cell death and follicle damage.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A patient presents with a rapidly enlarging, stony-hard neck mass that is fixed to surrounding tissues. If this is a form of thyroiditis, which systemic condition is most likely associated?
back:
• IgG4-related disease.
• The diagnosis is Riedel thyroiditis.
• Characterized by dense fibrous tissue and plasma cell infiltration.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Describe the specific T-cell mechanism responsible for the depletion of thyroid epithelial cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell-mediated killing.
• Direct destruction of thyroid follicular cells following a breakdown in self-tolerance.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Distinguish between Granulomatous thyroiditis and Hashimoto thyroiditis based on radioactive iodine uptake during the hyperthyroid phase.
back:
• Both conditions show decreased radioactive iodine uptake.
• This distinguishes them from Graves disease, which shows diffusely increased uptake.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Which specific autoantibodies are detected in the vast majority of patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis?
back:
• Antithyroglobulin antibodies.
• Antithyroid peroxidase (microsomal) antibodies.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The characteristic metaplastic response of thyroid follicular epithelium to chronic injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis, featuring abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (also known as oxyphil cells)
• Represent follicular cells with high mitochondrial density
• Hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless goiter, fatigue, and cold intolerance. Serum labs reveal elevated TSH and anti-thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies. Identify the most likely diagnosis and its primary histological hallmark.
back:
• Diagnosis: Hashimoto Thyroiditis
• Histology: Extensive mononuclear infiltrate (lymphocytes and plasma cells) with well-developed germinal centers and atrophic follicles.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the major immunologic mechanisms through which thyrocyte injury occurs during the pathogenesis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell mediated cell death
• Cytokine-mediated injury (Th1 cells releasing IFN-γ)
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) involving anti-thyroglobulin or anti-TPO antibodies.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the clinical presentation and microscopic appearance of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis with those of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Granulomatous: Painful thyroid, triggered by viral infection, histology shows multinucleate giant cells/granulomas.
• Hashimoto: Painless, autoimmune origin, histology shows lymphocytic infiltrates with germinal centers and Hürthle cells.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Name the rare form of thyroiditis characterized by extensive, hard 'woody' fibrosis that extends beyond the thyroid capsule and is associated with IgG4-related disease.
back:
• Riedel Thyroiditis
• Clinically mimics malignancy by appearing fixed
• Part of systemic IgG4-related fibro-inflammatory conditions.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In the initial phase of Hashimoto thyroiditis, a transient state of hyperthyroidism resulting from follicle rupture and hormone leakage is called [___].
back:
• Hashitoxicosis
• Characterized by elevated free T4/T3 and suppressed TSH
• Precedes the gradual progression to permanent hypothyroidism.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 30-year-old woman, 4 months postpartum, presents with mild tachycardia and a painless goiter. Laboratory tests show mild hyperthyroidism followed by a brief hypothyroid state. Identify this condition.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless/Postpartum) Thyroiditis
• An autoimmune process with lymphocytic inflammation
• Most patients eventually return to a euthyroid state.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Analyze the laboratory findings expected in the active phase of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis regarding thyroid hormones and radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU).
back:
• Hormones: Elevated free T4 and T3 (due to follicle destruction)
• TSH: Suppressed
• RAIU: Paradoxically decreased (unlike Graves disease) because the damaged follicular cells cannot trap iodine.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast 'Hashitoxicosis' with Graves disease regarding their mechanism of hyperthyroidism.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis: Passive release of preformed hormone due to gland inflammation/destruction.
• Graves: Active hyper-synthesis of hormone due to TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies (TSI).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Patients with long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis carry a significantly increased risk for the development of which specific extra-thyroidal malignancy?
back:
• Extranodal Marginal Zone B-cell Lymphoma
• Often occurs within the thyroid gland itself
• Arises from chronic lymphocytic stimulation.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the thyroid follicles are frequently lined by [___] cells, which are metaplastic epithelial cells containing abundant, granular eosinophilic cytoplasm.
back:
Hürthle (oxyphil) cells
* Represent a metaplastic response of follicular epithelium to chronic injury
* Contain numerous mitochondria
* Characteristically seen alongside a dense lymphocytic infiltrate

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a sudden, painful enlargement of the thyroid gland following a recent viral upper respiratory infection. Microscopic examination reveals multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
* Most common cause of thyroid pain
* Triggered by viral infections (seasonal)
* Self-limited course (typically 6-8 weeks)

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells in the pathogenesis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
Direct cell-mediated destruction
* T cells recognize thyroid autoantigens
* Induce apoptosis of thyroid follicular cells
* Leads to progressive depletion of thyroid parenchyma and subsequent hypothyroidism

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake and clinical pain associated with Graves disease versus granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis during their respective thyrotoxic phases.
back:
Radioactive Iodine Uptake:
* Graves: Diffusely increased (hyperfunction)
* Granulomatous: Diminished (leakage of preformed hormone)
Clinical Pain:
* Graves: Painless
* Granulomatous: Painful

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the specific malignancy for which patients with long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis carry a significantly increased risk.
back:
Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma
* Arises within the thyroid gland
* Driven by chronic autoimmune stimulation and lymphocytic infiltration

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Riedel thyroiditis is an extremely rare condition characterized by extensive fibrosis of the thyroid and surrounding neck structures, and it is considered a manifestation of [___]-related disease.
back:
IgG4 (Immunoglobulin G4)
* Characterized by systemic fibro-inflammatory processes
* Presents as a hard, fixed thyroid mass
* Clinically mimics thyroid carcinoma

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 30-year-old female presents four months postpartum with a painless, mildly enlarged thyroid and symptoms of hyperthyroidism. Laboratory tests show the presence of antithyroid peroxidase antibodies. State the most likely diagnosis.
back:
Subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis
* Variant known as postpartum thyroiditis
* Autoimmune basis (often transitions to hypothyroidism)
* Lacks the Hürthle cell change seen in Hashimoto

category: Define thyroiditis
coreConcept: Mechanism of transient hyperthyroidism in thyroiditis
front: Describe the sequence of hormonal leakage in the early stages of subacute thyroiditis.
back:
Inflammatory destruction release
* Viral or autoimmune injury disrupts follicles
* Preformed T3 and T4 leak into circulation
* Causes transient primary hyperthyroidism with low TSH and low iodine uptake

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the histologic features of Hashimoto thyroiditis with subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis regarding fibrosis and Hürthle cell metaplasia.
back:
Hashimoto Thyroiditis:
* Prominent fibrosis
* Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia
Subacute Lymphocytic:
* Minimal to absent fibrosis
* Absent Hürthle cell metaplasia

category: Define thyroiditis
front: List the two primary circulating autoantibodies found in the vast majority of patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
Specific Autoantibodies:
* Antithyroglobulin antibodies
* Antithyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The most common cause of hypothyroidism in areas where dietary iodine levels are sufficient is [___].
back: Hashimoto thyroiditis (also known as chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 48-year-old female presents with a painless, diffuse goiter and gradual weight gain. Histology shows extensive lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and Hürthle cell metaplasia. Identify the diagnosis.
back: Hashimoto thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Describe the primary immunologic mechanism of thyrocyte destruction in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell mediated cell death.
• Cytokine-mediated injury (IFN-γ from activated Th1 cells).
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the painful nature and typical triggers of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis with Subacute Lymphocytic thyroiditis.
back:
• Granulomatous: Painful; triggered by viral infections; features giant cells.
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Painless; often autoimmune/postpartum; lymphocytic infiltrates without giant cells.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the defining histologic hallmark of "Hürthle cells" found in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: Metaplastic follicular epithelial cells containing abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A rare, hard, and fixed thyroid mass characterized by extensive fibrosis extending beyond the gland capsule and associated with IgG4-related disease is [___].
back: Riedel thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 35-year-old female presents with a tender thyroid gland following an upper respiratory infection. Scintigraphy reveals decreased iodine uptake despite elevated serum T3 and T4. Identify the diagnosis.
back: Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the pathophysiological mechanism of the "Hashitoxicosis" phase during the early course of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Follicle disruption leads to uncontrolled leak of preformed hormones.
• Causes transient thyrotoxicosis before the gland reaches a hypothyroid state.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings between Graves disease and Granulomatous thyroiditis during their respective thyrotoxic phases.
back:
• Graves disease: Diffusely increased uptake.
• Granulomatous thyroiditis: Decreased uptake (due to damaged follicles).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Name three non-endocrine autoimmune diseases that occur with increased frequency in patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
• Sjögren syndrome.
• Myasthenia gravis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The condition defined by a diverse group of disorders characterized by thyroid inflammation is collectively termed [___].
back:
• Thyroiditis.
• Key subtypes include Hashimoto, subacute granulomatous, and subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis.
• Manifests with varying degrees of thyroid dysfunction and mass effects.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painful, enlarged thyroid following a viral upper respiratory infection. Biopsy reveals multinucleated giant cells enclosing pools of colloid. This indicates [___].
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Triggered by viral antigens or host tissue damage.
• Stimulates a self-limited cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the immune mechanisms leading to thyrocyte destruction in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell mediated killing.
• Cytokine-mediated (IFN-gamma) macrophage activation.
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) via antithyroid antibodies.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the clinical presentation and radioactive iodine uptake of Subacute Granulomatous Thyroiditis versus Graves Disease.
back:
• Granulomatous: Painful thyroid, viral trigger, and decreased iodine uptake.
• Graves: Painless, autoimmune TSH-receptor activation, and diffusely increased iodine uptake.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: State the systemic disease association and physical examination hallmark of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Associated with IgG4-related disease.
• Hallmark is a hard, "fixed" thyroid mass mimicking carcinoma.
• Caused by extensive fibrosis extending beyond the capsule.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, follicular epithelial cells metaplastically transform into large cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm called [___].
back:
• Hürthle (oxyphil) cells.
• Feature large nuclei with prominent nucleoli.
• Represents a cellular response to chronic autoimmune injury.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 30-year-old woman three months after delivery presents with a painless goiter and mild hyperthyroidism. Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are positive. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Subacute lymphocytic (postpartum) thyroiditis.
• Characterized by lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal centers.
• Typically lacks the fibrosis or Hürthle cell change of Hashimoto.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Describe the proposed mechanism of cellular injury in Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Viral-induced host damage exposing sequestered antigens.
• Stimulates a cytotoxic T-cell response against follicular cells.
• Self-limited process that typically returns to euthyroid state.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the extent of fibrosis in "classic" Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is localized and confined within the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Extensive fibrosis penetrates the capsule into contiguous neck structures.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Define "hashitoxicosis" in the context of thyroiditis progression.
back:
• A transient initial hyperthyroid phase.
• Caused by inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles.
• Results in the acute release of preformed thyroid hormones into blood.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: In regions where dietary iodine intake is sufficient, the primary cause of hypothyroidism in the adult population is [___].
back: Hashimoto Thyroiditis (Chronic Autoimmune Thyroiditis).

category: Define thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of Subacute Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with severe anterior neck pain radiating to the ear, accompanied by fever and malaise. She reports having a flu-like illness two weeks ago. Thyroid radioactive iodine uptake is low. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back: Granulomatous (de Quervain) Thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of cytokines and CD4+ Th1 cells in the destructive phase of Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
back:
• Th1 cells secrete interferon-gamma.
• This activates macrophages which damage follicles.
• Locally released cytokines (TNF) promote thyrocyte apoptosis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the palpation findings and degree of tissue involvement in Riedel Thyroiditis versus 'classic' Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
back:
• Riedel: Hard, 'woody' fixed mass; fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures (IgG4-related).
• Hashimoto: Rubbery, diffuse enlargement; fibrosis is confined within the thyroid capsule.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the variant of thyroiditis that typically occurs in parous women and histologically shows granulomas restricted to the spermatic-equivalent tubules of the thyroid, often presenting with a painless mass.
back: Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) Thyroiditis.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The characteristic metaplastic change in Hashimoto Thyroiditis, where follicular cells develop abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm rich in mitochondria, is referred to as [___] change.
back: Hürthle cell (or oxyphil cell) metaplasia.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A patient with newly diagnosed Hashimoto Thyroiditis unexpectedly presents with heat intolerance, tachycardia, and elevated free T4. This transient hyperthyroid state is known as [___].
back: Hashitoxicosis (caused by the initial inflammatory disruption of follicles releasing preformed thyroid hormones).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Describe the cellular mechanism leading to the formation of the hallmark 'Schiller-Duval-like' giant cells in Granulomatous Thyroiditis.
back:
• Follicular disruption releases colloid into the interstitium.
• Extravasated colloid triggers a foreign-body reaction.
• Multinucleated giant cells form to sequester and phagocytose the colloid.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the typical radioactive iodine (RAI) uptake pattern in Graves Disease with the pattern seen in the thyrotoxic phase of Subacute Thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased RAI uptake (active synthesis).
• Subacute Thyroiditis: Decreased RAI uptake (leakage of preformed hormone; synthesis is suppressed).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: State the most significant neoplastic risk associated with the chronic inflammatory milieu of Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
back: Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (Thyroid Lymphoma).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The most common cause of hypothyroidism in regions of the world where iodine levels are sufficient is [___].
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis (struma lymphomatosa)
• Characterized by gradual and progressive thyroid failure
• Female predominance (10:1 to 20:1)

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless, symmetric goiter and lethargy. Biopsy reveals follicles lined by cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm. What is the diagnosis and the specific term for these cells?
back:
• Diagnosis: Hashimoto thyroiditis
• Cells: Hürthle cells (oncocytes)
• Represent a metaplastic response to chronic follicular injury

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the three main immunologic mechanisms contributing to thyroid follicular cell death in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell mediated destruction
• Cytokine-mediated injury from activated CD4+ Th1 cells
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (NK cells)

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the nature of thyroid pain and the presence of multinucleate giant cells between Hashimoto thyroiditis and Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Typically painless enlargement; lacks giant cells (shows lymphocytic germinal centers).
• Granulomatous: Exquisitely painful thyroid; contains giant cells enclosing pools of colloid.

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Define 'Hashitoxicosis' and explain its underlying mechanism.
back:
• Transient hyperthyroidism during early Hashimoto thyroiditis
• Caused by inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles
• Results in leakage of preformed T3 and T4 into circulation

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The presumed etiology of [___] thyroiditis is a viral infection, often preceded by a history of an upper respiratory infection.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• Characterized by a seasonal incidence (peaking in summer)
• Results in self-limited thyroid inflammation

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 30-year-old female presents 3 months postpartum with mild hyperthyroidism and a painless goiter. She has high titers of antithyroid peroxidase antibodies. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis
• Often occurs in the postpartum period
• May eventually evolve into overt hypothyroidism

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain how the immune response in Granulomatous thyroiditis is initiated and why it differs from Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Initiated by virus-induced tissue damage exposing thyroid antigens
• Stimulates a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response
• Unlike Hashimoto, it is self-limited and not self-perpetuating

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast Riedel thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis based on the extent of fibrotic tissue spread.
back:
• Hashimoto: Interstitial fibrosis is present but limited to the gland capsule.
• Riedel: Dense fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into surrounding neck structures (fixed mass).

category: Define thyroiditis
front: List the two most common circulating autoantibodies found in the majority of patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Antithyroglobulin antibodies
• Antithyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies
• Essential for confirming autoimmune etiology

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the follicular cells undergo a metaplastic response to chronic injury, resulting in cells with abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (Oxyphil cells)
• Characterized by granular eosinophilic cytoplasm
• Represent a response to ongoing autoimmune-mediated cellular stress
• Often show large nuclei with prominent nucleoli.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 50-year-old female presents with painless, symmetric thyroid enlargement and weight gain. Histology reveals dense lymphocytic infiltrates with well-developed germinal centers. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis
• Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas
• Characterized by autoimmune follicular destruction
• Microscopic hallmark: Mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate with germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the three primary immunologic mechanisms that contribute to thyroid follicular cell death in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell mediated killing
• Cytokine-mediated injury (Th1 cells releasing IFN-γ for macrophage activation)
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) via antithyroid antibodies.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the microscopic features of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those of Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) Thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and significant interstitial fibrosis.
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Minimal to no fibrosis; lacks significant Hürthle cell change.
• Both: Feature lymphocytic infiltrates and germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the morphologic evolution of Granulomatous (de Quervain) Thyroiditis from the early active phase to the later stages.
back:
• Early: Neutrophilic microabscesses and follicular disruption.
• Intermediate: Granulomatous inflammation with multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid.
• Late: Chronic inflammatory infiltrate and replacement fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
coreConcept: Giant Cell Response in de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis is microscopically distinguished from other forms by the presence of [___] enclosing fragmented colloid pools.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells
• Occurs in response to virus-induced host tissue damage
• Forms a patchy, self-limited granulomatous reaction
• Often preceded by an upper respiratory infection.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 40-year-old female presents with severe neck pain and an enlarged, firm thyroid following a viral prodrome. A biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation and multinucleated cells. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) Thyroiditis
• Most common cause of thyroid pain
• Triggered by viral infections (seasonal peaks)
• Characterized by transient hyperthyroidism followed by recovery.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: How does the extent of fibrosis help distinguish Riedel thyroiditis from the fibrosis seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis?
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is confined within the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Extensive "woody" fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures.
• Riedel is often associated with IgG4-related disease.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the typical gross cut-surface appearance of Graves disease with that of a Multinodular Goiter.
back:
• Graves: Diffuse, beefy-red, and meaty (resembling muscle).
• Multinodular Goiter: Coarsely irregular with nodules of brown, gelatinous colloid.
• Graves shows symmetric enlargement; goiter is often asymmetric.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: State the typical gross findings of the thyroid gland in a patient with chronic Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric enlargement
• Firm and somewhat nodular consistency
• Pale, yellow-tan cut surface
• Intact capsule well-demarcated from adjacent tissues.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the atrophic thyroid follicles are frequently lined by epithelial cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm termed [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (oxyphil cells)
• Represent a metaplastic response of follicular cuboidal epithelium
• Characteristic of Hashimoto but not specific to it

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painful neck mass and fever following an upper respiratory infection. Histology reveals multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid. Diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• Triggered by viral infection or post-viral inflammatory response
• Most common cause of thyroid pain

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the cellular mechanism leading to follicular destruction in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T cell-mediated killing of thyrocytes
• Cytokine-mediated injury (IFN-γ from Th1 cells activates macrophages)
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) via NK cells

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the microscopic features of Hashimoto thyroiditis with Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Significant fibrosis and prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Minimal to no fibrosis or Hürthle cell change
• Both: Feature lymphocytic infiltrates and germinal centers

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the subtype of thyroiditis characterized by a hard, "fixed" neck mass and fibrosis extending into adjacent neck structures.
back:
• Riedel thyroiditis
• Associated with IgG4-related disease systemic involvement
• Clinically mimics thyroid carcinoma due to "woody" consistency

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The early active inflammatory phase of granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis is histologically characterized by the presence of [___] forming microabscesses.
back:
• Neutrophils
• Precedes the development of characteristic granulomatous lesions
• Followed by aggregates of lymphocytes and macrophages

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 30-year-old woman presents 3 months postpartum with a painless goiter and mild hyperthyroidism. FNAC shows lymphocytic infiltration but no Hürthle cells. Diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis
• Postpartum variant is a common autoimmune subtype
• One-third eventually progress to overt permanent hypothyroidism

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the mechanism of transient 'Hashitoxicosis' during the early stages of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Inflammation causes initial follicle disruption
• Preformed thyroid hormones are leaked into the bloodstream
• Results in transient hyperthyroidism before progressive glandular failure

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the gross appearance of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Diffuse, symmetric, pale yellow-tan, and firm
• Granulomatous: Unilateral or bilateral enlargement; firm, yellow-white patchy areas
• Hashimoto is painless; Granulomatous is extremely painful

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Name the specific malignancy for which patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis are at a significantly increased risk.
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma
• Develops within the chronic inflammatory thyroid environment
• Also associated with increased risk for papillary carcinoma

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Thyroiditis is defined as a diverse group of disorders sharing the common characteristic of [___].
back:
* Thyroid inflammation
* Includes autoimmune, viral, and fibrotic subtypes
* Pathogenesis often leads to transient or permanent thyroid dysfunction

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 48-year-old female presents with a painless, symmetric goiter and symptoms of cold intolerance and fatigue. Laboratory findings show anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies. Diagnosis?
back:
* Hashimoto thyroiditis
* Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions
* Autoimmune-mediated destruction of thyroid parenchyma

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain how CD8+ cytotoxic T cells and Th1-derived cytokines contribute to thyrocyte injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* CD8+ T cells: Directly kill thyroid follicular cells
* Th1 cytokines (IFN-̳): Recruit and activate macrophages
* Result: Progressive depletion of thyroid epithelial cells and replacement by fibrosis

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the evolution of hypothyroidism in subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis versus Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Hashimoto: Gradually progressive and usually permanent thyroid failure
* Painless thyroiditis: Often transient and self-limited (postpartum variant)
* Evolution: One-third of painless cases evolve to overt hypothyroidism over 10 years

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the most common precipitating trigger and seasonal pattern associated with granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
* Trigger: Viral infection (often preceded by an upper respiratory infection)
* Viruses: Coxsackievirus, mumps, adenovirus
* Pattern: Seasonal incidence peaking in summer

category: Define thyroiditis
front: The microscopic presence of [___] enclosing fragmented pools of colloid is the defining histologic hallmark of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
* Multinucleate giant cells
* Component of granulomatous inflammation
* Accompanied by lymphocytic and activated macrophage infiltrates

category: Define thyroiditis
front: A 52-year-old male presents with a rock-hard, fixed thyroid mass that mimics anaplastic carcinoma. Histology reveals extensive fibrosis extending into adjacent neck structures. Diagnosis?
back:
* Riedel thyroiditis
* Rare disorder characterized by dense systemic fibrosis
* Association: Linked to IgG4-related disease

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Explain the pathophysiologic mechanism of 'hashitoxicosis' seen early in some patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Follicle disruption: Autoimmune attack ruptures thyroid follicles
* Hormone leak: Releases preformed T4/T3 into systemic circulation
* Labs: Transient hyperthyroidism (high T4, low TSH) with low radioactive iodine uptake

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Contrast the metabolic mechanism of thyrotoxicosis in Graves disease versus the 'thyroiditis' group (de Quervain or painless).
back:
* Graves: Hyperthyroidism (increased synthesis) due to TSI stimulation
* Thyroiditis: Hormone leak (passive release) due to follicular damage
* RAIU Scan: Increased uptake in Graves; decreased uptake in thyroiditis

category: Define thyroiditis
front: Identify the specific metaplastic follicular epithelial cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm that are characteristic of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* H3rthle cells (Oxyphil cells)
* Metaplastic response of low cuboidal epithelium to chronic injury
* Distinguishing feature from subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: [___] are metaplastic epithelial cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm that serve as a hallmark histological feature of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
Hürthle cells (Oxyphil cells).
- Found lining atrophic follicles.
- Represent a metaplastic response to chronic autoimmune injury.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a sudden onset of neck pain, fever, and a firm, tender thyroid following a viral upper respiratory infection. Histology reveals multinucleated giant cells surrounding fragmented colloid. Diagnosis: [___].
back:
Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
- Most common cause of thyroid pain.
- Triggered by viral infections (mumps, measles, Coxsackie).

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the specific immunologic mechanisms responsible for follicular destruction in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
- CD8+ T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity.
- Cytokine-mediated injury (Th1-derived IFN-γ activating macrophages).
- Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (anti-thyroid antibodies).

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the microscopic findings of Hashimoto thyroiditis with Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis regarding metaplasia and stroma.
back:
- Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and interstitial fibrosis.
- Painless: Lacks significant Hürthle cells and fibrosis; limited to lymphocytic infiltration and germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the defining morphological hallmark and the systemic association of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
- Extensive, dense fibrosis extending through the thyroid capsule into adjacent neck structures.
- Associated with systemic IgG4-related disease.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The pathognomonic histological lesion in de Quervain thyroiditis involves [___] enclosing pools of colloid within fragmented follicles.
back:
Multinucleate giant cells.
- Forms part of the granulomatous reaction.
- Follows an initial neutrophilic/microabscess phase.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 32-year-old woman presents 4 months postpartum with a painless thyroid enlargement and mild hyperthyroidism. Laboratory tests show elevated T4 and low TSH. Biopsy reveals lymphocytic infiltration but no fibrosis. Diagnosis: [___].
back:
Subacute Lymphocytic (Postpartum/Painless) thyroiditis.
- Autoimmune process.
- Clinically manifests as transient hyperthyroidism followed by recovery or hypothyroidism.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the morphological transition of thyroid follicles during the progression of Granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
- Early phase: Neutrophilic infiltration with follicular disruption and microabscesses.
- Late phase: Aggregates of lymphocytes, macrophages, and multinucleate giant cells creating colloid-containing granulomas.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the gross appearance of Hashimoto thyroiditis with that of a normal thyroid gland.
back:
- Hashimoto: Diffusely enlarged, pale yellow-tan, and firm (rubbery).
- Normal: Fleshy, soft, and reddish-brown.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: List the components of the characteristic mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate seen in autoimmune thyroiditis.
back:
- Small lymphocytes.
- Mature plasma cells.
- Well-developed germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, follicular epithelial cells often undergo a metaplastic response to chronic autoimmune injury, resulting in cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (Oxyphil cells).
• Characterized by mitochondria-rich, granular cytoplasm.
• Represents a cellular reaction to chronic inflammation.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a severely painful, tender thyroid and transient hyperthyroidism following a flu-like illness. Microscopic examination of the gland would likely reveal [___].
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid pools.
• Aggregates of lymphocytes and macrophages.
• Early neutrophilic microabscesses.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the specific cell-mediated immune mechanisms that lead to progressive thyroid depletion in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell-mediated killing of thyrocytes.
• Cytokine-mediated injury (Th1 cells secreting IFN-γ).
• Macrophage activation resulting in follicle damage.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the histological features of Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Lacks Hürthle cell metaplasia.
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Lacks prominent fibrosis.
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cells, follicular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the characteristic gross and microscopic morphological hallmarks of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Gross: Hard, "woody," and fixed thyroid mass.
• Microscopic: Dense fibrous tissue replacing parenchyma.
• Extension: Fibrosis penetrates the capsule into neck structures.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The pathognomonic histological feature of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis involves multinucleated [___] enclosing pools of colloid.
back:
• Giant cells.
• Forms in response to fragmented or extravasated colloid.
• Associated with collapsed follicles and chronic inflammation.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 32-year-old female, 3 months postpartum, presents with a painless goiter and mild hyperthyroidism. Biopsy shows lymphocytic infiltration and germinal centers but no Hürthle cells. State the underlying diagnosis.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic (Postpartum) thyroiditis.
• Self-limited autoimmune process.
• Histologically mimics Hashimoto but lacks metaplasia/scarring.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the viral-induced mechanism suspected in the development of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Viral respiratory infection triggers host tissue damage.
• Released thyroid antigens stimulate Cytotoxic T-lymphocytes.
• T-cells damage follicles in a limited, non-self-perpetuating reaction.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the lymphocytic infiltrate of Hashimoto thyroiditis with that of Grave's disease.
back:
• Hashimoto: Dense infiltrate with well-developed germinal centers and follicle destruction.
• Grave's: Interstitial T-cell-predominant infiltrate without follicle destruction.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: List the three essential microscopic features that define the classic 'Struma Lymphomatosa' pattern in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate (lymphocytes and plasma cells).
• Well-developed germinal centers.
• Follicular atrophy with Hürthle cell change.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the follicular epithelial cells respond to chronic autoimmune injury by undergoing metaplasia into cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle (oxyphil) cells.
• These represent a metaplastic response of low cuboidal epithelium to chronic inflammatory stress.
• They contain numerous mitochondria, giving the granular appearance.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 40-year-old female presents with an acutely painful, enlarged thyroid following a recent upper respiratory infection. Histology reveals multinucleated giant cells and neutrophilic microabscesses. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• It is the most common cause of thyroid pain.
• Characterized by a post-viral inflammatory response and a self-limiting course.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the cellular mechanism of thyrocyte destruction mediated by CD8+ T cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Direct killing of thyroid follicular cells by cytotoxic CD8+ T cells.
• Cytokine-mediated injury via IFN-gamma released from Th1 cells.
• Subsequent replacement of parenchyma by fibrosis and lymphocytic infiltrates.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis with the distinctive fibrotic pattern seen in Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Interstitial fibrosis is restricted within the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Dense, systemic-type fibrosis extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures.
• Riedel is often a manifestation of IgG4-related disease.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the characteristic clinical and histological features of subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis.
back:
• Clinical: Painless goiter with transient hyperthyroidism (often postpartum).
• Histology: Lymphocytic infiltration and patchy follicle disruption.
• Key Distinction: Lacks the Hürthle cell metaplasia and germinal centers of Hashimoto.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The histological hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis is a widespread mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate containing small lymphocytes and mature plasma cells that frequently form [___].
back:
• Well-developed germinal centers.
• This lymphoid hyperplasia often results in a firm, pale, yellow-tan, and nodular appearance on the cut surface.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A woman with a chronic painless goiter suddenly develops palpitations and heat intolerance. Laboratory tests show low radioactive iodine uptake. Identify this transient phase and its underlying cause.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis.
• Caused by the acute rupture of thyroid follicles during inflammatory destruction.
• Leads to a transient leak of preformed thyroid hormones into the circulation.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
