front: Explain how the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan distinguishes Granulomatous thyroiditis from Graves disease during a hyperthyroid presentation.
back:
• Granulomatous: Low iodine uptake because damaged follicles cannot trap iodine.
• Graves: High, diffuse iodine uptake because follicular cells are hyperfunctioning.
• This differentiates hormone leak from hyper-synthesis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the typical gross appearance of the thyroid gland in de Quervain thyroiditis with that of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• de Quervain: Asymmetric enlargement; involved areas are firm, yellow-white, and may adhere to surrounding structures.
• Hashimoto: Diffuse, symmetric enlargement; cut surface is yellow-tan and well-demarcated from adjacent tissues.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Which specific histological feature is most useful to distinguish Hashimoto thyroiditis from follicular neoplasms in fine-needle aspiration?
back:
• Presence of a heterogeneous population of lymphocytes and plasma cells.
• Found in conjunction with clusters of metaplastic Hürthle cells.
• Neoplasms typically show monomorphic cell populations.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The characteristic metaplastic response of thyroid follicular cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis, appearing as cells with abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm, is the formation of [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (also known as oxyphil cells).
• These represent a response of the low cuboidal epithelium to chronic autoimmune injury.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 40-year-old female presents with a painful, enlarged thyroid and fever following a viral upper respiratory infection. Biopsy reveals multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid. The diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• This is the most common cause of thyroid pain.
• Characterized by a self-limited inflammatory course.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the role of specific T-cell populations in the progressive destruction of thyroid follicles during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells: Direct killing of thyroid epithelial cells.
• CD4+ Th1 cells: Secretion of IFN-gamma, which activates macrophages to damage follicles.
• Result: Progressive depletion of thyrocytes and replacement by fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the epithelial metaplasia and fibrotic changes found in Hashimoto thyroiditis with those in Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and significant interstitial fibrosis.
• Painless Thyroiditis: Lacks prominent Hürthle cells and significant fibrosis; characterized mainly by lymphocytic infiltration.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the primary morphological hallmark that distinguishes Riedel thyroiditis from all other inflammatory thyroid conditions.
back:
• Extensive, dense fibrosis extending beyond the thyroid capsule.
• It invades contiguous neck structures (trachea, esophagus).
• Clinically mimics carcinoma by forming a hard, fixed mass.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The prominent mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate in Hashimoto thyroiditis is microscopically distinguished by the presence of well-developed [___].
back:
• Germinal centers.
• These are located within the dense lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate that replaces the parenchyma.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 28-year-old female develops a painless goiter and mild hyperthyroidism three months after delivery. Histology shows focal follicular disruption and lymphocytic aggregates without Hürthle cells. Name the condition.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic (Postpartum) Thyroiditis.
• It is a variant of autoimmune thyroiditis often seen in the postpartum period.
• Typically follows a self-limited clinical course.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the cellular composition and arrangement of the 'granuloma' in de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Patchy aggregates of lymphocytes, activated macrophages, and plasma cells.
• Multinucleate giant cells surround or enclose fragmented colloid pools.
• Often preceded by a neutrophilic microabscess phase.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the nature of thyroid enlargement and consistency in Graves disease versus Multinodular Goiter.
back:
• Graves: Symmetrical, diffuse enlargement with a 'meaty' beefy-red parenchyma.
• Multinodular Goiter: Asymmetrical, irregular enlargement with multiple colloid-filled nodules and frequent areas of hemorrhage/calcification.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Name the clinical-morphological phenomenon in Hashimoto thyroiditis where acute follicular disruption leads to transient hyperthyroidism.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis.
• Caused by the inflammatory spillover of preformed thyroid hormones from damaged follicles before the inevitable transition to hypothyroidism.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the metaplastic response of follicular epithelium to chronic injury results in the formation of [___] cells, characterized by abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm.
back:
Hürthle (oxyphil) cells.
• These represent a characteristic metaplastic response to chronic autoimmune-mediated injury.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with sudden onset of a tender, enlarged thyroid and fever two weeks after an upper respiratory infection. Histology reveals multinucleated giant cells surrounding fragmented colloid. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Characterized by post-viral inflammation.
• The most common cause of thyroid pain.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the primary cell-mediated pathways leading to follicular depletion and destruction in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell destruction of thyrocytes.
• Th1 cytokine-mediated (IFN-gamma) macrophage activation.
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the microscopic findings of Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and significant interstitial fibrosis.
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Lacks significant Hürthle cell change and prominent fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: List the three characteristic components of the "granulomatous" response seen in the active phase of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid.
• Activated macrophages, plasma cells, and lymphocytes.
• Collapsed and damaged thyroid follicles.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The rare variant of thyroiditis presenting as a hard, fixed mass mimicking carcinoma due to extensive systemic [___] is known as Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
IgG4-related fibrosis.
• Involves the thyroid and contiguous neck structures.
• Associated with extra-thyroidal sites like the retroperitoneum.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A middle-aged woman presents with a painless symmetric goiter. FNAC shows a heterogeneous population of lymphocytes and numerous cells with small regular nuclei and abundant pink cytoplasm. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
Hashimoto thyroiditis.
• Lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal centers.
• Presence of Hürthle cells is a diagnostic hallmark in FNAC samples.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the temporal progression of inflammatory infiltrates during the active phase of Granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Early phase: Neutrophils forming microabscesses with follicle disruption.
• Late phase: Lymphocytes and macrophages forming granulomas with giant cells.
• Recovery: Patchy chronic inflammation and fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the anatomic distribution and extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is limited and never extends beyond the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Extensive, woody fibrosis penetrates the capsule into adjacent neck structures.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the clinical subtype of thyroiditis that is morphologically indistinguishable from Subacute Lymphocytic thyroiditis but occurs in roughly 5% of women following delivery.
back:
Postpartum thyroiditis.
• Presents with mild transient hyperthyroidism or painless goiter.
• One-third progress to overt hypothyroidism over a decade.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The histological hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis is the presence of metaplastic follicular epithelial cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (Oxyphil cells).
• Represent a response to chronic follicular injury.
• Feature large nuclei with prominent nucleoli.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painful, tender neck mass following a viral sore throat. Histology reveals multinucleated giant cells surrounding fragmented colloid. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Granulomatous (De Quervain) Thyroiditis.
• Most common cause of thyroid pain.
• Characterized by granulomatous inflammation and neutrophil microabscesses.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the role of T-cells in the tissue destruction characteristic of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cells: Direct killing of thyrocytes.
• CD4+ Th1 cells: Secrete IFN-gamma to activate macrophages.
• Results in progressive parenchymal depletion and lymphocytic infiltration.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the microscopic findings of Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding Hürthle cell change and fibrosis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and interstitial fibrosis.
• Painless Thyroiditis: Lacks Hürthle cell change and significant fibrosis.
• Both share lymphocytic infiltrates and germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Distinguish the fibrotic involvement in Riedel Thyroiditis from classic Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Riedel: Dense fibrosis extending through the capsule into adjacent neck structures.
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is confined within the intact thyroid capsule.
• Riedel is often associated with IgG4-related disease.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In the early active phase of Granulomatous Thyroiditis, the primary microscopic finding consists of follicles replaced by [___].
back:
• Neutrophils forming microabscesses.
• Progresses later to lymphocytic, macrophage, and giant cell aggregates.
• Eventually leads to follicular collapse and scarring.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A postpartum female presents with transient hyperthyroidism followed by a painless goiter. Fine-needle aspiration shows lymphocytic infiltration and germinal centers but no Hürthle cells. Diagnosis?
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic (Postpartum) Thyroiditis.
• Autoimmune in nature.
• Distinguished from Hashimoto by lack of Hürthle cell metaplasia.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
coreConcept: Giant Cell Formation in De Quervain
front: Describe the histogenesis of multinucleated giant cells in Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Viral-induced follicular damage releases colloid into the interstitium.
• Extravasated colloid elicits a foreign-body type reaction.
• Macrophages fuse to form giant cells that ingest/enclose the colloid.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the thyroid's gross appearance in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Graves disease.
back:
• Hashimoto: Firm, pale yellow-tan, and distinctly nodular/bosselated.
• Graves: Symmetrically enlarged, soft, and meaty/beefy red (resembling muscle).
• Both typically involve an intact capsule.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: What is the clinical significance of finding prominent germinal centers in a thyroid biopsy?
back:
• Suggests Hashimoto or Subacute Lymphocytic Thyroiditis.
• Indicates a chronic, organized lymphocytic immune response.
• In Hashimoto, associated with increased risk of B-cell lymphoma.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: The histologic hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis, characterized by transformed follicular epithelial cells with abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm, is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (oxyphil cells).
• They represent a metaplastic response to chronic injury.
• Characteristically surround atrophic thyroid follicles.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painless, diffusely enlarged thyroid and gradual hypothyroidism. Biopsy reveals dense lymphocytic infiltrates with well-developed germinal centers. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
• Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions.
• Strong association with autoantibodies against thyroglobulin and peroxidase.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the role of the viral trigger in the development of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Virus-induced host tissue damage exposes thyroid antigens.
• This stimulates a self-limited cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response.
• Results in follicle destruction and release of preformed T3/T4.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the macroscopic and clinical presentation of Granulomatous thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Granulomatous: Unilateral or asymmetric enlargement; exquisitely painful/tender gland.
• Hashimoto: Diffuse, symmetric enlargement; painless; rubbery consistency.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the three primary immunologic mechanisms responsible for thyrocyte injury in Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T cell-mediated cell death.
• Cytokine-mediated death (IFN-gamma from Th1 cells activating macrophages).
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis, the characteristic microscopic finding involving multinucleate giant cells surrounding pools of colloid is termed [___].
back:
• Granulomatous inflammation.
• Distinguishes it from lymphocytic variants.
• Elicited by the spillover of colloid from disrupted follicles.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A postpartum woman presents with a painless goiter and mild transient hyperthyroidism. Histology shows lymphocytic infiltration and germinal centers but lacks fibrosis and Hürthle cell change. Name the likely condition.
back:
• Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) Thyroiditis.
• Distinguished from Hashimoto by the absence of fibrosis and Hürthle metaplasia.
• Common in the postpartum period.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Discuss the pathological extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Interstitial fibrosis is limited; it does not extend beyond the thyroid capsule.
• Riedel: Extensive, dense fibrosis that invades contiguous neck structures, mimicking carcinoma.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the lymphocytic morphology of Subacute Lymphocytic thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Painless Thyroiditis: Lymphocytic infiltrates/germinal centers present; lacks Hürthle cell change.
• Hashimoto: Lymphocytic infiltrates/germinal centers present; prominent Hürthle cell change and fibrosis.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the specific non-epithelial malignancy for which patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis are at increased risk.
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALT lymphoma).
• Arises due to chronic lymphocytic stimulation within the gland.
• Usually presents as rapid enlargement of a pre-existing goiter.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the atrophic thyroid follicles are often lined by metaplastic epithelial cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
* H'u00fcrthle (oxyphil) cells
* Represent a metaplastic response to chronic follicular injury
* High-yield diagnostic feature in fine-needle aspiration specimens

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A 52-year-old female presents with a painless, diffusely enlarged, firm thyroid and clinical features of myxedema. Histology reveals extensive lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates and well-developed germinal centers. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
* Hashimoto thyroiditis
* Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions
* Characterized by progressive destruction of thyroid parenchyma

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Outline the characteristic microscopic features of Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis during its peak inflammatory stage.
back:
* Disrupted follicles with neutrophil microabscesses
* Chronic inflammatory cells (lymphocytes, macrophages, plasma cells)
* Multinucleate giant cells enclosing central pools of colloid
* Eventual replacement by focal scarring

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the histological progression of subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding fibrosis and H'u00fcrthle cell change.
back:
* Painless Thyroiditis: Lacks significant fibrosis and H'u00fcrthle cell change.
* Hashimoto: Features prominent fibrosis and characteristic H'u00fcrthle cell metaplasia.
* Both: Exhibit lymphocytic infiltration and germinal centers.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Identify the salient morphological hallmark that distinguishes Riedel thyroiditis from other inflammatory thyroid disorders.
back:
* Extensive, dense fibrosis involving the thyroid
* Extension of fibrosis beyond the gland capsule into surrounding neck structures
* Clinically produces a hard and fixed mass (IgG4-related disease component)

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Granulomatous thyroiditis is believed to be triggered by a [___] and typically presents with a seasonal peak during summer months.
back:
* Viral infection
* Frequently associated with a preceding upper respiratory infection
* Causes virus-induced host tissue damage and cytotoxic T-cell response

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: A woman 4 months postpartum presents with mild hyperthyroidism and a painless, moderately enlarged thyroid. Biopsy shows large germinal centers but no H'u00fcrthle cells. Predict the clinical course.
back:
* Postpartum (Subacute Lymphocytic) Thyroiditis
* Transient hyperthyroidism followed by possible hypothyroidism
* Approximately one-third evolve into overt Hashimoto thyroiditis over 10 years

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Explain the role of CD8+ T-cells and cytokines in the progressive depletion of thyrocytes in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells: Direct destruction of thyroid follicular cells.
* Cytokines: Th1 cells release IFN-̳, which recruits and activates injurious macrophages.
* Leads to progressive parenchymal replacement by fibrosis and lymphocytes.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Contrast the follicle morphology and colloid appearance in Graves disease versus Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Graves: Tall, crowded columnar cells with scalloped colloid margins (hyperplasia).
* Hashimoto: Atrophic follicles with H'u00fcrthle cell change and parenchymal destruction.
* In Graves, papillae lack fibrovascular cores, unlike papillary carcinoma.

category: Describe salient morphological features of clinically significant subtypes of thyroiditis: i
front: Describe the typical gross appearance of the cut surface of a thyroid gland affected by classic Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Pale, yellow-tan, and firm cut surface
* Symmetric and diffuse enlargement (usually)
* Intact capsule with prominent nodularity observed within the parenchyma

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the thyroid follicles are often lined by metaplastic epithelial cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle (oxyphil) cells
• Represent a response to chronic injury
• Characteristically seen in fine-needle aspiration samples

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 52-year-old female presents with a painless goiter and initial symptoms of heat intolerance and palpitations. Lab results show elevated free T4 and suppressed TSH, but a 24-hour iodine uptake test is low. Identify this transient phase.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis
• Caused by the initial inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles
• Results in the release of preformed thyroid hormones

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD4+ Th1 cells in the destruction of thyroid follicular cells during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Secrete inflammatory cytokines (e.g., interferon-gamma)
• Recruit and activate macrophages
• Result in macrophage-mediated follicular damage

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the pattern of fibrosis in classic Hashimoto thyroiditis with that observed in Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is variable and confined within the thyroid capsule
• Riedel: Extensive fibrosis that extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures (IgG4-related)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis are at a significantly increased risk for developing which specific type of extranodal hematologic malignancy?
back:
• B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
• Specifically, extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALT lymphoma)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Polymorphisms in immune-regulation genes, such as [___] and PTPN22, are linked to an increased susceptibility to both Hashimoto thyroiditis and type 1 diabetes.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4)
• Also linked to IL2RA (interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A fine-needle aspiration of a firm, diffuse goiter in a 45-year-old female reveals a dense mononuclear infiltrate with well-developed germinal centers. Identify the likely diagnosis and the expected serum TSH level.
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis
• TSH will be elevated (compensatory for hypothyroidism)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the immunologic mechanism involving CD8+ T cells in Hashimoto-related tissue injury.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T cells directly destroy thyroid follicular cells
• Mechanism stems from a breakdown in self-tolerance to thyroid autoantigens

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding Hürthle cell change.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia is a hallmark
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Typically lacks Hürthle cell change and significant fibrosis

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the two primary autoantigens targeted by circulating antibodies in the majority of Hashimoto thyroiditis cases.
back:
• Thyroglobulin
• Thyroid peroxidase (TPO)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The characteristic metaplastic response of thyroid follicular epithelial cells to chronic autoimmune injury, resulting in cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (Oxyphil cells)
• Characterized by packed mitochondria and granular appearance
• Often surround atrophic follicles in a background of dense lymphocytic infiltration.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a painless, symmetrically enlarged thyroid and symptoms of lethargy and cold intolerance. Discuss the specific immune-mediated mechanisms responsible for the destruction of her thyrocytes.
back:
• CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell mediated cell death
• Cytokine-mediated damage (Th1 cells secreting IFN-γ to activate macrophages)
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) via antithyroid antibodies.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of Antithyroid Peroxidase (TPO) and Antithyroglobulin antibodies in the diagnosis of autoimmune thyroiditis versus biopsy findings.
back:
• Serum markers: Circulating TPO and thyroglobulin antibodies indicate a breakdown in self-tolerance.
• Histology: Distinguishes Hashimoto from other types via germinal centers and Hürthle cells.
• Antibodies assist diagnosis but do not solely confirm cell death.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 50-year-old woman with a diffuse, firm goiter is suspected of having either Hashimoto Thyroiditis or Subacute Lymphocytic (Painless) Thyroiditis. Contrast the microscopic features used to distinguish these two autoimmune conditions.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and extensive fibrosis.
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Lacks significant fibrosis and Hürthle cell change.
• Both: Feature mononuclear infiltrates and germinal centers, but Hashimoto shows progressive parenchymal destruction.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the primary pharmacological replacement agent used to manage Hashimoto-induced hypothyroidism and its expected effect on serum TSH levels.
back:
• Levothyroxine (Synthetic T4)
• Acts by restoring the circulating pool of thyroid hormone
• Suppresses elevated TSH via negative feedback on the anterior pituitary somatotrophs and hypothalamus.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: During the early clinical phase of Hashimoto thyroiditis, a transient state of hyperthyroidism caused by the inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles and release of preformed hormone is termed [___].
back:
• Hashitoxicosis
• Features elevated free T4/T3 and low TSH
• Characterized by decreased radioactive iodine uptake, distinguishing it from the hyperfunction of Graves disease.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass that is causing airway compression. Evaluate the most likely malignant transformation associated with this clinical history.
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma
• Arises due to chronic antigenic stimulation of the thyroid's lymphocytic infiltrate
• Patients have a significantly increased risk compared to the general population.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe how polymorphisms in immune-regulatory genes like CTLA4 and PTPN22 contribute to the common pathogenesis of Hashimoto thyroiditis and Type 1 Diabetes.
back:
• Leads to a generalized breakdown in T-cell self-tolerance
• Impairs the function of regulatory T-cells (Tregs)
• Facilitates the survival and activation of autoreactive effector T-cells against organ-specific antigens.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the serum TSH and radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) findings in the late atrophic stage of Hashimoto thyroiditis with the findings in Graves disease.
back:
• Hashimoto (Late): Elevated TSH (compensatory) with low RAIU due to parenchymal loss.
• Graves: Low TSH (suppressed) with diffusely increased RAIU due to stimulating autoantibodies (TSI).

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Name the specific cytokine produced by CD4+ Th1 cells that is primarily responsible for recruiting and activating macrophages in the Hashimoto thyroid lesion.
back:
• Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ)
• Induces follicular cell injury and apoptosis
• Promotes a pro-inflammatory microenvironment that sustains the autoimmune attack and progressive thyroid destruction.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The histological hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis, representing metaplastic follicular epithelial cells with abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm, is the [___].
back:
• H'u00fcrthle cell (also known as oxyphil cell).
  • Contains high mitochondrial density.
  • Represents a response to chronic follicular injury.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 55-year-old female presents with a painless, symmetrically enlarged thyroid and recent weight gain. Histology shows dense lymphocytic infiltrates and well-developed germinal centers. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis (Struma lymphomatosa).
  • Characterized by autoimmune parenchymal destruction.
  • Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD8+ T-cells in the tissue-specific destruction seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Mediate direct cytotoxic cell death of thyrocytes.
  • Recognize thyroid-specific autoantigens.
  • Contribute significantly to the progressive depletion of follicular epithelium.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the clinical hormonal profile of the initial "Hashitoxicosis" phase with that of the standard late-stage Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis: Transient hyperthyroidism (High T4, Low TSH) due to follicular rupture and hormone leakage.
  • Late-stage: Permanent hypothyroidism (Low T4, High TSH) due to total parenchymal loss and fibrosis.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the primary mechanism of action for thyroid-specific autoantibodies in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).
  • Antibodies target thyroglobulin and thyroid peroxidase.
  • Natural killer (NK) cells bind to these antibodies to initiate thyrocyte lysis.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Individuals with Hashimoto thyroiditis carry a significantly increased risk for the development of the hematopoietic malignancy known as [___].
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma.
  • Often referred to as MALT lymphoma within the thyroid.
  • Presents as a rapidly enlarging mass in a pre-existing goiter.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with positive anti-thyroglobulin antibodies is found to have polymorphisms in CTLA4 and PTPN22. Explain the pathophysiological significance of these genetic findings.
back:
• Associated with breakdown in T-cell self-tolerance.
  • CTLA4: Negatively regulates T-cell activation.
  • PTPN22: Encodes a phosphatase that modulates signaling in lymphoid cells.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the specific cytokine-mediated pathway that recruits activated macrophages to the thyroid during autoimmune inflammation.
back:
• Activated CD4+ Th1 cells secrete Interferon-gamma (IFN-̳).
  • IFN-̳ activates macrophages in the thyroid interstitium.
  • Results in bystander follicular damage and parenchymal collapse.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the distribution and limits of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is variable and strictly confined within the thyroid capsule.
  • Riedel: Dense, extensive fibrosis extending into adjacent neck structures (e.g., trachea, esophagus).

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Name the two most high-yield autoantibodies used to confirm a clinical diagnosis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Anti-thyroglobulin (anti-Tg) antibodies.
  • Anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies.
  • Present in the vast majority of patients with autoimmune thyroiditis.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The metaplastic response of thyroid follicular epithelium to chronic autoimmune injury, resulting in cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cell (oxyphil) change
• Represents a response of low cuboidal epithelium to injury
• Characteristic histological feature of Hashimoto thyroiditis

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless, firm, diffusely enlarged thyroid. Biopsy shows dense mononuclear infiltrates with well-developed germinal centers and atrophic follicles. Name the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis
• Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas
• Gradual thyroid failure due to autoimmune destruction

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells in the tissue damage associated with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Mediate direct killing of thyroid follicular epithelial cells
• Recognize thyroid autoantigens presented on the cell surface
• Leads to progressive depletion of thyroid parenchyma

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings in the early 'hashitoxicosis' phase of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those found in Graves disease.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis: Decreased uptake due to follicle disruption and leakage
• Graves disease: Diffusely increased uptake due to TSH receptor stimulation
• Distinguishes transient leakage from active hyperthyroidism

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the specific type of malignancy for which patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis carry a significantly increased risk.
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALT lymphoma)
• Arises within the thyroid gland due to chronic lymphocytic stimulation
• Association with other autoimmune diseases often coexists

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Genetic susceptibility to Hashimoto thyroiditis is linked to polymorphisms in immune-regulatory genes, specifically [___] and PTPN22.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte–associated antigen-4)
• Also associated with IL2RA (interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain)
• Shared genetic loci with Type 1 Diabetes and Graves disease

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with bradycardia, cold intolerance, and a pale yellow-tan thyroid on ultrasound. Describe the expected serum TSH and Free T4 levels.
back:
• Elevated serum TSH levels
• Decreased serum Free T4 (Thyroxine)
• Pattern reflects primary thyroid failure with loss of negative feedback

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the mechanism by which Th1 cytokines like interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) contribute to follicular injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Secreted by activated CD4+ helper T-cells
• Promotes recruitment and activation of macrophages
• Activated macrophages cause indirect damage to thyroid follicles

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the histological presence of 'germinal centers' in Hashimoto thyroiditis with their presence in Subacute Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent, well-developed lymphoid germinal centers
• Granulomatous: Absent; instead shows multinucleate giant cells and granulomas
• Reflects autoimmune vs. viral-triggered inflammatory pathways

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the primary antibody-mediated mechanism suspected in thyroid cell injury during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC)
• Binding of antithyroglobulin or antithyroid peroxidase antibodies
• Followed by NK cell or macrophage-mediated destruction

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Follicular epithelial cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis undergo a metaplastic response to chronic injury, resulting in cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm called [___].
back:
• Hürthle cells (also known as oxyphil cells)
• These represent a characteristic metaplastic change
• They are typically seen in the background of a lymphocytic infiltrate

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 52-year-old female presents with a firm, painless goiter and gradual weight gain. Laboratory studies reveal elevated TSH and positive anti-thyroglobulin antibodies. Identify the underlying mechanism of injury.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis
• Breakdown of self-tolerance to thyroid autoantigens
• Progressive autoimmune destruction of thyroid parenchyma
• Leads to gradual thyroid failure and hypothyroidism

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells in the progression of follicle depletion during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• They serve as major immune effectors
• Mediate direct killing of thyroid follicular cells
• Recognize antigens on the thyroid cell surface
• Contribute to the characteristic parenchymal loss

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A middle-aged woman presents with a hard thyroid mass. Contrast the extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis with that of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is limited to the gland and does not extend beyond the capsule
• Riedel: Extensive fibrosis involves the thyroid and contiguous neck structures, mimicking carcinoma

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Name the three primary immune-regulation genes whose polymorphisms are most strongly associated with a genetic susceptibility to Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4)
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22)
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain)

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Chronic autoimmune thyroiditis significantly predisposes patients to the development of a specific hematologic malignancy known as [___].
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALT lymphoma)
• Arises within the thyroid gland itself
• Results from long-standing chronic inflammatory stimulation

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with newly diagnosed Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with a period of anxiety and tachycardia. Labs show low TSH and high Free T4. This transient hyperthyroid phase is caused by [___].
back:
• Hashitoxicosis
• Caused by physical disruption of thyroid follicles
• Results in the acute release of preformed thyroid hormones into the circulation

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the mechanism by which CD4+ Th1 cells facilitate thyrocyte injury in an autoimmune environment.
back:
• They secrete inflammatory cytokines, primarily interferon-gamma
• Recruits and activates macrophages in the thyroid parenchyma
• Macrophages release factors that cause bystander damage to follicles

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the diagnostic radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan results typically seen in Graves disease versus Hashimoto thyroiditis during its hyperthyroid phase.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased uptake throughout the gland
• Hashimoto (Hashitoxicosis): Decreased uptake due to follicle damage rather than hyperfunction

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the hallmark histological feature characterized by mononuclear aggregates and pale centers commonly found in the thyroid stroma of Hashimoto patients.
back:
• Lymphocytic infiltrates with well-developed germinal centers
• Resembles reactive lymph node architecture
• Distinguishes it from subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis where germinal centers are not prominent

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, follicular epithelial cells often undergo a metaplastic response to chronic injury, transforming into [___], which are distinguished by their abundant, granular, and intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm.
back:
* Hürthle cells (also known as oxyphil cells)
* These cells contain a high density of mitochondria
* They are a hallmark histologic feature but are not pathognomonic as they appear in other thyroid lesions.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 52-year-old female presents with a painless, firm goiter and symptoms of lethargy and cold intolerance. Histology reveals a dense mononuclear infiltrate with well-developed germinal centers. Identify the underlying diagnosis.
back:
* Hashimoto Thyroiditis
* It is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions
* Characterized by autoimmune-mediated destruction of the thyroid gland leading to progressive organ failure.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells and Th1-derived cytokines in the progressive destruction of the thyroid gland in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* CD8+ cytotoxic T cells directly kill thyroid follicular cells
* Th1 cells secrete interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), which activates macrophages
* These activated macrophages release inflammatory cytokines that induce thyrocyte injury and follicle collapse.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the extent and anatomic boundaries of fibrosis seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis with those characteristic of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
* Hashimoto: Interstitial fibrosis may be abundant but is strictly confined within the thyroid capsule.
* Riedel: Fibrosis is extensive and penetrates the capsule to involve adjacent neck structures, mimicking malignancy.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the shared genetic susceptibility locus between Hashimoto thyroiditis and type 1 diabetes that encodes a negative regulator of T-cell activation, which is a target for specific immunotherapies.
back:
* CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4)
* Other non-HLA associations include PTPN22 and IL2RA
* These polymorphisms contribute to a general breakdown in immune tolerance across multiple endocrine tissues.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The early, transient hyperthyroid state in Hashimoto thyroiditis, resulting from the inflammatory disruption of follicles and the subsequent leakage of preformed hormones into the circulation, is known as [___].
back:
* Hashitoxicosis
* Clinically mimics hyperthyroidism with elevated free T4 and suppressed TSH
* Distinguished from Graves disease by a low radioactive iodine uptake scan due to follicular injury.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with long-standing Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass and stable TSH levels. Specify the malignancy this patient is at a significantly higher risk of developing.
back:
* Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALT lymphoma)
* Arises due to chronic lymphocytic stimulation within the thyroid
* Requires careful differentiation from the aggressive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the immunologic mechanism of Antibody-Dependent Cell-Mediated Cytotoxicity (ADCC) as it contributes to the pathogenesis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Antithyroid antibodies (anti-TPO and anti-TG) bind to thyrocyte antigens
* Natural Killer (NK) cells recognize these antibodies via Fc receptors
* NK cells then execute targeted lysis of the antibody-coated follicular epithelial cells.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the metabolic feedback loop status during the 'Hashitoxicosis' phase versus the late, chronic phase of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
* Hashitoxicosis: Hormone leakage suppresses TSH via negative feedback, simulating hyperthyroidism.
* Late Phase: Permanent follicle destruction reduces T3/T4 synthesis, triggering a compensatory rise in serum TSH due to lost feedback inhibition.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the most common cause of primary hypothyroidism in geographic regions where dietary iodine intake is considered sufficient.
back:
* Hashimoto Thyroiditis (Struma Lymphomatosa)
* It shows a strong female predominance (up to 20:1)
* Peak incidence occurs in women between 45 and 65 years of age.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The two most prevalent circulating autoantibodies detected in Hashimoto thyroiditis are directed against thyroglobulin and [___].
back:
• Thyroid peroxidase (TPO).
• Indicates a breakdown in self-tolerance to thyrocyte antigens.
• Frequently used as a diagnostic serum marker for autoimmune thyroid failure.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 52-year-old female presents with a painless, enlarged thyroid and fatigue. A biopsy reveals lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and epithelial cells possessing granular, intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis.
• The eosinophilic cells are Hürthle (oxyphil) cells.
• These represent a metaplastic response of follicular cells to chronic autoimmune injury.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD8+ T cells in the tissue destruction characteristic of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CD8+ cytotoxic T cells recognize self-antigens on follicular cells.
• They induce direct thyrocyte death via perforin-granzyme pathways.
• This contributes to the progressive depletion of thyroid parenchyma.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the histological presence of Hürthle cells and fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis: Displays prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and variable interstitial fibrosis.
• Subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis: Typically lacks both Hürthle cell change and significant fibrosis.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the clinical phenomenon of 'hashitoxicosis' occurring during the early stages of the disease.
back:
• A transient state of hyperthyroidism.
• Caused by the inflammatory disruption of thyroid follicles.
• Results in the sudden systemic release of preformed T3 and T4 hormones.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Genetic susceptibility to Hashimoto thyroiditis is linked to polymorphisms in the [___] gene, which encodes a protein that inhibits T-cell activation.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T Lymphocyte-Associated Antigen-4).
• Also associated with other autoimmune conditions like Type 1 Diabetes.
• Impacts the regulation of peripheral T-cell tolerance.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 60-year-old woman with chronic Hashimoto thyroiditis develops a rapidly enlarging, firm neck mass. Imaging confirms it arises from the thyroid. What specific hematopoietic malignancy is this patient at increased risk for?
back:
• Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma.
• Arises within the chronic inflammatory milieu of the gland.
• Must be distinguished from the typical painless goiter of thyroiditis.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe how the Th1 cytokine Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) contributes to follicular injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Secreted by activated CD4+ Th1 cells.
• Promotes the recruitment and activation of macrophages.
• Macrophages then release pro-inflammatory cytokines that directly damage thyroid follicles.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis with that seen in Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is limited to the thyroid gland and does not cross the capsule.
• Riedel: Features dense, woody fibrosis that extends beyond the capsule into adjacent neck structures.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: List the three classic histological hallmarks seen in a thyroidectomy specimen from a patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Dense mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate (lymphocytes and plasma cells).
• Well-developed lymphoid germinal centers.
• Atrophic follicles lined by metaplastic eosinophilic Hürthle cells.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: In Hashimoto thyroiditis, the metaplastic response of follicular cells to chronic autoimmune injury results in the formation of [___].
back: * H'ürthle (oxyphil) cells. * These are epithelial cells with abundant eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. * They represent a transformation of low cuboidal follicular cells into a more metabolically active, granular state.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless goiter and gradual weight gain. A biopsy reveals lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and metaplastic oxyphil cells. This patient is at significantly increased risk for [___].
back: * B-cell lymphoma. * Specifically, extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. * Chronic autoimmune stimulation within the thyroid gland is the primary predisposing factor for this malignancy.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD4+ Th1 cells in the immune-mediated destruction of thyroid parenchyma during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * Th1 cells secrete inflammatory cytokines, particularly interferon-gamma (IFN-̳). * This recruits and activates macrophages within the gland. * Activated macrophages cause direct damage to thyroid follicles, leading to progressive parenchymal loss.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the microscopic appearance of thyroid follicles in Hashimoto thyroiditis with those found in Graves disease.
back: * Hashimoto: Atrophic follicles lined by H'ürthle cells with dense lymphocytic infiltrates. * Graves: Hyperplastic follicles with tall, crowded columnar epithelium, scalloped colloid, and small papillae lacking fibrovascular cores.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the three primary immune-regulation gene polymorphisms associated with increased susceptibility to Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * CTLA4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte–associated antigen-4). * PTPN22 (protein tyrosine phosphatase-22). * IL2RA (interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain). * These genetic loci are shared with other autoimmune diseases like Type 1 Diabetes.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The initial, transient hyperthyroid state occasionally seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis, caused by the physical disruption of thyroid follicles, is termed [___].
back: * Hashitoxicosis. * Involves the acute release of preformed T3 and T4 into the systemic circulation. * Clinically mimics hyperthyroidism with elevated free T4 and low TSH levels.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A middle-aged woman presents with thyroid enlargement and fatigue. FNA reveals H'ürthle cells and a heterogeneous population of lymphocytes. These findings are most consistent with [___].
back: * Hashimoto thyroiditis. * Also known as struma lymphomatosa. * The combination of oxyphil metaplasia and chronic inflammatory infiltrates are hallmark diagnostic features in cytological samples.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the mechanism of antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) as it relates to thyrocyte injury in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * Antithyroid antibodies (peroxidase or thyroglobulin) bind to the thyroid cell surface. * Natural Killer (NK) cells bind to these antibodies via Fc receptors. * Triggers NK cell-mediated lysis of the targeted thyroid epithelial cells.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Distinguish the pattern of thyroid fibrosis in "classic" Hashimoto thyroiditis from the fibrosis characteristic of Riedel thyroiditis.
back: * Hashimoto: Fibrosis is interstitial but stays confined within the intact capsule of the gland. * Riedel: Dense, extensive fibrosis penetrates the capsule and invades contiguous neck structures.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Name the specific mononuclear inflammatory cell types and structures that characteristically replace normal thyroid parenchyma in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: * Small lymphocytes and plasma cells. * Well-developed lymphoid germinal centers. * This infiltrate leads to progressive follicular atrophy and extensive destruction of the functional thyroid units.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous thyroiditis is classically triggered by a [___], often following a history of an upper respiratory infection.
back:
• Viral infection (e.g., mumps, coxsackievirus, adenovirus).
• Occurs seasonally with a peak in summer.
• Self-limited process that typically resolves in 6 to 8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical presentation of de Quervain thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with an exquisitely tender neck mass and pain radiating to the jaw following a sore throat. Lab tests reveal elevated T3/T4 and suppressed TSH. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Most common cause of thyroid pain.
• Characterized by transient hyperthyroidism followed by recovery.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the immune-mediated mechanism responsible for the parenchymal destruction in de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Virus-induced tissue damage exposes thyroid antigens.
• Stimulates a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response.
• Damages thyroid follicles until the viral stimulus is cleared (non-self-perpetuating).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings in Granulomatous Thyroiditis with those of Graves Disease during the thyrotoxic phase.
back:
• Granulomatous: Low/diminished uptake due to follicle destruction and leakage.
• Graves Disease: High/diffusely increased uptake due to hyperfunctioning TSH receptors stimulating synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the pathognomonic histologic feature observed during the peak inflammatory stage of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid.
• Aggregates of lymphocytes, macrophages, and plasma cells.
• Patchy disruption or collapse of thyroid follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The initial histologic phase of granulomatous thyroiditis is uniquely characterized by the formation of [___] before the appearance of giant cells.
back:
• Neutrophilic microabscesses.
• Involves early follicle disruption and neutrophilic infiltration.
• Eventually replaced by granulomatous inflammation and chronic inflammatory cells.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient with painful thyroiditis exhibits a sequence of hyperthyroidism, followed by a brief hypothyroid state, and final restoration of euthyroidism. Apply this clinical progression to the likely underlying pathology.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Initial phase: Leakage of preformed hormones (T3/T4).
• Secondary phase: Temporary hormone depletion.
• Final phase: Follicular regeneration and recovery.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe why thyrotoxicosis in Granulomatous Thyroiditis is considered 'not associated with hyperthyroidism' strictly defined.
back:
• It results from the release of preformed hormone due to physical damage.
• True hyperthyroidism requires hyperfunction (increased synthesis) of the gland.
• The gland is actually inflamed and damaged, not hyperactive.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Differential of Autoimmune vs. Subacute Thyroiditis
front: Distinguish between Granulomatous Thyroiditis and Hashimoto Thyroiditis based on pain and risk of permanent thyroid failure.
back:
• Granulomatous: Exquisitely painful; low risk of permanent hypothyroidism.
• Hashimoto: Painless; high risk of gradual, permanent thyroid failure (autoimmune destruction).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Gross Morphology of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: Identify the characteristic macroscopic gross features of the thyroid gland in a patient with de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Firm, yellow-white areas of involvement.
• Intact capsule (rarely adheres to surrounding neck structures).
• Unilateral or bilateral enlargement that is often patchy.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis is clinically distinguished from other inflammatory thyroid conditions by being preceded by a history of [___].
back:
• Viral upper respiratory infection.
• Common triggers include coxsackievirus, mumps, or adenovirus.
• It typically presents with a seasonal peak during the summer.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Diagnostic Lab Contrast in De Quervain
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a tender, enlarged thyroid and symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. Lab tests reveal elevated T4/T3 and suppressed TSH, but a radioactive iodine scan shows significantly decreased uptake. Identify the underlying pathology.
back:
• Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Hyperthyroidism is transient and results from the release of preformed hormones from damaged follicles rather than increased synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of multinucleate giant cells in the histological progression of De Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• They aggregate around damaged follicles.
• Their primary role is to enclose and respond to pools of released colloid.
• This creates the characteristic granulomatous inflammatory pattern following the early neutophilic phase.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the typical findings of radioactive iodine uptake in Granulomatous thyroiditis versus Graves disease.
back:
• Granulomatous thyroiditis: Low/decreased uptake due to follicle destruction and leakage.
• Graves disease: Diffusely increased uptake due to autoantibodies stimulating the TSH receptor and hormone synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary clinical reason that Granulomatous thyroiditis is considered a self-limited condition.
back:
• The immune response is virus-initiated rather than a self-perpetuating autoimmune breakdown.
• Most patients experience spontaneous recovery and return to a euthyroid state within 6–8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: During the early active phase of granulomatous thyroiditis, the thyroid parenchyma is frequently infiltrated by [___] forming microabscesses.
back:
• Neutrophils.
• These are later replaced by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages as the granulomatous reaction develops.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient with a history of recent upper respiratory infection presents with severe neck pain and transient hyperthyroidism. If this condition is De Quervain thyroiditis, describe the expected outcome for the thyroid function after two months.
back:
• Complete spontaneous recovery.
• Normal thyroid function (euthyroid state) generally returns after the 6–8 week limited inflammatory course concludes.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the pathogenesis through which a viral trigger causes thyroid follicle destruction in subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Virus-induced tissue damage releases thyroid antigens.
• This stimulates a host cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response.
• The T-cells target and injure the thyroid follicular epithelial cells.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Distinguish between Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis and Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding clinical pain and associated gender ratio.
back:
• De Quervain: Very painful/tender thyroid; 4:1 female predominance.
• Hashimoto: Painless thyroid enlargement; 10:1 to 20:1 female predominance.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Name the most common clinical cause of thyroid pain.
back:
• Granulomatous (De Quervain) thyroiditis.
• It is distinguished from the rare Riedel thyroiditis or localized infections by its subacute, self-limiting nature.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous thyroiditis is classically triggered by a preceding [___] infection, with clinical cases often peaking during the summer months.
back:
• Upper respiratory tract (viral)
• Linked to mumps, coxsackievirus, and adenovirus
• Pathogenesis involves virus-induced tissue injury exposing thyroid antigens.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with sudden onset of severe anterior neck pain radiating to the jaw, accompanied by fever and palpitations. Lab results show elevated free T4 and suppressed TSH. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• Pain is the clinical hallmark
• Hyperthyroidism is transient due to hormone release from damaged follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the mechanism leading to the transient thyrotoxic phase in Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
back:
• Virus-induced inflammation causes follicular cell damage
• Preformed thyroid hormones leak into the systemic circulation
• Not caused by glandular hyperfunction or new hormone synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) and clinical features of Graves disease with Granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Painless enlargement; diffusely increased RAIU (hyperfunction)
• Granulomatous: Exquisitely painful gland; markedly decreased RAIU (inflammation and follicle leakage).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the histological hallmark seen during the mature inflammatory phase of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid
• Patchy follicular disruption and collapse
• Aggregates of lymphocytes, macrophages, and plasma cells.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: In the early active phase of granulomatous thyroiditis, the thyroid parenchyma may show disruption of follicles and replacement by [___] forming microabscesses.
back:
• Neutrophils
• This acute inflammatory phase is transient
• Followed later by characteristic granulomatous and lymphocytic infiltrates.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient recovering from a painful goiter now shows low T4 and high TSH levels 8 weeks after initial symptoms. Explain the clinical progression of this thyroiditis.
back:
• Initial hyperthyroid phase (hormone leak)
• Subsequent transient hypothyroid phase (hormone depletion)
• Typical progression to a euthyroid state within 6-8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the immune-mediated pathophysiology that drives thyroid follicle destruction in Granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Virus-induced damage exposes host thyroid antigens
• Stimulates a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CD8+) response against thyrocytes
• Destruction is limited and not self-perpetuating.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the pain profile and inflammatory markers (ESR) in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Painless, diffuse goiter; normal ESR/CRP
• Granulomatous: Exquisitely painful thyroid; markedly elevated ESR and CRP (acute phase reactants).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: List the typical laboratory profile expected during the acute phase of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• High Serum T3/T4 and suppressed TSH
• Markedly elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
• Markedly low radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU).

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The follicular epithelial cells in Hashimoto thyroiditis that undergo a metaplastic response to chronic injury and develop abundant, granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm are known as [___].
back: - Hürthle (oxyphil) cells. - Represent a metaplastic response to chronic follicular injury. - Characterized by an accumulation of mitochondria within the cytoplasm.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 55-year-old female presents with fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. Physical exam reveals a firm, painless, symmetrically enlarged thyroid. Serum anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are present. State the most likely diagnosis.
back: - Hashimoto thyroiditis. - Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions. - Characterized by a 10:1 to 20:1 female predominance.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD4+ Th1 cells in the destruction of thyroid follicular cells during Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: - Activated Th1 cells secrete proinflammatory cytokines (e.g., IFN-gamma). - Cytokines recruit and activate macrophages in the interstitium. - Activated macrophages cause direct follicular damage and thyrocyte death.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the anatomic extent of fibrosis in 'classic' Hashimoto thyroiditis with that seen in Riedel thyroiditis.
back: - Hashimoto: Fibrosis is variable but strictly confined to the gland and does not cross the capsule. - Riedel: Extensive fibrosis involves the thyroid and penetrates into adjacent neck structures.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Identify the primary hematopoietic malignancy for which patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis carry a significantly increased risk.
back: - Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. - Also known as MALT lymphoma. - Arises within the thyroid parenchyma secondary to chronic lymphoid stimulation.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
coreConcept: Microscopic Hallmarks of Chronic Autoimmune Thyroiditis
front: The diagnostic hallmark of Hashimoto thyroiditis in histological sections is an extensive infiltration of the thyroid parenchyma by a [___] inflammatory infiltrate.
back: - Mononuclear (lymphoplasmacytic). - Typically includes well-developed germinal centers. - Associated with the gradual depletion and atrophy of thyroid follicles.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with a transient period of elevated T3 and T4 levels and low TSH. Describe the pathophysiological event occurring.
back: - Hashitoxicosis. - Caused by the acute disruption of thyroid follicles. - Leads to the leakage of preformed thyroid hormones into the circulation.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Describe the mechanism of antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) in the pathogenesis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: - Binding of antithyroid antibodies (anti-TG or anti-TPO) to follicular cells. - Natural Killer (NK) cells bind the Fc portion of these antibodies. - Triggers NK cell-mediated lysis of the target thyrocytes.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan results in Hashitoxicosis with those typically seen in Graves disease.
back: - Hashitoxicosis: Characterized by decreased RAIU (leakage of preformed hormone). - Graves Disease: Characterized by diffusely increased RAIU (autonomous hyperfunction).

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
coreConcept: Genetic Susceptibility in Autoimmune Thyroid Disease
front: Name the three immune-regulatory gene loci most strongly linked to the breakdown of self-tolerance in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: - CTLA4 (cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4). - PTPN22 (protein tyrosine phosphatase-22). - IL2RA (interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous thyroiditis is classically preceded by a [___] infection, often occurring in a seasonal pattern peaking in summer.
back:
• Viral infection
• Common triggers: Coxsackievirus, mumps, measles, and adenovirus.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical presentation of De Quervain Thyroiditis
front: A 40-year-old female presents with severe neck pain radiating to the jaw and a tender, firm thyroid gland following a recent sore throat. Diagnosis?
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• It is the most common cause of thyroid pain.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Mechanisms of hormone release in Thyroiditis
front: Explain the mechanism behind transient thyrotoxicosis observed in the early phase of granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Viral-induced inflammation disrupts thyroid follicles.
• Leakage of preformed T3 and T4 into the blood.
• It is not due to hyperfunction or new synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) in a patient with Graves disease versus a patient in the thyrotoxic phase of De Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased uptake due to cell hyperfunction.
• De Quervain: Significantly decreased uptake due to follicular damage and TSH suppression.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Laboratory profile of acute Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: List the most common laboratory findings regarding thyroid hormones and TSH during the acute phase of granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Elevated free T4 and T3
• Depressed/Low TSH
• Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The diagnostic histologic hallmark of granulomatous thyroiditis is the presence of [___] enclosing pools of colloid.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells
• Forms a granulomatous reaction around collapsed follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient with painful thyroid enlargement currently shows elevated T4. Describe the expected natural progression of thyroid function if the condition remains untreated.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism (2–6 weeks)
• Transient hypothyroidism (due to depletion)
• Euthyroid recovery (within 6–8 weeks).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain why the thyroid gland in De Quervain thyroiditis may appear hard and fixed, clinically mimicking a malignancy.
back:
• Severe inflammatory response.
• Replacement of injured areas by dense fibrosis.
• Fibrosis may rarely extend to adjacent structures.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast granulomatous thyroiditis with subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis regarding their typical patient presentation.
back:
• Granulomatous: Painful, tender gland; viral origin.
• Lymphocytic: Painless, non-tender gland; autoimmune origin; often postpartum.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary cells found in the thyroid parenchyma during the earliest 'active' phase of granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Neutrophils
• They typically form microabscesses within the follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis is believed to be triggered by an antecedent [___] and is most common in women aged 40 to 50.
back:
* Viral infection (often upper respiratory).
* Associated with mumps, measles, or adenovirus.
* Demonstrates a seasonal peak in summer.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a sudden, exquisitely painful thyroid mass and fever. Labs reveal elevated T4, low TSH, and significantly decreased radioactive iodine uptake. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
* Granulomatous (De Quervain) Thyroiditis.
* Most common cause of thyroid pain.
* Low iodine uptake distinguishes this from Graves' disease.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of thyroid follicle disruption in the transient hyperthyroidism seen during the early phase of De Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
* Inflammation causes follicle rupture.
* Preformed thyroid hormones leak into the blood.
* Results in thyrotoxicosis without increased hormone synthesis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the histologic features of Granulomatous thyroiditis with Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding Hürthle cell change and the inflammatory infiltrate.
back:
* Granulomatous: Lacks Hürthle cell metaplasia; hallmark is multinucleated giant cells.
* Hashimoto: Features prominent eosinophilic Hürthle cells and lymphoid germinal centers.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary clinical management goal for the hyperthyroid phase of de Quervain thyroiditis compared to permanent hyperthyroid conditions.
back:
* Supportive care only (e.g., pain relief).
* Disease is self-limited.
* Most patients return to a euthyroid state within 6-8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The hallmark histologic feature of Granulomatous thyroiditis is the presence of [___] that enclose central pools of colloid.
back:
* Multinucleate giant cells.
* Formed as part of a granulomatous reaction.
* Response to released colloid from damaged follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient presents with thyrotoxic symptoms and a tender neck. If the ESR is high but the thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies are negative, which diagnosis is most likely?
back:
* Subacute Granulomatous (De Quervain) Thyroiditis.
* High ESR is a typical inflammatory marker.
* Absence of TPO antibodies helps exclude Hashimoto disease.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Discuss the sequence of the inflammatory response in Granulomatous thyroiditis, beginning with the early active phase.
back:
* Early: Neutrophil infiltration and microabscess formation.
* Late: Replacement by lymphocytes and activated macrophages.
* Final: Granulomas with giant cells and focal fibrosis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast Riedel thyroiditis with De Quervain thyroiditis based on the physical examination of the neck and the extent of fibrosis.
back:
* Riedel: Hard, fixed mass simulating cancer; fibrosis extends beyond the capsule.
* De Quervain: Tender mass; fibrosis is localized to the gland.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the characteristic gross appearance of the thyroid gland in a patient with subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
* Unilateral or bilateral enlargement.
* Gland is firm with an intact capsule.
* Cut section shows yellow-white, firm areas.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The pathognomonic microscopic feature of de Quervain thyroiditis consists of [___] enclosing disrupted pools of colloid.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells
  • These surround granulomatous aggregates of lymphocytes and macrophages
  • Represents the response to escaped thyroglobulin

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with a sudden onset of severe anterior neck pain radiating to the jaw and a fever following a viral respiratory illness. Examination shows a tender, firm thyroid. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
  • It is the most common cause of thyroid pain
  • Typically affects women aged 40 to 50 years

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain why radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) is low during the thyrotoxic phase of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism results from leakage of preformed hormones from damaged follicles
  • Not due to increased synthesis
  • Inflammation suppresses follicular function and iodine trapping

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the inflammatory triggers and clinical course of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those of granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Trigger: Hashimoto is autoimmune/self-perpetuating; Granulomatous is post-viral/self-limited
  • Pain: Hashimoto is painless; Granulomatous is characteristically tender
  • Outcome: Hashimoto leads to permanent failure; Granulomatous usually recovers to normal

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary pathogenesis and seasonal pattern associated with de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Pathogenesis: Virus-initiated cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response to altered thyroid antigens
  • Common Viruses: Mumps, coxsackievirus, adenovirus
  • Pattern: Seasonal peak in summer

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: During the early active phase of granulomatous thyroiditis, follicles are frequently replaced by [___].
back:
• Neutrophils forming microabscesses
  • This is later followed by the characteristic granulomatous inflammation

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient with suspected de Quervain thyroiditis has elevated T3/T4 and suppressed TSH. If a TRH stimulation test is performed, describe the expected response.
back:
• No significant rise in TSH levels
  • High levels of circulating preformed thyroid hormones maintain negative feedback on the pituitary

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: How does the thyroid hyperfunction in Graves disease differ physiologically from the thyrotoxicosis seen in granulomatous thyroiditis?
back:
• Graves: Increased hormone synthesis via TSH-receptor autoantibodies
  • Thyroiditis: Destruction of follicles with massive release of preformed T3/T4
  • Scintigraphy: Graves shows diffuse high uptake; Thyroiditis shows low uptake

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the typical duration and phases of the clinical course in a patient with granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Hyperthyroid phase: Lasts 2–6 weeks due to follicle disruption
  • Recovery phase: Occurs over 6–8 weeks
  • End result: Most patients return to a normal euthyroid state

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: List the most common systemic symptoms that accompany the thyroid tenderness in subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Fever and malaise
  • Fatigue
  • Transient signs of thyrotoxicosis (tremor, palpitations, weight loss)

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis is believed to be triggered by a [___], often occurring after an upper respiratory infection.
back:
• Viral infection
