• Common agents include Coxsackievirus, mumps, measles, and adenovirus
• Characterized by a seasonal incidence, peaking in the summer months.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with acute neck pain, fever, and mild symptoms of hyperthyroidism. A radioiodine scan shows significantly decreased uptake. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• It is the most common cause of thyroid pain
• Thyrotoxicosis results from follicle disruption and hormone leakage, not hyperfunction.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the role of the host immune response in the destruction of follicular cells during De Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Viral infection causes host tissue damage
• Damage stimulates a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response
• T-cells target thyroid antigens, causing patchy follicle destruction
• Process is self-limited and not self-perpetuating.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the histologic findings of Granulomatous thyroiditis with those of Hashimoto thyroiditis regarding Hürthle cells and inflammatory cell types.
back:
• Granulomatous: Multinucleate giant cells enclosing colloid; lacks Hürthle cells.
• Hashimoto: Prominent eosinophilic Hürthle cell metaplasia; dense lymphocytic infiltrates with germinal centers; lacks giant cells.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the radioactive iodine uptake pattern in De Quervain thyroiditis during the initial hyperthyroid phase and identify the reason for this finding.
back:
• Diminished (low) radioactive iodine uptake
• Hyperthyroidism is caused by the release of preformed T3/T4 from ruptured follicles, which suppresses TSH and prevents new iodine uptake.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The hallmark histologic feature of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis is the presence of [___] enclosing fragmented pools of colloid.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells
• Histology also shows patchy infiltration by activated macrophages, lymphocytes, and plasma cells
• Early stages may show microabscesses formed by neutrophils.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient recovering from a summer upper respiratory infection develops a tender, enlarged thyroid. Lab tests show elevated free T4 and low TSH. The condition resolves without treatment in 8 weeks. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• Characteristically demonstrates a self-limited clinical course
• Most patients return to a euthyroid state within 6 to 8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain why the hyperthyroidism seen in Granulomatous thyroiditis is typically transient rather than a permanent state of hyperfunction.
back:
• Not caused by increased hormone synthesis
• Results from sudden rupture of follicles by inflammation
• Once preformed hormone is depleted and inflammation subsides, the gland repairs itself.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Differentiate between Subacute Lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis and Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis based on clinical symptoms and etiology.
back:
• Granulomatous: Marked by severe thyroid pain/tenderness; viral-triggered.
• Painless: Non-tender gland; usually autoimmune (anti-TPO antibodies present)
• Both show transient hyperthyroidism with low iodine uptake.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: List the classic gross morphologic findings of a thyroid gland affected by De Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Unilateral or bilateral enlargement
• Firm, intact capsule
• Cut surface reveals firm, yellow-white areas that stand out from normal brown parenchyma.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous thyroiditis is most commonly triggered by a preceding [___] infection.
back:
• Viral (upper respiratory) infection.
• Often follows a seasonal pattern (summer peaks).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with fever and an exquisitely tender thyroid gland that developed two weeks after a flu-like illness. Lab tests reveal elevated T4 and suppressed TSH. State the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
• Characterized by painful thyroid enlargement and transient hyperthyroidism.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain why radioactive iodine uptake is diminished in de Quervain thyroiditis despite the patient being in a thyrotoxic state.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism is caused by the leakage of preformed hormones from ruptured follicles, not overproduction.
• Damaged follicular cells are unable to actively trap iodine during the inflammatory phase.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A 42-year-old patient has a firm, painful neck mass and tachycardia. Contrast the expected thyroid scintigraphy results if the cause is a toxic adenoma versus granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Toxic Adenoma: Increased uptake localized to a single “hot” nodule.
• Granulomatous Thyroiditis: Diffusely diminished or low iodine uptake across the gland.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Identify the primary reason for avoiding antithyroid thionamide therapy (e.g., methimazole) during the hyperthyroid phase of de Quervain thyroiditis.
back:
• Thionamides only inhibit the synthesis of new hormones.
• Thyrotoxicosis in this condition is due to the release of preformed hormone stores from damaged follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: On microscopic examination of de Quervain thyroiditis, the pathognomonic feature consists of [___] enclosing pools of colloid.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells.
• These form a granulomatous reaction around extracellular colloid.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient presents with acute thyroid pain and transient hyperthyroidism. If the clinical course is typical for granulomatous thyroiditis, describe the expected outcome regarding thyroid function after 8 weeks.
back:
• Complete recovery to a euthyroid state.
• The process is self-limited and the immune response is not self-perpetuating.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the mechanism distinguishing the pathogenesis of de Quervain thyroiditis from Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• De Quervain: Triggered by viral infection; causes transient, virus-induced tissue damage and a limited T-cell response.
• Hashimoto: Chronic autoimmune breakdown in self-tolerance; causes progressive, permanent follicular destruction.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the early active phase morphology of granulomatous thyroiditis with the later diagnostic stage.
back:
• Early: Neutrophilic infiltration and microabscess formation.
• Later: Granulomatous aggregates of lymphocytes, activated macrophages, and giant cells.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Characterize the most common clinical palpation finding and typical demographic for granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Exquisitely painful, firm thyroid enlargement.
• Most common in women (4:1 ratio) aged 40 to 50 years.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis is most commonly triggered by a [___] infection, often occurring seasonally in the summer months.
back:
• Viral (e.g., mumps, coxsackievirus, adenovirus)
• Suggested mechanism involves host tissue damage inciting a T-lymphocyte response
• Preceded by an upper respiratory illness.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A 45-year-old female presents with acute anterior neck pain, fever, and transient palpitations following a summer cold. Lab tests show elevated free T4 and suppressed TSH. Describe the underlying pathology driving this thyrotoxicosis.
back:
• Follicular disruption
• Release of preformed thyroid hormones (leakage)
• Not caused by increased hormone synthesis or hyperfunction.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the diagnostic finding on radioactive iodine uptake scintigraphy that distinguishes Granulomatous thyroiditis from Graves disease.
back:
• Granulomatous: Diminished radioactive iodine uptake
• Graves: Diffusely increased radioactive iodine uptake
• Low uptake in thyroiditis occurs despite elevated serum T3/T4 levels.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the histologic hallmarks of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those of Granulomatous thyroiditis regarding follicles and cell types.
back:
• Hashimoto: Germinal centers, Hürthle cell metaplasia, and diffuse lymphocytic infiltrates
• Granulomatous: Multinucleate giant cells enclosing fragmented colloid pools and neutrophilic microabscesses (early).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: State the standard diagnostic step used to differentiate painful de Quervain thyroiditis from hyperfunctioning 'toxic' nodules in a patient with neck discomfort.
back:
• Radionuclide scanning
• de Quervain: Patchy or globally 'cold' (diminished uptake)
• Toxic nodules: Focal 'hot' areas (localized increased uptake).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: In the early, active inflammatory phase of de Quervain thyroiditis, the classic microscopic feature is follicle disruption accompanied by [___].
back:
• Neutrophils forming microabscesses
• Followed by lymphocytic/macrophage aggregates
• Culminates in multinucleate giant cell formation.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient diagnosed with de Quervain thyroiditis currently exhibits high T4 and suppressed TSH. Predict the likely thyroid function and TSH status of this patient in 8 weeks.
back:
• Spontaneous recovery to euthyroid state
• Normal TSH and T4 levels expected
• Self-limited course (typically 6–8 weeks).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the immune mechanism of follicular destruction in Granulomatous thyroiditis with that of Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Granulomatous: Limited virus-initiated cytotoxic T-cell response
• Riedel: Extensive IgG4-related systemic fibrosis involving the thyroid and adjacent neck structures.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Differentiate the metabolic feedback loop response during the hyperthyroid phase of de Quervain thyroiditis from that of a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
back:
• de Quervain: Low TSH due to negative feedback from leaked T3/T4 (primary)
• TSH Adenoma: High TSH causing secondary hormone elevation (loss of inhibition).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Gross Pathology of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: Identify the characteristic gross morphologic appearance of the involved parenchymal areas in a gland affected by subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Firm, yellow-white areas
• Stands out from normal rubbery, brown thyroid tissue
• Gland may be unilaterally or bilaterally enlarged.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: The development of granulomatous thyroiditis is classically associated with a preceding history of [___], indicating a viral trigger.
back:
• Upper respiratory infection (URI)
• Associated with viral agents like mumps, measles, or adenovirus
• Often seasonal, peaking in summer months.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: A 42-year-old woman presents with severe neck pain radiating to the jaw, a low-grade fever, and a firm, tender thyroid. She reports having a flu-like illness three weeks ago. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
• Most common cause of thyroid pain
• Characterized by a painful, enlarged gland.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Explain the immunopathogenesis of Granulomatous Thyroiditis following a viral infection.
back:
• Virus-induced host tissue damage releases thyroid antigens
• Stimulates a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response
• Results in follicular cell injury rather than a self-perpetuating autoimmune process.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings during the thyrotoxic phase of Granulomatous Thyroiditis with those of Graves disease.
back:
• Granulomatous: Decreased uptake (due to follicular cell damage/hormone leak)
• Graves Disease: Diffusely increased uptake (due to autonomous hyperfunction).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
coreConcept: Histological Hallmark of de Quervain Thyroiditis
front: Identify the specific microscopic feature involving follicular colloid that is diagnostic for Granulomatous Thyroiditis.
back:
• Multinucleate giant cells enclosing pools of colloid
• Forms the hallmark granulomatous reaction
• Associated with collapsed and damaged follicles.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: In the natural history of Granulomatous Thyroiditis, the initial thyrotoxic phase is typically followed by a transient period of [___].
back:
• Hypothyroidism
• Caused by depletion of preformed hormone reserves
• Usually followed by recovery to a euthyroid state in 6–8 weeks.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: A patient with a painful thyroid nodule has high serum T4, low TSH, and extremely low iodine-131 uptake. Explain why the iodine uptake is low despite symptoms of thyrotoxicosis.
back:
• Thyrotoxicosis results from the release of preformed hormone (leakage)
• Damaged follicular cells are unable to trap new iodine
• Gland is not hyperfunctioning (hyperthyroidism).

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Describe the evolution of histologic findings in de Quervain thyroiditis from the early active phase to the late recovery phase.
back:
• Early: Neutrophilic microabscesses and follicular disruption
• Active: Lymphocytes, macrophages, and giant cell granulomas
• Late: Chronic inflammation and focal fibrosis.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: Contrast the microscopic features of Hashimoto thyroiditis with those of Granulomatous Thyroiditis regarding cellular metaplasia and inflammatory patterns.
back:
• Hashimoto: Germinal centers and Hürthle cell metaplasia predominate
• Granulomatous: Multinucleate giant cells and granulomas predominate; Hürthle cells are typically absent.

category: Granulomatous Thyroiditis
front: State the standard prognosis for Granulomatous Thyroiditis and the timeframe for return of normal thyroid function.
back:
• Prognosis: Self-limited and excellent
• Normal function returns: Usually within 6 to 8 weeks
• Most patients regain full thyroid function.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In the pathogenesis of Graves' disease, the primary autoantibody responsible for mimicking the physiological action of TSH is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• Binds and activates TSH receptors on follicular cells.
• Induces cAMP-mediated synthesis and release of T3 and T4.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and proptosis. Examination reveals scaly thickening over the shins. Identify the clinical triad and its underlying immunologic cause.
back:
• Diagnosis: Graves' Disease.
• Triad: Hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter), Ophthalmopathy, and Dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).
• Cause: Type II Hypersensitivity (Autoimmune).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of CD4+ T-cells and cytokines in the development of infiltrative ophthalmopathy in Graves' disease.
back:
• T-cells secrete cytokines (e.g., IFN-γ).
• Stimulate fibroblasts to produce hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid).
• Leads to osmotic swelling of extraocular muscles and retro-orbital edema.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic appearance of the small papillae seen in Graves' disease with the papillae found in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Graves: Simple papillae lacking fibrovascular cores.
• Papillary CA: Complex branching papillae with dense fibrovascular cores.
• Nuclei: Graves lacks the 'Orphan Annie eye' nuclei characteristic of Carcinoma.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Name the specific gene polymorphisms that contribute to the breakdown of self-tolerance in individuals susceptible to Graves' disease.
back:
• CTLA-4 and PTPN22 (immune regulation genes).
• HLA-DR3 haplotype.
• TSH receptor (TSHR) gene locus variants.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Histologically, the thyroid in Graves' disease shows follicular cells that actively resorb colloid for hormone synthesis, resulting in a characteristic [___] appearance at the follicle margins.
back:
• Scalloped (or 'moth-eaten') colloid.
• Lined by tall, crowded columnar epithelium.
• Reflects rapid turnover and hyperfunctioning state.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A thyrotoxic patient's radionuclide scan shows diffusely increased iodine uptake. Applying the pathogenesis of Graves' disease, why is the hyperactivity global rather than nodular?
back:
• TSI autoantibodies are systemic.
• They stimulate TSH receptors globally across all follicles.
• Leads to symmetric, diffuse follicular hyperplasia.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Define how the mechanism of hormone production in Graves' disease differs from standard Type II hypersensitivity reactions.
back:
• Standard Type II: Leads to cell death/lysis.
• Graves: Stimulatory Type II reaction.
• TSI mimics the ligand, bypassing the pituitary to cause autonomous cellular hyperfunction.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the typical thyroid stroma in Graves' disease with that seen in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Minimal fibrosis; lymphocytic infiltrates (T-cells/B-cells) with germinal centers common.
• Hashimoto's: Extensive fibrosis; Hürthle cell metaplasia; heavy mononuclear infiltrate destroys follicles.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the salient gross morphological features of the thyroid gland in an untreated patient with Graves' disease.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric enlargement (usually 80g+).
• Smooth, intact capsule.
• Beefy-red, 'meaty' parenchyma due to extreme hypervascularity.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In the pathogenesis of Graves disease, the primary autoantibody responsible for mimicking the action of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• It represents a Type II hypersensitivity reaction.
• TSI binds the TSH receptor, activating adenyl cyclase and increasing cAMP.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 35-year-old female presents with tachycardia, diffuse thyroid enlargement, and proptosis. Name the third pathognomonic clinical feature required to complete the classic triad of Graves Disease.
back:
• Localized infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).
• Characterized by scaly, non-pitting thickening of the skin overlying the shins.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of cytokines and fibroblasts in the development of Graves ophthalmopathy.
back:
• CD4+ T-cells release cytokines that stimulate retro-orbital fibroblasts.
• Fibroblasts produce hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (e.g., hyaluronic acid).
• Leads to edema, extraocular muscle swelling, and fatty infiltration.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake pattern of Graves disease with that seen in Subacute Granulomatous Thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves Disease: Diffusely increased uptake throughout the hyperactive gland.
• Granulomatous Thyroiditis: Markedly diminished uptake due to follicle disruption and release of preformed hormone.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the characteristic histological appearance of the colloid-epithelium interface in an untreated Graves thyroid.
back:
• "Scalloped" or moth-eaten margins of the colloid.
• Result of rapid, active resorption of thyroglobulin by hyperactive tall columnar cells.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Genetic susceptibility to Graves disease is strongly linked to polymorphisms in the [___] HLA haplotype and the CTLA4 gene.
back:
• HLA-DR3.
• Also associated with the PTPN22 gene, which regulates T-cell responses.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with exophthalmos has a suppressed TSH level. Explain why peripheral edema is absent in this patient despite significant skin thickening on the legs.
back:
• The dermopathy (pretibial myxedema) is caused by glycosaminoglycan deposition, not fluid imbalance.
• Unlike cardiac failure, this is a localized infiltrative process.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the physiological signal transduction cascade triggered when Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) binds to its target receptor.
back:
• TSI binds the G-protein coupled TSH receptor.
• Activates the Gsα subunit and Adenyl Cyclase.
• Increases intracellular cAMP, stimulating thyroid growth and T3/T4 release.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic effect of preoperative Iodine therapy versus Propylthiouracil (PTU) on the Graves gland.
back:
• Iodine: Induces involution, colloid accumulation, and decreased vascularity.
• PTU: Exaggerates epithelial hyperplasia by blocking T4 synthesis, leading to compensatory TSH-driven growth.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the type of epithelial cells lining the follicles in a hyperplastic Graves thyroid compared to a normal thyroid.
back:
• Graves: Tall, crowded columnar cells with small papillary projections.
• Normal: Low cuboidal to flat epithelial cells.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Grave’s disease is primarily characterized by the production of an autoantibody known as [___], which binds to and activates the TSH receptor.
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• Mimics TSH action by binding the TSH receptor
• Stimulates adenylyl cyclase to increase T3 and T4 release

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 32-year-old female presents with palpitations, weight loss, and proptosis. Physical exam reveals a firm, non-pitting thickening of the skin over her shins. Explain the pathogenesis of this cutaneous finding.
back:
• Known as pretibial myxedema (infiltrative dermopathy)
• T-cell cytokines stimulate fibroblasts
• Causes accumulation of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid)
• Results in dermal thickening and edema

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of T-cell-mediated cytokines in the development of Grave's ophthalmopathy.
back:
• CD4+ T-cells secrete cytokines (e.g., IFN-γ)
• Stimulate retro-orbital fibroblasts to synthesize glycosaminoglycans
• Leads to osmotic edema, fat accumulation, and muscle swelling
• Causes displacement of the eyeball (exophthalmos)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the intrafollicular papillae seen in Grave’s disease with those seen in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back:
• Grave’s: Small, crowded papillae lacking fibrovascular cores
• PTC: Branching papillae with dense fibrovascular stalks
• Grave’s lacks PTC nuclear features (Orphan Annie nuclei/pseudoinclusions)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
coreConcept: Genetic Predisposition to Autoimmune Thyroid Disease
front: Identify three specific genetic loci associated with an increased susceptibility to both Grave’s disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• HLA-DR3
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte–associated antigen-4)
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22)
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Upon gross inspection, the thyroid gland in Grave’s disease shows diffuse, symmetric enlargement and a soft, meaty appearance resembling [___].
back:
• Skeletal muscle
• Due to diffuse follicular hypertrophy and hyperplasia
• Typically accompanied by increased vascularity (audible bruits clinically)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with suspected hyperthyroidism undergoes a biopsy showing tall, columnar follicular cells and colloid with "scalloped" margins. Identify the specific cellular activity causing this scalloping.
back:
• Active resorption of colloid by hyperplastic follicular cells
• Driven by continuous TSI stimulation of TSH receptors
• Indicates high turnover of thyroglobulin into T3/T4

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the histological changes induced in a Grave’s disease thyroid following preoperative treatment with iodine.
back:
• Induces involution of hyperplastic follicular epithelium
• Promotes massive accumulation of colloid
• Blocks thyroglobulin secretion and decreases gland vascularity

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the "staring gaze" of general thyrotoxicosis with the infiltrative ophthalmopathy specific to Grave’s disease.
back:
• Staring gaze: Sympathetic overstimulation of Müller’s superior tarsal muscle
• Grave's Ophthalmopathy: True proptosis due to retro-orbital inflammation and GAG deposition
• Sympathetic gaze lag occurs in all thyrotoxic states; proptosis is Grave's-specific

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Enumerate the three classic clinical findings that constitute the triad of Grave’s Disease.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism with diffuse goiter
• Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos)
• Localized infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody responsible for the hyperthyroidism in Graves' disease, which mimics the action of TSH by binding to its receptor, is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• A subtype of IgG antibody
• Activates adenyl cyclase to increase synthesis and release of T3 and T4.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with heat intolerance, weight loss, and protruding eyeballs (proptosis). Lab tests show low TSH and high free T4. Identify the diagnosis and its clinical triad.
back:
• Graves' Disease
• Triad: Hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter), Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos), and Localized dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the biological mechanism responsible for the retro-orbital tissue expansion leading to exophthalmos in Graves' disease.
back:
• CD4+ T-cell infiltration and cytokine release
• Fibroblast stimulation leads to glycosaminoglycan (hyaluronic acid) deposition
• Results in osmotic edema and increased retro-orbital fat.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic features of the epithelial papillae seen in Graves' disease with those of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Graves' Disease: Small, crowded papillae lacking true fibrovascular cores.
• Papillary Carcinoma: Branching papillae with dense fibrovascular stalks and Orphan Annie eye nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: How does the administration of preoperative iodine affect the morphology of the thyroid gland in Graves' disease?
back:
• Induces involution of the hyperplastic epithelium
• Promotes colloid accumulation by blocking thyroglobulin secretion
• Reduces gland vascularity to facilitate surgery.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Graves' disease, the histological finding of follicular cells actively resorbing thyroglobulin leads to a characteristic [___] appearance of the colloid margins.
back:
• Scalloped (or moth-eaten)
• Caused by intense epithelial hyperactivity
• Tall columnar cells crowd the follicle lumen.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient presents with high T3/T4 and low TSH. Radioactive iodine scan shows a diffusely increased uptake. Contrast this with the uptake pattern expected in subacute thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves': Diffuse, uniform increase in iodine uptake.
• Subacute Thyroiditis: Decreased uptake due to follicle destruction and release of preformed hormone.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the pathogenesis of pretibial myxedema (dermopathy) in Graves' disease.
back:
• T-cell mediated autoimmune response
• Accumulation of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans in the dermis
• Leads to scaly thickening and induration of the overlying skin.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the gross appearance of the thyroid in Graves' disease with that of a typical Multinodular Goiter.
back:
• Graves': Diffuse, symmetric enlargement; beefy red, meaty parenchyma.
• Multinodular Goiter: Asymmetric enlargement; irregular nodules with gelatinous colloid and cystic changes.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List two non-MHC genetic polymorphisms associated with increased susceptibility to Graves' disease.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4)
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22)
• Both are involved in regulating T-cell inhibitory responses.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The most specific autoantibody subtype in Grave’s Disease that mimics the action of TSH and triggers continuous thyroid hormone release is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI).
• It binds to the TSH receptor on follicular epithelial cells, stimulating adenyl cyclase and increasing cAMP.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, weight loss despite increased appetite, and protruding eyeballs. Describe the likely gross morphology of the thyroid gland.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric hypertrophy and hyperplasia.
• Soft, meaty parenchyma resembling skeletal muscle.
• Intact capsule without significant nodularity.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of glycosaminoglycans in the development of Grave’s infiltrative ophthalmopathy.
back:
• Activated T-cells secrete cytokines that stimulate fibroblasts.
• Hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid) accumulate in the retro-orbital space.
• This causes osmotic edema and fatty infiltration, displacing the eyeball forward.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic papillae seen in Grave’s Disease with the papillae found in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Grave’s: Small papillae created by crowded tall columnar cells; they lack true fibrovascular cores.
• Papillary Carcinoma: Branching papillae with dense fibrovascular stalks and characteristic ground-glass nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List the three clinical findings comprising the classic triad of Grave’s Disease.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter).
• Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos).
• Localized infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Grave's disease, the thyroid follicles are lined by [___] epithelial cells that actively resorb colloid, resulting in a [___] appearance at the colloid edges.
back:
• Tall columnar.
• Scalloped or 'moth-eaten'.
• This indicates highly active hormone synthesis and resorption.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with Grave’s Disease is treated with preoperative iodine. Describe the resulting change in the thyroid's histologic appearance.
back:
• Involution of the follicular epithelium.
• Accumulation of colloid (blocks thyroglobulin secretion).
• Reduced gland vascularity, facilitating safer surgical excision.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the cellular mechanism by which Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) induces goiter enlargement.
back:
• TSI binds to and activates TSH receptors.
• Triggers the G-protein/cAMP signaling pathway.
• Stimulates follicular cell hypertrophy (increased size) and hyperplasia (increased number).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the localized skin findings of Grave’s Disease with the skin changes seen in generalized myxedema of hypothyroidism.
back:
• Grave’s: Pretibial myxedema (localized scaly thickening and induration, usually over shins).
• Hypothyroidism: Generalized non-pitting edema with broadening and coarsening of facial features.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Name the specific HLA allele most frequently associated with an increased genetic susceptibility to Grave’s Disease.
back:
• HLA-DR3.
• Other associations include polymorphisms in CTLA4, PTPN22, and IL2RA.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody responsible for the pathogenesis of Graves' disease, which functions by mimicking the action of TSH at its receptor, is [___].
back: • Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI) • A subtype of IgG antibody • Binds and activates the TSH receptor on follicular cells

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 35-year-old female presents with proptosis and a wide, staring gaze. Pathogenesis of this specific feature involves the infiltration of the retro-orbital space by T-cells and the accumulation of [___].
back: • Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) • Specifically hydrophilic molecules like hyaluronic acid • Causes edema and swelling of extraocular muscles

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI) in the development of hyperthyroidism at the cellular level.
back: • Binds to the TSH receptor • Constitutively activates adenyl cyclase • Increases intracellular cAMP levels • Triggers excessive thyroid hormone synthesis and release

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 28-year-old female presents with diffuse neck swelling, palpitations, and heat intolerance. Fine-needle aspiration reveals intrafollicular papillae. Contrast this specific microscopic feature with those seen in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back: • Graves: Crowded follicular cells forming papillae lacking fibrovascular cores • PTC: Papillae possess dense fibrovascular stalks • Graves lacks Orphan Annie eye nuclei found in PTC

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the characteristic microscopic appearance of intrafollicular colloid and follicular epithelial cells in an untreated Graves' disease patient.
back: • Epithelium: Tall, columnar, and crowded • Colloid: Pale appearance with scalloped margins • Margins reflect active resorption by hyperplastic cells

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Graves' disease is clinically recognized by a triad of symptoms consisting of hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter), localized infiltrative dermopathy, and [___].
back: • Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos) • Protrusion of the eyeballs • Associated with extraocular muscle weakness

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old patient with hyperthyroidism undergoes a radioactive iodine scan showing diffusely increased uptake. Explain the underlying mechanism for this scan pattern compared to a toxic adenoma.
back: • Graves: Global stimulation of all TSH receptors by circulating TSI antibodies • Toxic Adenoma: Focal uptake in a single autonomous nodule with suppression of the rest of the gland

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe how CD4+ T-helper cells contribute to the infiltrative ophthalmopathy seen in Graves' disease.
back: • Secrete cytokines (e.g., IFN-gamma) • Stimulate retro-orbital fibroblast proliferation • Induce synthesis of extracellular matrix proteins (glycosaminoglycans) • Promotes adipose and connective tissue expansion

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the macroscopic appearance of the thyroid gland in Graves' disease with that found in a toxic multinodular goiter (MNG).
back: • Graves: Symmetrically enlarged, soft, and "beefy" deep red parenchyma • MNG: Asymmetrically enlarged, coarsely nodular, with areas of fibrosis and hemorrhage

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify two immune-regulatory genes whose polymorphisms are associated with a higher genetic susceptibility to Graves' disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back: • CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4) • PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22) • Reflects shared breakdown in self-tolerance

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Grave’s Disease, the primary pathogenic autoantibody that binds to and activates the TSH receptor, mimicking the action of thyrotropin, is known as [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• Binds to the TSH receptor on follicular cells.
• Constitutively activates adenyl cyclase.
• Triggers excessive synthesis and release of T3 and T4.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 32-year-old female presents with a wide-eyed staring gaze and proptosis. Explain the underlying pathophysiology of her ocular presentation in Grave's disease.
back:
• Activation of retro-orbital T-cells.
• Cytokine-mediated stimulation of fibroblasts.
• Deposition of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid).
• Results in extraocular muscle edema and fatty infiltration.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the cellular mechanism behind the characteristic 'scalloping' of the colloid margins seen histologically in Grave’s Disease.
back:
• Indicates intense resorption of thyroglobulin.
• Hyperplastic follicular cells rapidly internalize colloid for hormone production.
• Follicular epithelium becomes tall and columnar to facilitate increased turnover.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the papillary projections of Grave’s Disease with those of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma regarding their core structure.
back:
• Graves' disease: Papillae result from cell crowding and lack true fibrovascular cores.
• Papillary Carcinoma: Features complex branching papillae with distinct fibrovascular stalks and Orphan Annie nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify three specific genetic loci associated with immune regulation that predispose individuals to Grave’s Disease.
back:
• CTLA4 (inhibitory T-cell receptor).
• PTPN22 (tyrosine phosphatase).
• HLA-DR3 (major histocompatibility complex allele).
• TSHR (TSH receptor gene locus).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: On gross examination, the Grave’s Disease thyroid gland typically appears symmetrically enlarged with a 'beefy red' parenchyma due to [___].
back:
• Markedly increased vascularity and blood flow.
• Diffuse hypertrophy and hyperplasia of follicle cells.
• Gland is usually firm with an intact capsule.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with Grave's Disease develops thick, scaly induration of the skin on her shins. Identify the diagnosis and the tissue-level changes responsible for this findng.
back:
• Pretibial Myxedema (infiltrative dermopathy).
• Accumulation of glycosaminoglycans in the dermis.
• Accompanied by mononuclear lymphocyte infiltration and edema.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the intracellular signaling cascade initiated upon the binding of Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) to the follicular cell receptor.
back:
• TSI binding activates G-protein coupled receptors.
• Stimulates adenyl cyclase, increasing intracellular cAMP.
• cAMP activates protein kinases to drive hormone synthesis.
• Leads to unregulated follicular cell hyperplasia.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast Grave's Disease with Subacute Granulomatous Thyroiditis regarding radioactive iodine uptake during the hyperthyroid phase.
back:
• Graves' disease: Diffusely increased uptake due to chronic TSH-receptor stimulation.
• Granulomatous thyroiditis: Decreased uptake because hormone release is due to follicle damage, not hyperfunction.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List the primary constituents of the interstitial inflammatory infiltrate observed in Grave’s Disease thyroid histology.
back:
• T-lymphocytes (predominant).
• B-cells and mature plasma cells.
• Arrangement into well-developed germinal centers throughout the parenchyma.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody in Grave's disease that binds the TSH receptor to mimic TSH action is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• Found in approximately 90% of patients
• Activates adenyl cyclase and increases thyroid hormone release.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations and bilateral proptosis. Labs reveal TSH <0.01 uIU/mL and elevated Free T4. Describe the underlying mechanism of her orbital symptoms.
back:
• Activated CD4+ T-cells release cytokines
• Fibroblasts synthesize hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)
• Resultant osmotic edema and fatty infiltration displace the eyeball.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the intracellular signaling pathway triggered by TSI binding in Grave's disease thyrocytes.
back:
• TSI activates G-protein coupled receptors
• Stimulates adenyl cyclase, raising cAMP levels
• Triggers cAMP-dependent protein kinases to increase hormone synthesis.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the histological features of the papillae found in Grave’s disease with those of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Grave's: Small, crowded papillae lack true fibrovascular cores
• Papillary Carcinoma: Complex, branching papillae possess dense fibrovascular stalks.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List the two salient microscopic findings of thyroid colloid in an untreated patient with Grave’s disease.
back:
• Pale/clear color (dilute appearance)
• Scalloped margins (due to active resorption by hyperplastic tall columnar epithelium).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Genetic susceptibility to Grave's disease is frequently associated with polymorphisms in the immune-regulating genes [___] and PTPN22.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte–associated antigen-4)
• Also associated with Hashimoto thyroiditis and Type 1 Diabetes.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with diffuse goiter develops scaly, non-pitting thickening of the skin over the shins. Name the clinical term and the substance responsible for this finding.
back:
• Pretibial Myxedema (Infiltrative Dermopathy)
• Caused by excessive accumulation of Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in the dermis.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of preoperative iodine administration in the management of the Grave’s disease thyroid gland.
back:
• Promotes epithelial involution
• Blocks thyroglobulin secretion, causing colloid accumulation
• Reduces gland vascularity prior to surgery.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the gross appearance of the thyroid parenchyma in Grave’s disease versus Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Grave's: Symmetrical, beefy red, soft (meaty) appearance
• Hashimoto: Pale, yellow-tan, firm, and nodular appearance.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the classic clinical triad that defines Graves disease.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter)
• Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos)
• Localized, infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody in Graves' Disease responsible for stimulating the TSH receptor and increasing thyroid hormone release is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• Binds to TSH receptors and mimics TSH action
• Activates adenyl cyclase to increase T3/T4 secretion

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and proptosis. Biopsy of the retro-orbital tissue would reveal an accumulation of [___].
back:
• Glycosaminoglycans (specifically hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate)
• Infiltration by mononuclear cells (predominantly T-cells)
• Edema and fatty infiltration of extraocular muscles

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the intracellular signaling mechanism triggered by Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) in Graves' Disease.
back:
• TSI binds to and activates the G-protein coupled TSH receptor
• Triggers activation of adenyl cyclase
• Increases intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) levels, stimulating follicle growth and hormone synthesis

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic papillary projections found in Graves’ Disease with those seen in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Graves: Small projections formed by crowded cells; lack true fibrovascular cores
• Carcinoma: Branching papillae containing dense fibrovascular stalks
• Nuclei: Normal in Graves; "Orphan Annie eye" or ground-glass in carcinoma

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the characteristic appearance of follicular colloid and its margins in untreated Graves’ Disease.
back:
• Colloid is characteristically pale in appearance
• Margins are "scalloped" or moth-eaten
• Result of active resorption of colloid by hyperplastic columnar epithelium

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The development of infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema) in Graves' Disease is primarily attributed to the deposition of [___] in the dermis.
back:
• Hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)
• Associated with lymphocytic infiltration and dermal thickening
• Present in only a minority of Graves' patients

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient presents with diffuse thyroid enlargement and a soft, 'meaty' red parenchyma on gross section. This appearance is most likely due to [___].
back:
• Diffuse hypertrophy and hyperplasia of follicular epithelial cells
• Increased vascularity and blood flow throughout the gland
• Characteristic of Graves' Disease (diffuse toxic goiter)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Detail the role of CD4+ Helper T-cells in the pathogenesis of Graves' infiltrative ophthalmopathy.
back:
• T-cells secrete cytokines that stimulate retro-orbital fibroblast proliferation
• Fibroblasts synthesize excess extracellular matrix proteins (GAGs)
• Leads to osmotic pressure increase, edema, and displacement of the eyeball

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the gross morphology of Graves’ Disease with a toxic Multinodular Goiter.
back:
• Graves: Diffuse, symmetric enlargement; smooth external surface
• Multinodular Goiter: Asymmetric enlargement; irregular, multiple nodules
• Graves lacks the extensive scarring and calcification common in chronic goiters

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the three specific immune-regulating gene loci associated with a genetic predisposition to Graves' Disease.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte–associated antigen-4)
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22)
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor α chain)

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody responsible for hyperthyroidism in Graves' disease, which acts as a functional TSH receptor agonist, is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• Binds and activates the TSH receptor on follicles.
• Mimics TSH by stimulating adenyl cyclase and cAMP.
• Found in approximately 90% of Graves' patients.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female with hyperthyroidism presents with proptosis and impaired extraocular muscle movement. This specific manifestation is driven by the retro-orbital accumulation of [___].
back:
• Hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (e.g., hyaluronic acid).
• T-cell infiltration and edema of orbital muscles.
• Increased adipocytes (fatty infiltration).
• Driven by CD4+ Th1 cell cytokines.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of adenyl cyclase and cyclic AMP (cAMP) once Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulins (TSI) bind to follicular epithelial cells.
back:
• TSI binding triggers G-protein activation.
• Activates the enzyme adenyl cyclase.
• Increases intracellular levels of cyclic AMP (cAMP).
• Stimulates excessive thyroid hormone synthesis and release.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic papillary structures seen in Graves' disease with those characteristic of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back:
• Graves: Small papillae represent crowded hyperplastic cells; lack true fibrovascular stalks.
• PTC: Complex branching papillae; possess distinct fibrovascular cores.
• Nuclei: Graves lacks the 'Orphan Annie' nuclei and psammoma bodies of PTC.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the characteristic gross appearance and consistency of the thyroid gland in an untreated case of Graves' disease.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric thyroid enlargement.
• Soft, 'beefy red' or meaty parenchyma.
• Resembles skeletal muscle consistency.
• Intact capsule with prominent vascularity.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Graves' disease, hyperactive follicular cells resorb thyroid colloid, resulting in a hallmark microscopic appearance known as [___].
back:
• Scalloped margins (scalloping).
• Reflects tall, columnar follicular cells actively extracting thyroglobulin.
• Colloid appears pale and depleted at follicle edges.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with Graves' disease presents with scaly thickening and induration of the skin overlying the shins. This dermopathy is caused by the deposition of [___].
back:
• Glycosaminoglycans (e.g., hyaluronic acid).
• Known clinically as Pretibial Myxedema.
• Accompanied by lymphocytic infiltration.
• Present only in a minority of Graves' cases.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify three non-thyroidal genetic polymorphisms that increase susceptibility to Graves' disease and are shared with Type 1 Diabetes.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen-4).
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22).
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain).
• These regulate T-cell signaling and self-tolerance.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Distinguish Graves' disease from Subacute Thyroiditis based on radionuclide scintigraphy (radioactive iodine uptake) findings.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased iodine uptake (hot scan).
• Subacute Thyroiditis: Decreased iodine uptake (cold scan).
• Graves involves true hyperfunction; Thyroiditis involves hormone leakage from damaged follicles.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Detail the characteristic interstitial lymphoid findings observed microscopically in Graves' thyroid parenchyma.
back:
• Diffuse mononuclear inflammatory infiltrates.
• Predominantly T-cells with scattered B-cells.
• Formation of well-developed germinal centers.
• Indicates underlying autoimmune-mediated hyperplasia.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody responsible for the pathogenesis of Graves’ disease by mimicking the action of TSH is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• An IgG antibody subtype.
• Binds to the TSH receptor, activating adenyl cyclase and hormone release.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 32-year-old female presents with palpitations, weight loss, and a diffuse, symmetric goiter. Her labs show high T4 and undetectable TSH. The most likely underlying immunologic mechanism is [___].
back:
• Type II hypersensitivity.
• Activation of follicular cells by autoantibodies (TSI).
• Independent of pituitary TSH control.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) findings in Graves’ disease with those found in Subacute (Granulomatous) Thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased uptake (hyperfunctional gland).
• Subacute Thyroiditis: Diminished uptake (follicle destruction and hormone leak).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient presents with a firm, enlarged thyroid and thyrotoxicosis. Histology reveals papillae within follicles. Distinguish this from Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma based on fibrovascular structure and nuclei.
back:
• Graves: Small papillae lack fibrovascular cores; nuclei are normal (no grooves/inclusions).
• Carcinoma: Branching papillae have dense fibrovascular cores; nuclei show "Orphan Annie" empty appearance.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the mechanism by which Propylthiouracil (PTU) reduces thyroid hormone levels during a Graves’ thyrotoxic crisis.
back:
• Inhibits the oxidation of iodide (blocks new hormone synthesis).
• Inhibits the peripheral conversion (deiodination) of T4 into the more active T3.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The hallmark laboratory finding used as a sensitive screening test for Graves’ disease is a [___] level of serum [___].
back:
• Low (depressed) serum TSH.
• Accompanied by elevated free T3 and T4 levels.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A Graves’ patient presents with scaly, orange-peel-like thickening of the skin over the shins. This infiltrative dermopathy is primarily caused by [___].
back:
• Accumulation of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (GAGs).
• Associated lymphocyte infiltration.
• Clinically termed "Pretibial Myxedema."

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the specific T-cell mediated mechanism that results in the proptosis characteristic of Graves' ophthalmopathy.
back:
• CD4+ T-cells secrete cytokines (e.g., IFN-gamma).
• Stimulates fibroblasts to produce glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid).
• Leads to retro-orbital edema and extraocular muscle swelling.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis status in Graves’ disease versus a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma regarding TSH levels.
back:
• Graves: High T3/T4 suppresses the pituitary (Low TSH).
• TSH Adenoma: Pituitary autonomously secretes hormone (High TSH).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the characteristic microscopic change in the colloid margins of hyperplastic follicles in Graves’ disease.
back:
• Scalloped margins.
• Resulting from active resorption of colloid by tall columnar epithelial cells.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The specific autoantibody in Graves' disease that binds to the TSH receptor and mimics its action is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• It activates adenyl cyclase to increase thyroid hormone synthesis and release.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with weight loss, heat intolerance, and bulging eyes. Laboratory studies show low TSH and high Free T4. Explain the primary immunologic failure occurring in this patient.
back:
• Breakdown in self-tolerance to thyroid autoantigens (specifically the TSH receptor).
• Leads to production of stimulatory autoantibodies (TSI).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the role of cAMP-dependent protein kinases in the pathogenesis of Graves' disease upon autoantibody binding.
back:
• TSI binding activates the G-protein on follicular cells.
• This triggers adenyl cyclase, raising intracellular cAMP.
• Elevated cAMP stimulates follicular growth and excessive thyroid hormone production.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A biopsy of an enlarged thyroid shows tall follicular cells forming small papillae. Contrast these Grave’s-associated papillae with those found in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back:
• Graves': Small projections that lack true fibrovascular cores.
• PTC: Branching papillae with dense fibrovascular stalks and Orphan Annie eye nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the specific retro-orbital tissue changes responsible for the exophthalmos characteristic of Graves' disease.
back:
• Infiltration by T-cells and edema.
• Accumulation of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (e.g., hyaluronic acid).
• Increased number of adipocytes (fatty infiltration).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Graves' disease, the follicular epithelial cells actively resorb colloid, creating a characteristic [___] appearance at the colloid margins.
back: • Scalloped or "moth-eaten" appearance.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Despite achieving a euthyroid state with thionamides, a patient's proptosis persists. Apply the pathogenesis of infiltrative ophthalmopathy to explain why hormone control failed to resolve the eye symptoms.
back:
• Ophthalmopathy is driven by CD4+ T-cell cytokines and GAG deposition.
• These autoimmune orbital changes are independent of circulating thyroid hormone levels.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List the three specific genetic polymorphisms associated with immune regulation that increase susceptibility to both Graves' disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4).
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22).
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake findings in Graves' disease with those of Subacute Granulomatous Thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves': Diffuse, increased uptake (due to TSI hyperstimulation).
• Thyroiditis: Decreased uptake (due to follicular destruction and hormone leak).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the primary gross morphological characteristics of the thyroid gland in a patient with untreated Graves' disease.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric enlargement (often >80g).
• Intact capsule.
• Soft, beefy, deep-red parenchyma (resembling muscle).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The primary autoantibody in Graves disease that mimics the action of TSH by binding to its receptor is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• It stimulates adenyl cyclase and increases thyroid hormone release.
• Observed in approximately 90% of patients.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and a symmetric, painless, 'beefy red' thyroid enlargement. Histology reveals tall, crowded follicular cells with scalloped colloid margins. What is the underlying pathogenesis?
back:
• Breakdown in self-tolerance to thyroid autoantigens (Type II Hypersensitivity).
• B-cells produce TSIs that constitutively activate the TSH receptor.
• Leads to diffuse follicular hypertrophy and hyperplasia.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the mechanism behind the infiltrative ophthalmopathy seen in Graves disease that distinguishes it from simple lid lag.
back:
• Cytokines from activated CD4+ T-cells stimulate retro-orbital fibroblasts.
• Excess hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid) and adipocytes accumulate.
• Results in edema, extraocular muscle swelling, and displacement of the eyeball.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic features of the papillary projections found in Graves disease versus those found in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back:
• Graves: Small papillae created by crowded tall cells; lack true fibrovascular cores.
• PTC: Branching papillae with distinct fibrovascular stalks and characteristic 'Orphan Annie' nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the immediate histological effect of preoperative iodine administration on a hyperplastic Graves thyroid gland.
back:
• Induces involution of the follicular epithelium.
• Promotes accumulation of colloid by blocking thyroglobulin secretion.
• Decreases the vascularity of the gland.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In the laboratory diagnosis of Graves disease, the serum TSH level is classically [___] while free T4 is elevated.
back:
• Decreased (Suppressed).
• High levels of T3/T4 provide negative feedback to the anterior pituitary thyrotrophs.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient presents with exophthalmos and a diffuse, warm, nontender goiter. A radionuclide scan shows high, uniform uptake of iodine across both lobes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Graves Disease.
• High uptake distinguishes it from thyroiditis (low uptake) and toxic nodules (localized uptake).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Detail how the 'dermopathy' (pretibial myxedema) of Graves disease develops at the cellular level.
back:
• Infiltration of the dermis by T-cells.
• Cytokine-induced stimulation of fibroblasts.
• Deposition of glycosaminoglycans in the dermis, causing scaly skin thickening.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the colloid appearance in Graves disease with that seen in a diffuse nontoxic (simple) goiter during the involution phase.
back:
• Graves: Pale colloid with 'scalloped' margins due to active resorption.
• Simple Goiter: Abundant, brown, glassy, and translucent colloid with flattened epithelium.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: List the three specific immune-function gene polymorphisms most frequently linked to both Graves disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4).
• PTPN22 (Protein tyrosine phosphatase-22).
• IL2RA (Interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In the pathogenesis of Graves' Disease, the primary autoantibody responsible for mimicking the action of TSH is [___].
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).
• It is an IgG antibody that binds to the TSH receptor.
• TSI is detected in approximately 90% of patients.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and a visible protrusion of the eyeballs. Physical exam shows a diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid. Identify the underlying pathology.
back:
• Graves' Disease.
• Characterized by a triad: hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter), infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos), and localized dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain how Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) induces hyperthyroidism at the cellular level.
back:
• TSI binds the TSH receptor on follicular cells.
• It activates adenyl cyclase, mimicking TSH.
• This increases intracellular cAMP levels.
• Result: Constitutive synthesis and release of T3 and T4.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the morphology of the papillae found in Graves' Disease with those seen in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
back:
• Graves: Small papillae formed by crowded, tall epithelium projecting into lumens; lack fibrovascular cores.
• Papillary Ca: Branching papillae with distinct fibrovascular cores and 'Orphan Annie' nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Identify the primary substances responsible for the volume increase in the retro-orbital space in Graves' ophthalmopathy.
back:
• Hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate).
• Accumulate due to CD4+ T-cell cytokine stimulation of fibroblasts.
• Leads to edema, extraocular muscle swelling, and fatty infiltration.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Histological examination of a Graves' thyroid shows follicles lined by tall columnar cells that actively resorb colloid, giving its margins a [___] appearance.
back:
• Scalloped appearance.
• Result of active resorption of thyroid hormone precursors into the hyperplastic follicular cells.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A patient with suspected Graves' Disease undergoes a radionuclide scan of the neck. Describe the expected pattern of radioactive iodine uptake.
back:
• Diffusely increased uptake throughout the entire gland.
• This contrasts with toxic adenomas (focal 'hot' nodules) or thyroiditis (decreased uptake).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Briefly outline the genetic basis shared between Graves' Disease and Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
back:
• Polymorphisms in immune-regulatory genes.
• Key loci: CTLA4, PTPN22, and IL2RA.
• Both involve a breakdown in self-tolerance to thyroid antigens.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast Graves' Disease with Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis regarding radioactive iodine uptake and hormone status.
back:
• Graves: High uptake; high T3/T4 (true hyperthyroidism).
• Granulomatous: Low uptake; transient high T3/T4 (leakage of preformed hormone from damaged follicles).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the gross appearance of the thyroid parenchyma in an untreated patient with Graves' Disease.
back:
• Diffuse, symmetric enlargement.
• Intact capsule without significant nodules.
• Cut surface is pale, soft, and has a 'meaty' appearance resembling muscle.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: In Graves disease, the primary pathogenic autoantibody is [___], which binds to and activates the TSH receptor on follicular cells.
back: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI). It mimics TSH action, stimulating adenyl cyclase and increasing the synthesis and release of thyroid hormones (Type II hypersensitivity).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A 30-year-old female presents with palpitations, weight loss, and proptosis. Scintigraphy shows diffusely increased iodine uptake. Explain the underlying pathophysiology of her eye findings.
back: Infiltrative ophthalmopathy. T-cells secrete cytokines that stimulate retro-orbital fibroblasts to produce glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). This causes osmotic edema, extraocular muscle swelling, and fatty infiltration.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Describe the intracellular signaling pathway triggered by Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulins (TSI) once they bind to the thyrocyte receptor.
back: Binding activates G-protein (Gs) signaling, which stimulates adenyl cyclase. This increases intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP), promoting follicular cell hypertrophy, hyperplasia, and excessive hormone secretion.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the microscopic papillary structures seen in Graves disease with those seen in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PTC).
back: Graves papillae are small, formed by epithelial crowding, and lack true fibrovascular cores. PTC papillae are branching with distinct fibrovascular stalks and characteristic 'Orphan Annie eye' nuclei.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: State the typical laboratory profile (TSH and Free T4) expected in Graves disease and explain the mechanism behind the TSH value.
back: TSH is markedly decreased; Free T4 is increased. Low TSH results from negative feedback by high circulating T3/T4 levels on the anterior pituitary thyrotrophs.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: The localized infiltrative dermopathy characteristic of Graves disease, presenting as scaly thickening of the skin over the shins, is termed [___].
back: Pretibial Myxedema. It is caused by the deposition of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans and T-cell infiltration in the dermis, independent of the thyroid status.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: A neonate born to a mother with Graves disease presents with irritability and tachycardia. Identify the mechanism of this 'Neonatal Graves' and its prognosis.
back: Mechanism: Transplacental passage of maternal IgG autoantibodies (TSI). Prognosis: Usually transient; symptoms resolve as maternal antibodies are cleared from the infant's circulation.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Explain the morphologic basis for the 'scalloped' appearance of colloid margins in Graves disease follicles.
back: It represents rapid resorption of thyroglobulin (colloid) by the hyperactive, tall columnar follicular epithelial cells to meet the high demand for hormone production.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Contrast the radioactive iodine uptake pattern of Graves disease with that of Toxic Multinodular Goiter (Plummer Syndrome).
back: Graves Disease: Diffuse, symmetric, and uniform increased uptake. Toxic Multinodular Goiter: Patchy uptake with specific 'hot' autonomous nodules and 'cold' inactive areas.

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Grave’s Disease
front: Which specific HLA allele and non-HLA immune-regulation genes are most strongly associated with Graves disease susceptibility?
back: HLA Allele: HLA-DR3. Non-HLA: CTLA4 and PTPN22 (both involved in regulating T-cell inhibitory signals and self-tolerance).

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: The fundamental pathogenic mechanism of diffuse goiter involves a compensatory rise in [___] levels following impaired thyroid hormone synthesis.
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
• Triggers follicular cell hypertrophy and hyperplasia
• Aims to overcome hormone deficiency and maintain a euthyroid state

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: A 55-year-old female presents with a massive, irregular neck swelling and difficulty swallowing. Scintigraphy shows uneven iodine uptake with multiple "cold" and "warm" areas. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Multinodular Goiter
• Symptoms caused by mass effects (dysphagia, airway obstruction)
• Results from recurrent cycles of follicular hyperplasia and involution

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Explain the transition from a long-standing diffuse simple goiter into a multinodular goiter.
back:
• Variations in follicular cell response to TSH produce clones with growth advantages
• Physical stress leads to follicle/vessel rupture
• Hemorrhage, scarring, and calcification subsequently produce irregular nodularity

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Contrast the microscopic boundary of a hyperplastic nodule in multinodular goiter with that of a follicular adenoma.
back:
• Multinodular Goiter: Lacks a prominent, well-developed, or complete fibrous capsule
• Follicular Adenoma: Features a well-defined, intact, and continuous capsule
• Goiter nodules show compressed residual parenchyma at the periphery

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Define the clinical significance of Plummer Syndrome in the context of thyroid pathology.
back:
• Toxic Multinodular Goiter
• Development of autonomous, hyperfunctioning nodules in a long-standing goiter
• Produces hyperthyroidism without the ophthalmopathy or dermopathy seen in Graves disease

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: In regions where the soil and food supply lack sufficient [___], the prevalence of endemic goiter often exceeds 10% of the population.
back:
• Iodine
• Leads to reduced T3 and T4 synthesis
• Common in mountainous regions like the Andes or Himalayas

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Gross examination of a resected thyroid reveals a symmetrically enlarged, brown, glassy, and translucent gland with flattened follicular epithelium on microscopy. Identify this specific phase.
back:
• Phase of Colloid Involution (Colloid Goiter)
• Follows the hyperplastic phase of diffuse nontoxic goiter
• Occurs when dietary iodine increases or thyroid hormone demand decreases

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Describe how dietary goitrogens, such as those found in cassava root, contribute to the pathogenesis of goiter.
back:
• Contain thiocyanates that inhibit iodide transport within the thyroid
• Suppress T3 and T4 synthesis, triggering TSH-mediated enlargement
• Exacerbates concurrent dietary iodine deficiency

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Contrast the follicular epithelium in the hyperplastic phase versus the colloid involution phase of diffuse goiter.
back:
• Hyperplastic Phase: Tall, crowded columnar cells that may form pseudopapillary projections
• Colloid Involution Phase: Flattened, inactive cuboidal epithelium
• Involutional follicles are hugely distended with abundant colloid

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
front: Identify the clinical entity where a massive goiter grows behind the sternum and clavicles, potentially causing superior vena cava syndrome.
back:
• Intrathoracic or "Plunging" Goiter
• Causes compression of the trachea, esophagus, and large vessels
• Most commonly a manifestation of multinodular goiter in older adults

category: Describe the pathogenesis & salient morphological features of Diffuse and Multinodular goiter
coreConcept: Trophic effect of TSH in goitrogenesis
