• Low (suppressed) thyroglobulin 
• Distinguishes from Graves or Goiter where thyroglobulin is high 
• Associated with low RAIU scan.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 40-year-old woman presents with a painful, tender neck mass and symptoms of hyperthyroidism following a viral upper respiratory infection. Identify the diagnosis and its eventual functional outcome.
back:
• Granulomatous (de Quervain) Thyroiditis 
• Transient hyperthyroidism followed by transient hypothyroidism 
• Most patients return to a euthyroid state.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the dual mechanism by which Propylthiouracil (PTU) reduces circulating triiodothyronine (T3) levels during a thyroid storm.
back:
• Inhibits thyroid peroxidase (blocking organification) 
• Inhibits 5'-deiodinase (blocking peripheral T4 to T3 conversion) 
• Rapidly lowers biological activity.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the biochemical profiles (TSH and T4) of Primary Hypothyroidism with Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH; Low Free T4 
• Secondary: Low/Normal TSH; Low Free T4 
• Primary is usually due to Hashimoto or Iodine deficiency.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Name the most frequent cause of congenital hypothyroidism worldwide and the associated physical finding in the thyroid gland.
back:
• Endemic Iodine Deficiency 
• Presents as Goitrous Hypothyroidism (enlarged thyroid) 
• Leads to Cretinism if untreated in infancy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hypothyroidism, the diagnostic laboratory profile is uniquely characterized by a serum TSH level that is [___].
back:
• Elevated (High)
• Accompanied by decreased free T4 levels
• Due to loss of feedback inhibition on the pituitary.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 45-year-old female presents with heat intolerance, weight loss, and palpitations. Lab tests show low TSH and high free T4. Identify the most likely underlying autoimmune cause.
back:
• Graves Disease
• Caused by Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• Leads to diffuse hyperplasia of the thyroid.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the mechanism by which secondary (central) hypothyroidism results in decreased serum T4 levels.
back:
• Pituitary or hypothalamic failure
• Deficiency of TSH or TRH
• Results in loss of trophic stimulation to the thyroid gland.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the serum TSH levels found in primary hyperthyroidism with those seen in a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
back:
• Primary Hyperthyroidism: Low (suppressed) TSH
• Pituitary Adenoma (Secondary): Normal or raised TSH
• Both show elevated free T3 and T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three primary causes of thyrotoxicosis associated with actual hyperfunction (hyperthyroidism) of the gland.
back:
• Graves Disease (85% of cases)
• Toxic Multinodular Goiter
• Hyperfunctioning (Toxic) Adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The most frequent cause of congenital hypothyroidism worldwide is [___].
back:
• Endemic iodine deficiency in the diet
• Leads to cretinism if untreated in early childhood.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: An elderly patient with a long-standing multinodular goiter develops tachycardia and anxiety. Lab results reveal suppressed TSH and high T4. What is the specific clinical name for this state?
back:
• Toxic Multinodular Goiter
• Also known as Plummer Syndrome
• Caused by the development of an autonomous hyperfunctioning nodule.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the thyroid function panel profile expected in a patient with 'T3 Toxicosis'.
back:
• Low (suppressed) TSH
• Elevated serum free T3
• Normal or decreased free T4 levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the underlying causes of iatrogenic hypothyroidism with 'goitrous' primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Iatrogenic: Surgical resection, radioiodine ablation, or external radiation
• Goitrous: Hashimoto thyroiditis, iodine deficiency, or drugs (e.g., lithium).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the most sensitive screening test for detecting early stages of primary thyroid dysfunction.
back:
• Serum TSH concentration
• Levels are decreased in hyperthyroidism
• Levels are increased in primary hypothyroidism.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
coreConcept: Serum TSH as primary screening tool
front: The most sensitive screening test for diagnosing both primary hyperthyroidism and primary hypothyroidism is measurement of the serum [___] level.
back:
• Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
• Levels are decreased in primary hyperthyroidism
• Levels are increased in primary hypothyroidism

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 32-year-old female presents with heat intolerance, weight loss, and tremors. Lab work shows low TSH and elevated free T4. If a radioactive iodine scan shows focal uptake in a single "hot" nodule, the most likely diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Toxic adenoma
• Results from activating mutations in the TSH receptor or GNAS
• Nodule functions independently of pituitary TSH control

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain why serum TSH levels are characteristically elevated in primary hypothyroidism while T4 levels remain low.
back:
• Low T4 removes negative feedback on the pituitary
• Anterior pituitary increases TSH to stimulate the thyroid
• Primary thyroid damage prevents response to the TSH surge

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the laboratory profile of primary hyperthyroidism (Graves disease) with secondary hyperthyroidism (TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma).
back:
• Primary: Low TSH with High free T3/T4
• Secondary: High or inappropriately normal TSH with High free T3/T4
• Secondary is rare and indicates pituitary-driven excess

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify three common iatrogenic causes of acquired primary hypothyroidism encountered in surgical practice.
back:
• Total or subtotal thyroidectomy
• Radioactive iodine (I-131) ablation
• External beam radiation therapy to the neck

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In iodine-deficient regions, the most common cause of congenital hypothyroidism leading to cretinism is [___].
back:
• Endemic iodine deficiency
• Impairs synthesis of thyroxine (T4) during fetal development
• Results in increased TSH and compensatory goiter

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient with a history of long-term lithium use for bipolar disorder presents with cold intolerance. Laboratory evaluation reveals a high TSH and low T4. State the diagnosis and the role of the drug in this state.
back:
• Drug-induced primary hypothyroidism
• Lithium acts as a goitrogen, interfering with hormone synthesis
• High TSH reflects the loss of feedback inhibition

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the clinical phenomenon of "apathetic hyperthyroidism" commonly seen in elderly patients.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism presenting without classic adrenergic signs
• Presents as unexplained weight loss or worsening cardiac disease
• Suppressed TSH and high T4 confirm the diagnosis

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the levels of TSH and Free T4 in primary hypothyroidism versus central (secondary) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH, Low Free T4
• Central: Low/Normal TSH, Low Free T4
• Central results from pituitary or hypothalamic failure

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List the characteristic findings in a radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan for Graves disease versus Factitious Thyrotoxicosis.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased uptake ("hot" scan)
• Factitious: Low/Absent uptake ("cold" scan)
• Factitious is caused by exogenous intake of thyroxine

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The combination of decreased serum T4 and T3 levels with a compensatory increase in serum TSH is the classic laboratory profile for [___] hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary Hypothyroidism
• Mechanism: Loss of feedback inhibition on the pituitary
• Most common cause: Hashimoto thyroiditis or iodine deficiency

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 45-year-old female reports heat intolerance, weight loss, and tachycardia. Labs show elevated Free T4 and undetectable TSH. Radioactive iodine scan shows diffuse uptake. State the most likely diagnosis and its primary autoantibody.
back:
• Diagnosis: Graves Disease
• Autoantibody: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• Mechanism: TSI mimics TSH at the receptor, causing autonomous hormone release

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism leading to secondary (central) hypothyroidism and its expected TSH level.
back:
• Mechanism: Pituitary or hypothalamic failure leads to TSH deficiency
• TSH Level: Low or inappropriately normal
• Thyroid Hormones: Low Free T4 and T3

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the TSH and T4 levels in primary hyperthyroidism with those found in a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
back:
• Primary: Low TSH; High Free T4/T3
• Secondary (Pituitary Adenoma): Normal to High TSH; High Free T4/T3

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three common causes of primary thyrotoxicosis associated with hyperfunction of the thyroid gland.
back:
• Graves Disease (Diffuse hyperplasia)
• Toxic multinodular goiter (Plummer syndrome)
• Hyperfunctional (toxic) adenoma

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In a thyrotoxic patient, the discovery of a 'cold' thyroid nodule on radionuclide scanning suggests the excess hormone is likely due to [___] rather than autonomous gland hyperfunction.
back:
• Thyroiditis (leakage of preformed hormone)
• Factitious thyrotoxicosis (exogenous intake)
• Ectopic thyroid (e.g., Struma ovarii)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A neonate presents with severe intellectual disability, protruding tongue, and umbilical hernia. Laboratory tests confirm low T4 and high TSH. Identify the clinical term for this condition and its most common worldwide cause.
back:
• Condition: Cretinism
• Worldwide Cause: Endemic dietary iodine deficiency
• Secondary Cause: Dyshormonogenetic goiter (genetic biosynthetic defect)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the expected TSH response to a Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone (TRH) stimulation test in a patient with pituitary failure.
back:
• Response: Failure of TSH to rise
• Significance: Confirms the pituitary (secondary) origin of hypothyroidism
• Normal Result: Rapid TSH rise after administration

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the metabolic state 'Myxedema' from 'Cretinism' regarding age of onset and typical symptoms.
back:
• Cretinism: Infancy/Childhood; severe intellectual/growth disability
• Myxedema: Adulthood; fatigue, cold intolerance, non-pitting edema
• Both: Represent severe thyroid hormone deficiency

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate two iatrogenic causes of primary hypothyroidism commonly encountered in clinical practice.
back:
• Total or subtotal thyroidectomy
• Radioiodine ablation therapy (for Graves)
• External radiation therapy to the neck

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The most useful single screening test for hyperthyroidism, which is decreased even in the earliest subclinical stages, is the measurement of serum [___].
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• Suppression occurs due to feedback inhibition by high T3/T4
• Exceptions include rare secondary causes like TSH-secreting pituitary adenomas.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 30-year-old female presents with weight loss, heat intolerance, and a diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid. Labs show TSH <0.01 mU/L and elevated Free T4. Identify the most likely diagnosis and the specific stimulating autoantibody.
back:
• Graves Disease
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• TSI binds to and activates the TSH receptor, leading to autonomous thyroid hyperfunction.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the diagnostic utility of Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU) in distinguishing Graves disease from subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Diffusely increased uptake (hyperfunctioning gland)
• Thyroiditis: Decreased uptake (low RAIU)
• Thyroiditis involves the release of preformed hormone, not increased synthesis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the expected serum TSH and Free T4 levels in primary hypothyroidism with those seen in secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH; Low T4 (loss of feedback inhibition)
• Secondary: Low/Normal TSH; Low T4 (pituitary/hypothalamic failure)
• Primary causes include Hashimoto thyroiditis and iodine deficiency.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three distinct iatrogenic causes of primary hypothyroidism resulting from medical intervention.
back:
• Surgical thyroidectomy
• Radioiodine (I-131) ablation therapy
• Antithyroid drugs (Propylthiouracil, Methimazole) or Lithium.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Hypothyroidism developing in infancy or early childhood, often caused by endemic iodine deficiency or inborn errors of thyroid metabolism, is termed [___].
back:
• Cretinism
• Features: Severe intellectual disability, short stature, and coarse facial features
• Results from low maternal/fetal T3 and T4 levels during critical brain development.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 45-year-old male presents with fatigue, constipation, and cold intolerance. Labs show a T4 of 3.2 µg/dL (Normal: 5-12). If the cause is autoimmune destruction of the gland, describe the expected TSH level and serum cholesterol status.
back:
• Elevated TSH (Primary Hypothyroidism)
• Elevated total cholesterol/LDL
• Decreased thyroid hormone reduces the expression of hepatic LDL receptors.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the hormone levels and diagnostic requirements of "T3 toxicosis."
back:
• Elevated serum T3; Low TSH
• Free T4 levels are often normal or decreased
• Diagnosis requires direct serum T3 measurement to avoid missing the condition.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the mechanism of hyperthyroidism in Toxic Multinodular Goiter versus Factitious Thyrotoxicosis.
back:
• Toxic MNG: Autonomous hyperfunction (increased synthesis) within thyroid nodules
• Factitious: Exogenous intake of thyroxine (thyroid is inactive)
• Factitious thyrotoxicosis presents with low RAIU and an atrophic gland.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Name the rare condition characterized by secondary hyperthyroidism where serum TSH is inappropriately normal or elevated despite high circulating T3/T4.
back:
• TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma
• Fails to respond to TRH stimulation test
• Contrasts with Graves where high T4 suppresses TSH to undetectable levels.

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: The characteristic metaplastic change in Hashimoto thyroiditis where follicular cells develop abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm is known as [___].
back:
• Hürthle cell (or oxyphil) change
• Represents a response of low cuboidal epithelium to chronic injury
• Characterized by mitochondria-rich, granular cytoplasm

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A 50-year-old female presents with a painless goiter. Labs show transiently elevated T4 and low TSH, but radioactive iodine uptake is decreased. Identify this clinical phase of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashitoxicosis
• Caused by physical disruption of thyroid follicles
• Results in the release of preformed thyroid hormones into the blood

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Explain the role of CD4+ Th1 cells in the tissue destruction observed in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
back:
• Th1 cells secrete interferon-gamma (IFN-γ)
• This recruits and activates macrophages
• Activated macrophages cause direct damage to the thyroid follicles

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the lymphocytic infiltration of Hashimoto thyroiditis with that of subacute lymphocytic (painless) thyroiditis regarding Hürthle cells.
back:
• Hashimoto: Prominent Hürthle cell metaplasia and extensive fibrosis
• Subacute Lymphocytic: Minimal to no Hürthle cell change or significant fibrosis
• Both show lymphocytic infiltrates and germinal centers

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Beyond hypothyroidism, patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis have a significantly increased risk of developing which specific malignancy?
back:
• B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
• Specifically extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MALToma)
• Arises within the chronic inflammatory milieu of the gland

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Susceptibility to Hashimoto thyroiditis is genetically linked to polymorphisms in [___], which is a negative regulator of T-cell responses also associated with Type 1 Diabetes.
back:
• CTLA4 (Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4)
• Also associated with PTPN22 polymorphisms
• Indicates a shared genetic basis for breakdown in immune tolerance

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: A middle-aged female presents with gradual weight gain and cold intolerance. Histology of the thyroid shows a mononuclear infiltrate with germinal centers and atrophic follicles. Diagnosis?
back:
• Hashimoto thyroiditis
• Most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions
• Characterized by progressive autoimmune-mediated thyroid failure

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: How does the immune system carry out follicular destruction via antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) in Hashimoto thyroiditis?
back:
• Antithyroid antibodies (anti-thyroglobulin/anti-TPO) bind to follicular cells
• Natural Killer (NK) cells bind to the Fc portion of these antibodies
• NK cells then release cytotoxic granules to kill the thyroid cells

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: Contrast the extent of fibrosis in Hashimoto thyroiditis versus Riedel thyroiditis.
back:
• Hashimoto: Fibrosis is present but remains confined within the thyroid capsule
• Riedel: Fibrosis is extensive and invades adjacent neck structures (IgG4-related)
• Hashimoto presents as firm; Riedel presents as "hard and fixed"

category: Hashimoto Thyroiditis ii
front: What are the two most common autoantibodies detected in the serum of patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis?
back:
• Antithyroglobulin antibodies
• Antithyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies
• Present in the vast majority of patients

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, high levels of circulating free T3 and T4 exert negative feedback on the anterior pituitary, resulting in a characteristically [___] serum TSH level.
back:
• Low (suppressed)
• High T3/T4 typically suppresses TSH to <0.1 mU/L in primary gland hyperfunction.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 35-year-old female presents with weight loss, heat intolerance, and diffuse thyroid enlargement. Labs show high free T4 and suppressed TSH. Radioactive iodine scan shows diffuse, symmetric increased uptake. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Graves Disease
• The most common cause of endogenous primary hyperthyroidism
• Caused by Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulins (TSI) activating TSH receptors.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
coreConcept: Pathophysiology of TSH elevation in primary hypothyroidism
front: Explain the role of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis in elevating TSH levels during primary hypothyroidism (e.g., Hashimoto thyroiditis).
back:
• Thyroid failure reduces circulating T3/T4.
• This removes negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary.
• The pituitary increases TSH production to compensate for the hormone deficit.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the laboratory findings (TSH and Free T4) of primary hyperthyroidism with secondary (central) hyperthyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High Free T4 with suppressed (Low) TSH.
• Secondary: High Free T4 with elevated (High) or inappropriately normal TSH.
• Secondary is usually caused by a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three common iatrogenic causes of primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Total or subtotal surgical thyroidectomy.
• Radioactive iodine (I-131) ablation for hyperthyroidism.
• External neck irradiation (e.g., for head and neck malignancies).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The single most sensitive clinical screening test for diagnosing both subclinical and overt primary thyroid dysfunction is the measurement of serum [___].
back:
• TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone)
• TSH levels change significantly before free T3/T4 levels fall outside the normal range.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A neonate presents with a protruding tongue, coarse facial features, and umbilical hernia. This condition, termed cretinism, is most commonly caused by [___] in undeveloped global regions.
back:
• Endemic dietary iodine deficiency
• Results in severe T3/T4 deficiency during critical fetal and neonatal brain development.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the mechanism causing 'Thyroid Storm' in patients with underlying Graves disease.
back:
• Abrupt surge in circulating thyroid hormones.
• Triggered by acute stress (infection, trauma, or surgery).
• Results in massive sympathetic overactivity and catecholamine elevation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the most common etiology of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient vs. iodine-deficient geographic regions.
back:
• Iodine-sufficient: Hashimoto thyroiditis (autoimmune).
• Iodine-deficient: Endemic dietary iodine deficiency.
• Both result in low T3/T4 and high TSH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate three causes of thyrotoxicosis that are not associated with hyperthyroidism (glandular hyperfunction).
back:
• Factitious thyrotoxicosis (exogenous T4 intake).
• Struma ovarii (ectopic thyroid in ovarian teratoma).
• Subacute thyroiditis (leakage of preformed hormone due to inflammation).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum level of [___] is characteristically suppressed due to the sensitivity of the pituitary to negative feedback.
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• Suppression occurs despite elevated circulating free T3 and T4 levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 35-year-old female presents with heat intolerance, tremors, and diffuse thyroid enlargement. Labs show high free T4 and low TSH. Name the most likely autoimmune cause and its specific stimulating antibody.
back:
• Graves Disease
• Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)
• TSI binds to and activates the TSH receptor, mimicking its effect.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the role of the hypothalamus-pituitary axis in producing elevated TSH levels during primary hypothyroidism (e.g., Hashimoto thyroiditis).
back:
• Loss of negative feedback
• Decreased T3/T4 triggers the hypothalamus to release TRH
• Pituitary thyrotrophs increase TSH to stimulate the failing thyroid.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the thyroid function test profile (TSH and T4) of secondary hyperthyroidism with that of the more common primary form.
back:
• Primary: Low TSH; High T4 (Thyroid autonomy)
• Secondary: High TSH; High T4 (Pituitary-driven, e.g., adenoma)
• Secondary is extremely rare.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate the three most frequent causes of endogenous thyrotoxicosis associated with actual hyperfunction of the thyroid gland.
back:
• Graves Disease (Diffuse hyperplasia)
• Hyperfunctioning ("toxic") multinodular goiter
• Hyperfunctioning ("toxic") adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Worldwide, the primary environmental cause of endemic goiter and associated hypothyroidism is [___] deficiency.
back:
• Dietary Iodine
• Impairs hormone synthesis, leading to compensatory TSH-induced gland hypertrophy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient with a history of Sheehan syndrome presents with lethargy and bradycardia. Labs reveal low free T4 and inappropriately low TSH. Identify the category of hypothyroidism.
back:
• Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism
• Caused by pituitary or hypothalamic failure
• Distinguishable from primary by the lack of TSH elevation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the physiological scenario leading to "T3 Toxicosis" and its typical laboratory findings.
back:
• High serum T3 and low TSH, but normal free T4
• Occurs when the thyroid preferentially secretes triiodothyronine
• Requires direct T3 measurement for diagnosis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Distinguish between primary and secondary hypothyroidism based solely on the serum TSH response to low circulating T4.
back:
• Primary: Elevated TSH (Intact pituitary axis responding to low T4)
• Secondary: Low/Normal TSH (Defective pituitary/hypothalamus failing to stimulate thyroid).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three distinct iatrogenic causes that commonly result in primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Surgical thyroidectomy
• Radioactive iodine ablation (for Graves/cancers)
• Drugs (e.g., Lithium, Propylthiouracil, Amiodarone).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum laboratory profile typically reveals elevated levels of free T3 and T4 accompanied by a [___] level of serum Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH).
back:
• Low (suppressed) TSH.
• This results from negative feedback inhibition on the anterior pituitary by excess circulating thyroid hormones.
• It is the most sensitive screening finding for hyperthyroidism.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 35-year-old male presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, and a diffuse goiter. Labs show elevated Free T4 and inappropriately high-normal serum TSH. The most likely underlying cause is [___].
back:
• TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (Secondary hyperthyroidism).
• Unlike primary hyperthyroidism, the pituitary fails to respond to negative feedback.
• Results in over-stimulation of the thyroid gland by excess TSH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the role of the TRH stimulation test in distinguishing between pituitary and hypothalamic causes of secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• A rise in TSH after TRH administration suggests a hypothalamic cause (failure to release TRH).
• Absence of TSH response suggests a pituitary cause (anterior pituitary failure).
• Both present with low TSH and low Free T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the diagnostic Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU) and serum Thyroglobulin levels in Graves disease versus factitious thyrotoxicosis.
back:
• Graves Disease: Diffusely increased RAIU; elevated Thyroglobulin levels.
• Factitious Thyrotoxicosis: Decreased (suppressed) RAIU; low/undetectable Thyroglobulin levels.
• Both present with high Free T4 and suppressed TSH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate three common iatrogenic (treatment-related) causes of primary hypothyroidism in clinical practice.
back:
• Surgical thyroidectomy (total or subtotal).
• Radioiodine (I-131) ablation therapy for Graves disease.
• External beam radiation to the neck (e.g., for lymphoma).
• Antithyroid drugs (Propylthiouracil, Methimazole).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Neonatal hypothyroidism resulting from thyroid agenesis or inborn errors of thyroid metabolism, characterized by severe intellectual disability and short stature, is termed [___].
back:
• Cretinism.
• Labs show low T3/T4 and high TSH.
• Occurs if maternal thyroid hormone deficiency is present early in pregnancy before fetal gland development.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient undergoing psychiatric treatment with Lithium presents with cold intolerance and constipation. Labs show a TSH of 15 mIU/L (High) and Free T4 of 0.5 ng/dL (Low). Describe the underlying etiology.
back:
• Drug-induced primary hypothyroidism.
• Lithium interferes with thyroid hormone synthesis and release.
• Amiodarone and p-aminosalicylic acid are other common pharmacological causes.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the mechanism by which 'Toxic Multinodular Goiter' (Plummer Syndrome) leads to autonomous thyroid hormone production.
back:
• Somatic mutations in the TSH receptor (TSHR) or GNAS genes.
• Leads to constitutive activation of cAMP signaling.
• Resulting thyroid nodules function independently of TSH stimulation (thyroid autonomy).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the laboratory feedback loop status (TSH and T4) in Myxedema versus Sheehan Syndrome.
back:
• Myxedema (Primary Hypo): High TSH; Low T4/T3 (due to thyroid gland failure).
• Sheehan Syndrome (Secondary Hypo): Low/Normal TSH; Low T4/T3 (due to pituitary infarction).
• Myxedema features non-pitting edema from glycosaminoglycan accumulation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Which specific dietary substance, common in native African populations, acts as a goitrogen by inhibiting iodide transport within the thyroid?
back:
• Cassava root.
• Contains thiocyanate, which blocks the sodium-iodide symporter.
• Leads to decreased T4 synthesis, compensatory TSH rise, and diffuse nontoxic (colloid) goiter.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In secondary hyperthyroidism caused by a rare TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma, the serum level of TSH is typically [___].
back:
• Elevated or inappropriately normal.
• Accompanied by high Free T4 and T3 levels.
• Contrasts with primary hyperthyroidism where TSH is suppressed.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 40-year-old female presents with palpitations and heat intolerance. Labs show low TSH and high Free T4. A radionuclide scan reveals a solitary 'hot' nodule with suppression of the rest of the gland. Identify the likely cause.
back:
• Toxic Adenoma (Functional Follicular Adenoma).
• Pathophysiology: Somatic activating mutations in TSHR or GNAS.
• Result: Autonomous thyroid hormone production independent of TSH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the role of the negative feedback loop in why serum TSH is the most sensitive screening tool for primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Low T3/T4 levels trigger the anterior pituitary to increase TSH secretion.
• TSH rises logarithmically even before Free T4 falls below normal range.
• Elevated TSH confirms intrinsic thyroid gland failure.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the serum TSH and Free T4 levels in primary hypothyroidism versus secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH, Low Free T4 (e.g., Hashimoto's).
• Secondary: Low or inappropriately Normal TSH, Low Free T4 (e.g., Pituitary failure).
• Differentiation distinguishes thyroidal from hypothalamic-pituitary pathology.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate the three most common clinical disorders associated with endogenous hyperthyroidism resulting from glandular hyperfunction.
back:
• Graves Disease (Diffuse toxic hyperplasia).
• Toxic Multinodular Goiter (Plummer syndrome).
• Toxic Adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The most common cause of congenital hypothyroidism worldwide, often resulting in clinical cretinism, is [___].
back:
• Endemic Iodine Deficiency.
• Leads to impaired T3/T4 synthesis in utero or early infancy.
• Characterized by intellectual disability and short stature.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient presents with thyrotoxicosis symptoms but labs show low Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU). Identify the two likely inflammatory causes and the mechanism of hormone elevation.
back:
• Subacute Granulomatous (de Quervain) and Subacute Lymphocytic Thyroiditis.
• Mechanism: Leakage of preformed hormone from damaged follicles.
• Not due to new hormone synthesis (hyperfunction).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the triphasic thyroid function profile typically observed in the clinical course of subacute thyroiditis.
back:
• Phase 1: Thyrotoxicosis (High T4, Low TSH) due to follicle rupture.
• Phase 2: Transient Hypothyroidism (Low T4, High TSH) due to hormone depletion.
• Phase 3: Euthyroid state (Normal T4/TSH) upon recovery.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the pathogenesis of Endemic Goiter with that of Sporadic Goiter regarding the underlying cause of TSH elevation.
back:
• Endemic: Lack of dietary iodine in a geographic region.
• Sporadic: Ingestion of goitrogens (e.g., cassava, cabbage) or hereditary biosynthetic defects.
• Both: Compensatory TSH rise causes follicular hypertrophy/hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the primary medical interventions and conditions that result in iatrogenic hypothyroidism.
back:
• Surgical thyroidectomy (total or subtotal).
• Radioiodine (I-131) ablation for Graves or cancer.
• External neck radiation.
• Drugs: Lithium or antithyroid medications (Propylthiouracil).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum level of [___] is typically suppressed due to the negative feedback exerted by elevated free T3 and T4.
back:
• Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH).
• Elevated free hormones inhibit thyrotrophs in the anterior pituitary.
• This is the most sensitive early indicator of thyrotoxicosis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 40-year-old female presents with cold intolerance, weight gain, and a diffuse goiter. Lab tests show elevated TSH and low free T4. Identify the most likely autoimmune diagnosis and the characteristic antibodies involved.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
• Antithyroglobulin and Antithyroid Peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies.
• It is the leading cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the hormonal feedback loop mechanism that distinguishes secondary (central) hyperthyroidism from primary hyperthyroidism.
back:
• Primary: Excess thyroid-derived T3/T4 suppresses TSH secretion via negative feedback (Low TSH).
• Secondary: Pituitary adenoma autonomously secretes TSH, which drives T3/T4 synthesis (High TSH).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the laboratory findings (TSH and T4) and iodine uptake patterns of Graves disease with those of subacute (painless) lymphocytic thyroiditis.
back:
• Graves: Low TSH, High T4, and Diffuse High Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU).
• Thyroiditis: Low TSH, High T4 (leakage phase), but Low RAIU due to gland damage.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List the three primary causes of endogenous hyperthyroidism associated with hyperfunction of the thyroid gland.
back:
• Graves disease (diffuse toxic hyperplasia).
• Toxic multinodular goiter (Plummer syndrome).
• Hyperfunctioning (toxic) adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Hypothyroidism developing in infancy or early childhood that leads to severe intellectual disability and short stature is termed [___].
back:
• Cretinism.
• Caused by endemic iodine deficiency or congenital biosynthetic defects (dyshormonogenetic goiter).
• Thyroid hormone is critical for early brain development.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient with a history of Sheehan syndrome presents with lethargy and bradycardia. Labs reveal low TSH and low T4. Define this condition's classification and its primary anatomical origin.
back:
• Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism.
• Anatomical Origin: Anterior Pituitary (adenohypophysis).
• Results from TSH deficiency due to postpartum pituitary ischemic necrosis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe how iodine-induced hyperthyroidism (Jod-Basedow phenomenon) occurs in a patient with a preexisting long-standing goiter.
back:
• Occurs when iodine is administered to patients with iodine-deficient goiters.
• Preexisting autonomous nodules utilize iodine to synthesize excess T3/T4, bypassing pituitary regulation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Differentiate the expected serum TSH and free T4 levels in subclinical hypothyroidism versus overt primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Subclinical: Elevated TSH with Normal free T4.
• Overt: Elevated TSH with Low free T4.
• Subclinical status indicates mild thyroid failure requiring monitoring.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the single most sensitive screening test for the initial evaluation of both hyperthyroidism and primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Serum TSH (Thyrotropin) concentration.
• Minute changes in free thyroid hormones produce logarithmic changes in TSH levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum level of [___] is characteristically suppressed due to the negative feedback effect of elevated circulating Free T4 and T3.
back:
- TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone)
- Suppressed due to high T3/T4 feedback on pituitary thyrotrophs.
- This is the most sensitive screening test for diagnosing hyperthyroidism.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 40-year-old female presents with palpitations, tremors, and exophthalmos. Lab results show TSH <0.01 mIU/L and high Free T4. Identify the most common underlying cause.
back:
- Graves Disease
- Caused by thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) activating TSH receptors.
- Characterized by diffuse thyroid hyperplasia and low TSH.
- It is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the physiological mechanism by which chronic dietary iodine deficiency leads to the development of a diffuse nontoxic goiter.
back:
- Reduced iodine decreases T3/T4 synthesis.
- Low T4 triggers increased pituitary TSH secretion via loss of feedback.
- Elevated TSH causes follicular hypertrophy and hyperplasia, enlarging the gland.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the laboratory thyroid profile (TSH and Free T4) of primary hypothyroidism with that of secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
- Primary: Elevated TSH with Low Free T4 (e.g., Hashimoto thyroiditis).
- Secondary: Low or inappropriately Normal TSH with Low Free T4 (Pituitary failure).
- Primary results from intrinsic thyroid gland failure.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three common iatrogenic causes that lead to a state of primary hypothyroidism.
back:
- Total or subtotal surgical thyroidectomy.
- Radioiodine (I-131) ablation for hyperthyroidism.
- External beam radiation therapy to the neck for malignancies.
- These lead to permanent, primary thyroid hormone deficiency.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In the early phase of [___], thyrotoxicosis occurs not from hormone overproduction, but from the viral-induced inflammatory destruction of follicles and subsequent hormone leakage.
back:
- Granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
- Transient thyrotoxicosis results from follicle leakage, not overproduction.
- Transient state followed by recovery to euthyroidism in weeks.
- Usually triggered by a viral infection.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A child from a mountain region presents with coarse facial features, short stature, and severe intellectual disability. This intrauterine-onset primary hypothyroidism is called [___].
back:
- Cretinism.
- Results from iodine deficiency or dyshormonogenetic goiter.
- Laboratory findings: Markedly high TSH and Low Free T4.
- Protruding tongue and umbilical hernia are common clinical signs.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the mechanism of 'Hashitoxicosis' seen during the initial clinical stages of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis.
back:
- Inflammation causes follicular rupture and release of stored T3/T4.
- Results in transient high Free T4 and suppressed TSH.
- Eventually progresses to permanent hypothyroidism as parenchymal destruction continues.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Distinguish between 'Toxic Multinodular Goiter' and a 'TSH-secreting Pituitary Adenoma' based on serum TSH levels and thyroid scan findings.
back:
- Toxic Multinodular Goiter: Low TSH; Scan shows multiple 'hot' autonomous nodules.
- TSH Adenoma: High/Normal TSH; Scan shows diffusely increased iodine uptake.
- TSH Adenoma is a rare secondary cause.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the hormone levels characteristic of 'Subclinical Hypothyroidism'.
back:
- Elevated serum TSH level.
- Normal serum Free T4 and Free T3 levels.
- Often represents the earliest compensatory stage of thyroid failure.
- Patients are typically asymptomatic or have vague fatigue.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most frequent underlying cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, accounting for 85% to 95% of cases, is a solitary sporadic [___].
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma
• Characteristically solitary and well-circumscribed
• Composed mostly of uniform chief cells
• Often associated with a thin fibrous capsule

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 50-year-old female presents with recurrent renal calculi, bone pain, and fatigue. Labs show hypercalcemia and elevated serum Parathyroid Hormone (PTH). Identify the most likely underlying diagnosis.
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism
• Classic triad: 'stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans'
• Usually caused by autonomous PTH overproduction
• Results in increased osteoclast activity and renal calcium reabsorption

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
coreConcept: Mechanism of Humoral Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
front: Explain the role of Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP) in the development of hypercalcemia associated with malignancy.
back:
• Secreted ectopically by solid tumors (e.g., squamous cell lung cancer)
• Mimics PTH by binding to the same receptors
• Increases osteoclastic bone resorption
• Reduces renal calcium excretion; suppresses endogenous PTH

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
coreConcept: Differential Lab Contrast in Parathyroid Disorders
front: Contrast the biochemical lab profiles of Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Secondary Hyperparathyroidism regarding serum Calcium and Phosphate.
back:
• Primary: High serum Calcium; Low or normal Phosphate
• Secondary: Low or normal serum Calcium; High Phosphate (usually due to renal failure)
• Both show elevated serum PTH levels

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the most common non-parathyroid causes of hypercalcemia encountered in clinical practice.
back:
• Malignancy (most common symptomatic cause)
• Vitamin D toxicity
• Sarcoidosis (via macrophage activation of Vitamin D)
• Thiazide diuretics or prolonged immobilization

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The primary genetic defect in Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome type 1 (APS-1), which presents with hypoparathyroidism, candidiasis, and adrenal insufficiency, involves mutations in the [___] gene.
back:
• AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator)
• Results in failure of central T-cell tolerance
• Leads to immune destruction of endocrine organs
• Typically presents in childhood or adolescence

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with long-standing chronic renal failure presents with secondary hyperparathyroidism. If the parathyroid glands eventually become autonomous and hypercalcemia develops, the condition is termed [___].
back:
• Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
• Represents autonomous gland function after long-term reactive hyperplasia
• Often requires surgical parathyroidectomy
• Associated with extremely high PTH and high Calcium

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: How does chronic renal failure serve as a stimulus for the development of secondary hyperparathyroidism?
back:
• Hyperphosphatemia: Directly depresses serum Calcium
• Vitamin D deficiency: Reduced renal alpha-1-hydroxylase activity
• Low Calcium: Triggers compensatory PTH secretion to restore homeostasis
• Leads to diffuse parathyroid chief cell hyperplasia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Distinguish between hypoparathyroidism and pseudohypoparathyroidism based on serum PTH levels and hormonal response.
back:
• Hypoparathyroidism: Low PTH levels; usually iatrogenic or autoimmune
• Pseudohypoparathyroidism: Normal or High PTH; end-organ resistance to PTH
• Both manifest with hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the most frequent clinical cause of acquired hypoparathyroidism.
back:
• Iatrogenic (surgical) removal
• Occurs during thyroidectomy or radical neck dissection
• Inadvertent damage or removal of all four glands
• Presents acutely with tetany and neuromuscular irritability

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum level of TSH is characteristically [___] due to the negative feedback effect of elevated free T4 and T3.
back:
• Low (suppressed).
• T3 and T4 levels are elevated.
• Measurement of TSH is the most sensitive screening test for early disease.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 52-year-old female presents with mental sluggishness, cold intolerance, and weight gain. Biopsy shows atrophic follicles lined by eosinophilic Hürthle cells and prominent germinal centers. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis.
• The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas.
• High TSH and low T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the role of Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) in the pathogenesis of Graves disease.
back:
• TSI is an IgG autoantibody.
• It binds to the TSH receptor, mimicking TSH action.
• It stimulates adenyl cyclase, leading to autonomous overproduction of T3 and T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the hormone profiles of primary hypothyroidism with secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH, Low T4/T3 (Intrinsic gland failure).
• Secondary: Low/normal TSH, Low T4/T3 (Pituitary or hypothalamic failure).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List the classic clinical triad used to define Graves disease.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism (diffuse goiter).
• Infiltrative ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos).
• Localized dermopathy (pretibial myxedema).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Hypothyroidism developing in infancy or early childhood, resulting in severe intellectual disability and short stature, is termed [___].
back:
• Cretinism.
• Causes: Endemic iodine deficiency or inborn metabolic errors (dyshormonogenetic goiter).
• Features: Coarse facial features, protruding tongue, and umbilical hernia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient presents with tachycardia, moist skin, and a wide staring gaze (lid lag). If a radioiodine scan shows a single localized 'hot' nodule, the underlying cause is [___].
back:
• Toxic Adenoma.
• Characterized by autonomous thyroid hormone production.
• TSH is suppressed; free T4/T3 are elevated.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the physiological mechanism causing diffuse nontoxic (colloid) goiter in areas of low dietary iodine.
back:
• Low iodine leads to decreased T3/T4 synthesis.
• Lack of feedback causes a compensatory rise in TSH.
• Elevated TSH induces follicular cell hypertrophy and hyperplasia, enlarging the gland.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the concepts of hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis regarding their definitions.
back:
• Hyperthyroidism: Hypermetabolic state due to thyroid gland hyperfunction.
• Thyrotoxicosis: Hypermetabolic state due to elevated circulating free T3/T4 from any source (e.g., inflammation or exogenous intake).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the cause of 'apathetic hyperthyroidism' and its typical demographic.
back:
• Thyrotoxicosis where typical signs are blunted.
• Seen in older adults.
• Presents with unexplained weight loss or worsening cardiovascular disease.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, accounting for 85% to 95% of cases, is a solitary [___].
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma.
• Usually presents as a sporadic, well-circumscribed nodule.
• Associated with Cyclin D1 gene inversions or MEN1 mutations.
• Glands outside the adenoma are typically normal or shrunken.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with recurrent nephrolithiasis, bone pain, and constipation. Laboratory results show hypercalcemia and an inappropriately high serum PTH. Identify the most likely underlying diagnosis.
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism.
• Classically presents as "painful bones, renal stones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans."
• The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia.
• Typically caused by an autonomous parathyroid adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) in the renal handling of calcium and phosphate to maintain homeostasis.
back:
• Increases renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.
• Increases urinary phosphate excretion (lowering serum phosphate).
• Stimulates renal alpha-1-hydroxylase to activate Vitamin D.
• These actions raise serum ionized calcium levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the skeletal pathology of "osteitis fibrosa cystica" in primary hyperparathyroidism with the "calciphylaxis" seen in secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica: Characterized by subperiosteal bone resorption, "dissecting osteitis," and hemosiderin-laden "brown tumors."
• Calciphylaxis: Ischemic skin/organ damage due to widespread vascular calcification from secondary hyperparathyroidism, usually in chronic renal failure.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the top three causes of hypercalcemia in adults, specifically distinguishing the most common symptomatic cause.
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism (most common cause overall).
• Malignancy (most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia).
• Vitamin D toxicity or Sarcoidosis (granulomatous disease).
• Malignancy usually acts via PTH-related protein (PTHrP).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In the setting of chronic renal failure, the compensatory hypersecretion of PTH in response to prolonged hypocalcemia is termed [___].
back:
• Secondary hyperparathyroidism.
• Driven by hyperphosphatemia and decreased active Vitamin D.
• Results in diffuse hyperplasia of all four parathyroid glands.
• Often leads to renal osteodystrophy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient presents with circumoral paresthesias and carpopedal spasms following a radical neck dissection. Physical exam reveals a positive Trousseau sign. Explain the physiological basis of these findings.
back:
• Acquired hypoparathyroidism.
• Inadvertent removal of parathyroid glands during surgery.
• Low PTH leads to severe hypocalcemia.
• Hypocalcemia causes neuromuscular irritability (tetany).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the molecular pathogenesis and serum PTH profile of Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia (FHH).
back:
• Autosomal dominant loss-of-function mutation in CASR (calcium-sensing receptor).
• Decreased sensitivity to calcium in parathyroid and kidneys.
• Results in inappropriately high PTH levels despite hypercalcemia.
• Characterized by low urinary calcium excretion.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the biochemical serum PTH findings in primary hyperparathyroidism versus hypercalcemia associated with metastatic bone disease.
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: PTH is inappropriately high or high-normal relative to elevated calcium.
• Metastatic Bone Disease: PTH is suppressed (low) due to negative feedback from hypercalcemia.
• PTHrP may be elevated in non-metastatic malignancy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the genetic mutation associated with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1) and its classic triad of manifestations.
back:
• Mutation in AIRE (autoimmune regulator) gene.
• Triad: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, ectodermal dystrophy, and autoimmune hypoparathyroidism.
• Involves failure of central T-cell tolerance.
• Leads to autoantibodies against IL-17 and IL-22.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In primary hyperthyroidism, the serum TSH level is characteristically [___] due to negative feedback, while in rare TSH-secreting pituitary adenomas (secondary), TSH is [___].
back:
• TSH: Decreased (suppressed)
• TSH: Normal or Elevated
• Key: High levels of Free T4/T3 are present in both variants.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 50-year-old female presents with cold intolerance, weight gain, and a firm, enlarged thyroid. In iodine-sufficient regions like Pakistan, the most common cause of this hormonal profile is [___].
back:
• Diagnosis: Hashimoto Thyroiditis
• Mechanism: Autoimmune destruction of thyroid follicles
• Labs: High TSH, Low Free T3/T4

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the role of the pituitary-thyroid axis in the hormonal profile of secondary hyperthyroidism caused by a thyrotroph adenoma.
back:
• TSH: Elevated (autonomous pituitary secretion)
• T3/T4: Elevated (stimulated by high TSH)
• Feedback: Loss of normal T3/T4 negative feedback inhibition on pituitary.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the typical laboratory findings of TSH and Free T4 in primary hypothyroidism with secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH, Low Free T4 (Thyroid failure)
• Secondary: Low or Normal TSH, Low Free T4 (Pituitary/Hypothalamic failure)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the primary hormone levels and clinical status associated with 'subclinical' hyperthyroidism.
back:
• TSH Level: Decreased (suppressed)
• Free T4/T3: Within normal reference ranges
• Symptoms: Often asymptomatic; identified during routine screening.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Hypothyroidism in infancy resulting in severe intellectual disability and protruding tongue is termed [___], most commonly caused by [___] in endemic regions.
back:
• Term: Cretinism
• Cause: Dietary iodine deficiency
• Labs: Elevated TSH, Low T4

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient presents with tachycardia and weight loss. TSH is low, but Free T4 is normal. Identify the likely clinical variant and the next diagnostic lab to order.
back:
• Variant: T3 Toxicosis
• Lab: Serum Total/Free T3 measurement
• Hormone Profile: Low TSH, Normal T4, High T3

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the mechanism by which 'hot' nodules on radioiodine scintigraphy affect TSH levels and overall thyroid function.
back:
• Mechanism: Autonomous hormone production independent of TSH
• TSH Level: Low (suppressed by excess T3/T4)
• Thyroid Function: Hyperthyroidism (e.g., toxic adenoma)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the cause of hyperthyroidism in Graves disease with that of toxic multinodular goiter (Plummer Syndrome).
back:
• Graves: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) activating TSH receptors
• Plummer: Somatic activating mutations in TSHR or GNAS
• Levels: Both show Low TSH, High T3/T4

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify three common iatrogenic causes that lead to the development of primary hypothyroidism.
back:
• Surgical ablation (total thyroidectomy)
• Radioactive iodine therapy (I-131)
• Drugs: Lithium or antithyroid medications (e.g., methimazole)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
coreConcept: Etiology and Lab Findings of Hashimoto Thyroiditis
front: The most common cause of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions like Pakistan is [___], which biochemically presents with [___] TSH levels.
back:
• Cause: Hashimoto Thyroiditis (Autoimmune)
• TSH Level: Elevated (High)
• Hormone Status: Low serum T4 and T3 due to thyroid parenchymal destruction.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A female patient with a history of severe obstetric hemorrhage (Sheehan syndrome) presents with fatigue and weight gain. Lab results show low Free T4 and low TSH. Identify the category of hypothyroidism and the likely underlying pathology.
back:
• Category: Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism
• Pathology: Pituitary failure results in loss of TSH-mediated stimulus to the thyroid gland.
• Contrast: Unlike primary hypo, TSH is inappropriately low.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the mechanism by which excessive thyroid hormone leads to systemic weight loss despite polyphagia, and specify the TSH status in primary cases.
back:
• Mechanism: Thyroid hormone increases the basal metabolic rate, stimulating excessive catabolism of carbohydrates and lipids.
• TSH Level: Suppressed (Low) in primary hyperthyroidism.
• Result: Caloric demand exceeds intake.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the TSH and T4 levels seen in Hashimoto Thyroiditis with those found in Pituitary-associated Hypothyroidism.
back:
• Hashimoto (Primary): High TSH; Low T4/T3 (Gland is often enlarged/goitrous).
• Pituitary (Secondary): Low or inappropriately normal TSH; Low T4/T3 (Gland is typically atrophic).
• Distinction: TSH elevation confirms intact pituitary-thyroid feedback.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Detail the dual mechanism of action of Propylthiouracil (PTU) in treating severe hyperthyroidism regarding hormone synthesis and conversion.
back:
• Blocks Synthesis: Inhibits the oxidation of iodide and the organification of iodine.
• Peripheral Effect: Inhibits the peripheral deiodination of T4 into the more active T3.
• Result: Decreased TSH-receptor stimulation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In the rare clinical state of 'T3 Toxicosis,' serum levels of [___] are elevated, while [___] levels may remain normal or decreased.
back:
• Triiodothyronine (T3)
• Free Thyroxine (T4)
• TSH: Suppressed/Low (consistent with overall thyrotoxic state).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A newborn presenting with short stature, a protruding tongue, and umbilical hernia is diagnosed with Cretinism. State the expected TSH/T4 profile and the most common worldwide etiology.
back:
• Profile: High TSH; Low T4/T3.
• Etiology: Endemic dietary iodine deficiency (Congenital hypothyroidism).
• Pathophysiology: Impaired T4 synthesis in utero prevents normal brain and skeletal development.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Analyze why heart failure in thyrotoxicosis is often termed 'high-output failure' and specify the typical hormone levels found.
back:
• Mechanism: Increased peripheral oxygen demand and sympathetic tone lead to elevated cardiac output and contractility.
• Hormone Profile: Low TSH; High Free T4.
• Symptoms: Tachycardia, palpitations, and cardiomegaly.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the levels of TSH and T4 found in Primary Hyperthyroidism (e.g., Toxic Adenoma) versus Secondary Hyperthyroidism (e.g., TSH-secreting pituitary tumor).
back:
• Primary: Low (suppressed) TSH; High T4.
• Secondary: High (or inappropriately normal) TSH; High T4.
• Diagnosis: Measurement of TSH is the best differentiator.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Enumerate the three most common causes of endogenous hyperthyroidism and state the resulting TSH levels for these primary causes.
back:
• Causes:
  1. Graves Disease (Diffuse Hyperplasia)
  2. Toxic Multinodular Goiter
  3. Hyperfunctioning (Toxic) Adenoma
• TSH Levels: Consistently Low/Suppressed.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The most sensitive laboratory screening test for the diagnosis of primary hypothyroidism is the measurement of serum [___].
back:
● TSH (Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone)
● TSH levels are increased in primary hypothyroidism due to loss of negative feedback inhibition on the pituitary by T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 45-year-old female presents with cold intolerance, weight gain, and a firm, non-tender symmetrically enlarged thyroid. Laboratory results show High TSH and Low Free T4. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
● Hashimoto Thyroiditis
● It is the most common cause of autoimmune hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the failure of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid feedback loop in primary hyperthyroidism (e.g., Graves disease).
back:
● Autonomous or antibody-induced overproduction of T3/T4 by the thyroid gland.
● High circulating T3/T4 levels act on the pituitary to suppress TSH secretion.
● Result: High T3/T4 with a characteristically low/undetectable TSH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the serum TSH and Free T4 levels between Primary Hypothyroidism and Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism.
back:
● Primary: High TSH; Low Free T4 (Thyroid failure).
● Secondary: Low or inappropriately normal TSH; Low Free T4 (Pituitary/Hypothalamic failure).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List three major causes of thyrotoxicosis associated with hyperfunction (increased radioactive iodine uptake) of the thyroid gland.
back:
● Graves Disease (Diffuse hyperplasia)
● Toxic Multinodular Goiter (Plummer Syndrome)
● Hyperfunctional (Toxic) Adenoma

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In the clinical state of 'T3 Toxicosis,' the laboratory profile typically shows a suppressed TSH, normal Free T4, and elevated [___].
back:
● Serum T3 (Triiodothyronine)
● This occurs when hyperthyroidism is driven primarily by excessive T3 rather than T4 production.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient on long-term Lithium therapy for bipolar disorder develops lethargy and bradycardia. Predict the expected TSH and T4 levels and identify the thyroid status.
back:
● Primary Hypothyroidism
● High TSH; Low Free T4
● Lithium acts as a goitrogen, interfering with thyroid hormone synthesis and release.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism of secondary (pituitary-associated) hyperthyroidism.
back:
● Usually caused by a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
● Pituitary autonomously secretes TSH, bypassing normal negative feedback from thyroid hormones.
● Profile: High/Normal TSH with High Free T4/T3.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the hormone levels of Primary Hyperthyroidism with the profile of Secondary (Pituitary) Hyperthyroidism.
back:
● Primary: Low TSH; High Free T4.
● Secondary: High TSH; High Free T4.
● Both present with clinical features of thyrotoxicosis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Identify the most common cause of hypothyroidism globally and the corresponding TSH level expected in an adult.
back:
● Dietary Iodine Deficiency
● Elevated TSH (Compensatory increase due to lack of T4/T3 synthesis).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, accounting for 85% to 95% of cases, is a solitary [___].
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma
• Usually composed of uniform, polygonal chief cells
• Often separated from a rim of normal tissue by a delicate fibrous capsule

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and osteopenia. Labs show hypercalcemia and inappropriately elevated PTH. Identify the most likely underlying genetic alterations if this is a sporadic parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Overexpression of Cyclin D1 (CCDN1) due to gene inversion
• Somatic mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene
• Both lead to autonomous chief cell proliferation

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the skeletal mechanism of "dissecting osteitis" induced by excessive parathyroid hormone (PTH).
back:
• Activated osteoclasts tunnel centrally along the length of medullary bone trabeculae
• Creates a characteristic "railroad track" appearance
• Marrow spaces are replaced by fibrovascular tissue

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the laboratory profiles of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) in primary hyperparathyroidism versus hypercalcemia of malignancy.
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Elevated PTH; Low/Undetectable PTHrP
• Hypercalcemia of Malignancy: Low/Undetectable PTH; Elevated PTHrP (in ~80% of cases)
• PTHrP mimics PTH to induce osteoclastic bone resorption

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the components of the classic morphologic triad seen in severe, untreated primary hyperparathyroidism (Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica).
back:
• Osteoporosis (decreased bone mass)
• Brown tumors (hemosiderin-laden reactive masses)
• Peritrabecular fibrosis and cystic bone changes

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In the setting of chronic renal failure, hypocalcemia leads to compensatory overactivity of the parathyroid glands, a condition termed [___].
back:
• Secondary hyperparathyroidism
• Caused by hyperphosphatemia and decreased active Vitamin D (1,25-(OH)2D)
• Characterized by multiglandular parathyroid hyperplasia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 10-year-old child presents with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and new-onset tetany. Labs reveal hypocalcemia and low PTH. Identify the likely mutation and syndrome.
back:
• Mutation: AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene
• Syndrome: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1)
• Features: Hypoparathyroidism, Adrenal insufficiency, and candidiasis

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which inactivating mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor (CASR) lead to familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
back:
• Reduces parathyroid sensitivity to extracellular calcium
• Requires abnormally high serum calcium to suppress PTH secretion
• Leads to increased renal calcium reabsorption and asymptomatic hypercalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Distinguish between the Chvostek sign and Trousseau sign in the clinical evaluation of hypocalcemia.
back:
• Chvostek: Facial muscle twitching elicited by tapping the facial nerve
• Trousseau: Carpal spasm induced by inflating a blood pressure cuff above systolic
• Both indicate neuromuscular irritability due to low ionized calcium

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Specify the most frequent iatrogenic cause of acquired hypoparathyroidism.
back:
• Inadvertent removal of parathyroid glands during thyroidectomy
• Also occurs during radical neck dissection for malignancies
• Results in acute hypocalcemia, tetany, and potential laryngospasm

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common gene mutation in sporadic parathyroid adenomas, involving a pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11, leads to the overexpression of [___].
back: - Cyclin D1 (CCDN1). - Acts as a major regulator of the cell cycle. - Leads to autonomous chief cell proliferation and parathyroid enlargement.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 65-year-old male smoker with a lung mass presents with lethargy, constipation, and a serum calcium of 14 mg/dL. His PTH is low. Identify the likely mediator of his hypercalcemia.
back: - PTH-related peptide (PTHrP). - Secreted ectopically by tumors (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma). - Mimics PTH action on bone and kidney, causing hypercalcemia of malignancy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the physiological role of phosphate retention in the pathogenesis of secondary hyperparathyroidism during chronic renal failure.
back: - Hyperphosphatemia directly depresses serum ionized calcium levels. - It also inhibits renal alpha-1-hydroxylase, decreasing active Vitamin D (calcitriol). - Both factors stimulate compensatory PTH secretion and parathyroid hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast Primary Hyperparathyroidism with Secondary Hyperparathyroidism regarding serum calcium levels, phosphate levels, and the underlying state of the parathyroid glands.
back: - Primary: Hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, autonomous (adenoma/hyperplasia). - Secondary: Hypocalcemia or normocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia (in renal failure), compensatory hyperplasia. - Primary is a source of hypercalcemia; Secondary is a reaction to hypocalcemia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the clinical findings associated with the 'Psychic Moans' and 'Abdominal Groans' in symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism.
back: - Psychic Moans: Depression, lethargy, and central nervous system disturbances. - Abdominal Groans: Constipation, nausea, peptic ulcers, gallstones, and pancreatitis. - These reflect the systemic effects of chronic hypercalcemia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The syndrome of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN-1) is characterized by a germline mutation in the [___] gene, typically presenting with the '3 Ps'.
back: - MEN1 (encodes Menin). - 3 Ps: Parathyroid (hyperplasia/adenoma), Pancreas (PanNETs), and Pituitary (adenoma). - Parathyroid involvement is the most frequent and earliest clinical manifestation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 10-year-old child presents with tetany and chronic fungal infections of the skin. Laboratory tests confirm hypocalcemia and adrenal insufficiency. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back: - Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1). - Caused by AIRE gene mutations. - Characterized by the triad: Hypoparathyroidism, Addison disease, and Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the transition of parathyroid glands from a reactive state to an autonomous state in the development of tertiary hyperparathyroidism.
back: - Occurs after long-standing secondary hyperparathyroidism (usually renal failure). - Chronic overstimulation leads to parathyroid clones that proliferate independently of calcium levels. - Results in hypercalcemia that persists even after renal transplantation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the inheritance and urinary calcium excretion patterns of Primary Hyperparathyroidism with Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia (FHH).
