back: - Primary: Mostly sporadic, high urinary calcium excretion. - FHH: Autosomal dominant (CASR mutation), low urinary calcium (hypocalciuria). - FHH involves a higher 'set-point' for calcium sensing rather than tumor growth.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List three skeletal abnormalities classically associated with the 'Painful Bones' of severe, untreated primary hyperparathyroidism.
back: - Osteoporosis (decreased bone mass). - Brown Tumors (hemosiderin-laden cystic lesions). - Osteitis fibrosa cystica (peritrabecular fibrosis and bone loss). - Often presents with bone pain and pathological fractures.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In approximately 80% of patients with hypercalcemia of malignancy, the elevation in serum calcium is caused by the extra-glandular secretion of [___].
back:
* Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP)
* Mimics PTH action on bone and kidneys
* Commonly associated with solid tumors (lung, breast, renal carcinoma)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 40-year-old female post-thyroidectomy develops circumoral tingling and carpal spasms upon blood pressure cuff inflation. These signs of neuromuscular irritability indicate [___].
back:
* Hypocalcemia due to acquired hypoparathyroidism
* Result of accidental surgical removal/injury to parathyroid glands
* Presents with Chvostek and Trousseau signs

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the serum Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) and phosphate profile that distinguishes primary hyperparathyroidism from hypercalcemia caused by Vitamin D toxicity.
back:
* Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Elevated PTH and low serum phosphate (phosphaturia).
* Vitamin D Toxicity: Suppressed (low) PTH and elevated or normal phosphate.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the typical gross involvement of the parathyroid glands in a sporadic solitary adenoma versus secondary hyperparathyroidism from chronic renal failure.
back:
* Solitary Adenoma: Single enlarged gland (tan/red-brown nodule); remaining three glands are usually atrophic.
* Secondary Hyperparathyroidism: All four glands show symmetric or asymmetric diffuse/multinodular hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the three interrelated skeletal abnormalities that define von Recklinghausen disease of bone (severe primary hyperparathyroidism).
back:
* Generalized osteoporosis (reduced bone mass)
* Brown tumors (fibrovascular masses with hemorrhage)
* Osteitis fibrosa cystica (peritrabecular fibrosis and cystic degeneration)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common and often earliest clinical manifestation of the autosomal dominant syndrome [___], caused by mutations on chromosome 11q13.
back:
* Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia, type 1 (MEN-1)
* Characterized by the "three Ps": Parathyroid, Pancreas, and Pituitary abnormalities
* Involves multiglandular hyperplasia or adenomas

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old male with long-standing renal failure presents with bone pain and high serum phosphate. Describe the initial trigger for parathyroid hyperfunction in this scenario.
back:
* Chronic hyperphosphatemia lowers serum calcium directly.
* Reduced renal conversion of Vitamin D to its active form (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D).
* Resultant hypocalcemia causes compensatory parathyroid hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the biochemical and molecular basis for the diagnosis of Pseudohypoparathyroidism.
back:
* Biochemistry: Low calcium and high phosphate, but inappropriately high PTH.
* Basis: End-organ resistance to PTH signaling (often G-protein defects).
* Contrast: Differs from true hypoparathyroidism where PTH is low.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the effects of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) and Calcitonin on osteoclast activity and renal tubular handling of calcium.
back:
* PTH: Stimulates osteoclast differentiation (bone resorption) and increases renal calcium reabsorption.
* Calcitonin: Inhibits osteoclast activity and reduces renal tubular calcium reabsorption.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List the two most common molecular genetic alterations associated with the development of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
* Cyclin D1 (CCND1) gene inversion or protein overexpression
* MEN1 gene inactivating mutations (tumor suppressor locus)
* Both drive monoclonal cellular proliferation

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia in the ambulatory, non-hospitalized patient population is [___].
back:
* Primary hyperparathyroidism.
* Usually discovered incidentally on routine metabolic panels.
* Most frequently results from a solitary, sporadic parathyroid adenoma in 85-95% of clinical cases.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and proximal muscle weakness. Labs show Calcium 11.5 mg/dL and PTH 150 pg/mL (Normal: 10-65). Identify the most likely underlying pathology.
back:
* Primary Hyperparathyroidism (PHP).
* Results from autonomous overproduction of Parathyroid Hormone.
* Often involves a solitary adenoma or multiglandular hyperplasia in the context of MEN-1.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) on renal vitamin D metabolism to maintain calcium homeostasis.
back:
* PTH stimulates 1-alpha-hydroxylase in the proximal convoluted tubule.
* This enzyme converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D into active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.
* Active vitamin D subsequently increases intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the skeletal manifestations of Primary Hyperparathyroidism with those found in generalized Osteoporosis.
back:
* Hyperparathyroidism: Features dissecting osteitis, "brown tumors," and cystic bone replacement known as osteitis fibrosa cystica.
* Osteoporosis: Characterized by reduced bone mass and trabecular thinning without the pathognomonic cystic or hemorrhagic lesions.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List four common causes of hypercalcemia that are typically associated with suppressed (low) serum PTH levels.
back:
* Hypercalcemia of Malignancy (PTHrP or bone metastases).
* Vitamin D intoxication.
* Chronic granulomatous diseases (e.g., Sarcoidosis).
* Prolonged immobilization causing increased bone turnover.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Developmental failure of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches, resulting in congenital hypoparathyroidism and thymic defects, is characteristic of [___].
back:
* DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11 deletion).
* Presents with neonatal hypocalcemic tetany and T-cell immunodeficiency.
* Often associated with congenital heart disease and midline facial anomalies.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with chronic renal failure presents with a high PTH (850 pg/mL), low serum Calcium (7.8 mg/dL), and high Phosphate. Identify the specific type of hyperparathyroidism.
back:
* Secondary Hyperparathyroidism.
* Compensatory overactivity of parathyroid glands in response to chronic hypocalcemia.
* Driven by phosphate retention and deficient active Vitamin D (1,25-(OH)2D) production.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung presents with a calcium of 14 mg/dL and suppressed PTH. Explain the biochemical mechanism.
back:
* Humoral Hypercalcemia of Malignancy (HHM).
* Tumor-secreted Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP) mimics PTH action.
* PTHrP binds to PTH-1 receptors in bone and kidney, increasing systemic calcium levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the clinical presentation and elicitation of Chvostek sign versus Trousseau sign in hypoparathyroidism.
back:
* Chvostek: Facial muscle twitching elicited by tapping the facial nerve anterior to the ear.
* Trousseau: Carpal spasm induced by brachial artery occlusion with a blood pressure cuff.
* Both indicate neuromuscular irritability.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify three common causes of acquired or iatrogenic hypoparathyroidism.
back:
* Accidental removal during total thyroidectomy or radical neck dissection.
* Inadvertent excision of parathyroid glands mistaken for cervical lymph nodes.
* Post-surgical ischemic injury due to compromised parathyroid vascular supply.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia in the outpatient clinical setting is [___].
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism
• Most often caused by a solitary sporadic adenoma (85–95% of cases)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and "brown tumors" in the mandible. Lab results show hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. Identify the most likely underlying pathologic lesion.
back:
• Solitary Parathyroid Adenoma
• Clinically manifested as "painful bones, renal stones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans"

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of serum phosphorus and Vitamin D in the development of secondary hyperparathyroidism during chronic renal failure.
back:
• Hyperphosphatemia: Directly depresses serum calcium
• Alpha-1 hydroxylase loss: Decreases active Vitamin D, reducing intestinal calcium absorption
• Feedback: Hypocalcemia stimulates compensatory parathyroid hyperplasia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the biochemical profiles of Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Hypercalcemia of Malignancy regarding PTH and PTH-related protein (PTHrP).
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Elevated PTH; Normal/Low PTHrP
• Malignancy (PTHrP-mediated): Suppressed PTH; Elevated PTHrP
• Malignancy is the most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia in hospitalized patients

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the three interrelated skeletal abnormalities that define generalized osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone).
back:
• Increased osteoclast activity with peritrabecular fibrosis
• Dissecting osteitis (railroad track appearance)
• Brown tumors (hemosiderin-laden cystic masses)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A diagnostic sign of hypocalcemia characterized by carpal spasm induced by inflating a blood pressure cuff above systolic pressure is the [___].
back:
• Trousseau sign
• Indicates neuromuscular irritability due to low ionized calcium levels

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient presents with circumoral numbness and tetany 24 hours after a total thyroidectomy. Identify the likely diagnosis and the causative mechanism.
back:
• Iatrogenic Hypoparathyroidism
• Accidental removal or devascularization of all four parathyroid glands during neck surgery
• Results in acute hypocalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the molecular rearrangement involving Chromosome 11 and the CCDN1 gene observed in sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Pericentric inversion of Chromosome 11
• CCDN1 (Cyclin D1) is placed adjacent to the PTH gene promoter
• Causes parathyroid-specific overexpression of Cyclin D1, driving cell proliferation

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast Hypoparathyroidism with Pseudohypoparathyroidism regarding circulating PTH levels and the underlying cause of hypocalcemia.
back:
• Hypoparathyroidism: Low PTH due to gland destruction or agenesis
• Pseudohypoparathyroidism: Normal/High PTH due to end-organ resistance (G-protein signaling defect)
• Both present with hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List three mechanisms by which Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) increases serum ionized calcium levels.
back:
• Enhances renal tubular reabsorption of calcium
• Increases renal activation of Vitamin D (Alpha-1 hydroxylase)
• Stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption to release calcium into the ECF

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In the outpatient setting, the most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia discovered incidentally on routine serum chemistry panels is [___].
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism.
• Usually presents as an incidental laboratory discovery.
• Characterized by inappropriately elevated PTH levels relative to high serum calcium concentrations.
• Primarily caused by a solitary parathyroid adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 65-year-old male with a heavy smoking history presents with fatigue and constipation. Labs show serum calcium of 14 mg/dL and suppressed PTH. The likely mechanism is the ectopic secretion of [___].
back:
• PTH-related peptide (PTHrP).
• This is the most common mechanism of hypercalcemia in solid tumors (e.g., lung cancer).
• PTHrP mimics PTH action on bone and kidneys but is biochemically distinct.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of phosphate and Vitamin D metabolism in the development of secondary hyperparathyroidism during chronic renal failure.
back:
• Hyperphosphatemia from renal failure directly depresses serum calcium levels.
• Impaired alpha-1-hydroxylase availability reduces active Vitamin D synthesis.
• Persistent hypocalcemia and reduced Vitamin D feedback stimulate compensatory parathyroid hyperplasia and PTH hypersecretion.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast primary hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia of malignancy regarding their serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) and PTH-related peptide (PTHrP) profiles.
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: PTH is inappropriately elevated; PTHrP is normal.
• Malignancy-Associated Hypercalcemia: PTH is suppressed (low); PTHrP is frequently elevated.
• Distinction is critical as malignancy is the leading cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List the three interrelated skeletal abnormalities that define the condition known as generalized osteitis fibrosa cystica.
back:
• Osteoporosis: Loss of bone mass with subperiosteal resorption.
• Brown Tumors: Reactive masses resulting from microfractures and hemosiderin deposition.
• Dissecting Osteitis: Osteoclasts tunneling through trabeculae, creating a characteristic "railroad track" appearance.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Clinical findings such as Chvostek sign (facial nerve irritability) and Trousseau sign (carpopedal spasm) are diagnostic hallmarks of neuromuscular irritability caused by [___].
back:
• Hypocalcemia (Tetany).
• Chvostek sign is elicited by tapping the facial nerve.
• Trousseau sign is elicited by occluding circulation to the arm with a blood pressure cuff for several minutes.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 30-year-old female develops circumoral paresthesias and carpopedal spasms 24 hours after a total thyroidectomy for a large goiter. Identify the underlying etiology of her symptoms.
back:
• Acquired hypoparathyroidism.
• Results from the inadvertent removal of all four parathyroid glands during surgery.
• The acute loss of PTH leads to rapid hypocalcemia and resulting tetany.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the biological basis of pseudohypoparathyroidism and its characteristic biochemical presentation despite high serum parathyroid hormone levels.
back:
• End-organ resistance to PTH action due to genetic defects in G-protein signaling.
• Presents with hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia despite elevated PTH.
• Often associated with resistance to other hormones like TSH and FSH/LH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the gross glandular involvement typical of a sporadic parathyroid adenoma with that seen in primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma: Usually a solitary, well-circumscribed, tan-brown nodule involving a single gland.
• Primary Hyperplasia: Classically a multiglandular process involving all four glands, though enlargement may be asymmetric.
• Stromal fat is inconspicuous in both conditions.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify two recurrent molecular alterations found in the pathogenesis of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Cyclin D1 (CCDN1) gene inversions or overexpression.
• MEN1 tumor suppressor gene mutations with loss of heterozygosity.
• These mutations drive autonomous chief cell proliferation and monoclonal neoplastic growth.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia discovered during routine blood chemistry profiles is [___].
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism
  • Most cases are caused by a solitary parathyroid adenoma

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female with end-stage renal disease presents with elevated PTH levels, hyperphosphatemia, and low serum calcium. Identify the specific type of hyperparathyroidism and its immediate driver.
back:
• Secondary hyperparathyroidism
  • Driven by chronic hypocalcemia due to phosphate retention and reduced Vitamin D synthesis

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the humoral mechanism by which solid tumors (e.g., squamous cell lung carcinoma) typically induce symptomatic hypercalcemia without skeletal metastases.
back:
• Secretion of PTH-related protein (PTHrP)
  • PTHrP mimics PTH by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with autonomous PTH secretion undergoes a bone biopsy. Contrast the microscopic appearance of 'dissecting osteitis' with that of a 'brown tumor.'
back:
• Dissecting osteitis: Osteoclasts tunnel centrally along medullary trabeculae, resembling railroad tracks
  • Brown tumor: Reactive masses of fibrovascular tissue, hemorrhage, and hemosiderin at microfracture sites

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the two classic clinical signs used to elicit neuromuscular irritability (tetany) in a patient with suspected hypocalcemia.
back:
• Chvostek sign: Twitching of facial muscles on tapping the facial nerve
  • Trousseau sign: Carpal spasm induced by inflating a blood pressure cuff

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: To maintain calcium homeostasis, PTH promotes the activation of [___] in the kidneys, which directly increases intestinal calcium absorption.
back:
• Vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxy form)
  • Achieved via stimulation of the renal alpha-1-hydroxylase enzyme

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A child presents with a triad of hypoparathyroidism, primary adrenal insufficiency, and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. Identify the underlying genetic defect.
back:
• Mutation in the AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene
  • Diagnosis: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In the context of chronic renal failure, describe why the loss of renal parenchyma leads to the development of secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Decreased alpha-1-hydroxylase reduces active Vitamin D synthesis
  • Loss of Vitamin D-mediated feedback allows unchecked PTH secretion and diminishes intestinal calcium absorption

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the biochemical profiles of primary versus secondary hyperparathyroidism regarding serum calcium and phosphate levels.
back:
• Primary: Hypercalcemia and hypophosphatemia
  • Secondary: Hypocalcemia (or normal) and hyperphosphatemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Pseudohypoparathyroidism is characterized by end-organ resistance to PTH. Identify two other non-parathyroid hormone receptors that are often defective in this condition.
back:
• TSH receptor (causing mild hypothyroidism)
  • FSH/LH receptors (causing hypergonadotropic hypogonadism)

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: The biochemical hallmark of primary hyperthyroidism, such as in Graves disease or toxic multinodular goiter, is a [___] serum TSH level with an [___] in free T4.
back:
• Suppressed (Low) TSH
• Elevated (High) Free T4
• Reflects excessive thyroid hormone production and intact negative feedback on the anterior pituitary.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A 45-year-old female presents with fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. Lab results reveal elevated TSH and low free T4. Identify the most likely underlying diagnosis and mechanism.
back:
• Hashimoto Thyroiditis
• Primary hypothyroidism caused by autoimmune destruction of the thyroid gland
• Lack of T4 results in loss of feedback inhibition on the pituitary.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the diagnostic hormone level contrast used to distinguish primary hypothyroidism from central (secondary) hypothyroidism.
back:
• Primary: High TSH; Low Free T4 (Gland failure).
• Central: Low or inappropriately normal TSH; Low Free T4 (Pituitary/hypothalamic failure).
• TSH is the most sensitive screening marker.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient presents with signs of thyrotoxicosis but an unusually elevated TSH. Contrast this with the lab profile expected in a hyperfunctioning thyroid adenoma.
back:
• TSH-Secreting Adenoma (Secondary): High TSH; High Free T4.
• Toxic Adenoma (Primary): Low (Suppressed) TSH; High Free T4.
• Primary causes involve autonomous hormone production bypassing pituitary control.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Directly describe how the pharmacological action of Propylthiouracil (PTU) modifies circulating thyroid hormone levels.
back:
• Inhibits thyroid peroxidase (stops synthesis).
• Inhibits peripheral 5'-deiodinase (prevents T4 to T3 conversion).
• Reduces levels of the highly active T3 form in the blood.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: In iodine-deficient regions (Endemic Goiter), the lack of dietary iodine leads to [___] synthesis of T3/T4, which causes a compensatory [___] in TSH secretion.
back:
• Decreased/Low T3 and T4
• Increased/High TSH
• Sustained TSH elevation causes follicular cell hypertrophy and hyperplasia (Goiter).

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: A patient with symptoms of hyperthyroidism has a suppressed TSH and elevated T3, but a completely normal free T4 level. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• T3-Toxicosis
• Seen in early Graves disease or some toxic nodules
• Requires direct serum T3 measurement as T4 levels may be misleadingly normal.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Explain the laboratory findings (Thyroglobulin and radioactive uptake) that differentiate factitious thyrotoxicosis from endogenous hyperfunctioning causes.
back:
• Factitious: Low Thyroglobulin; Low radioactive iodine uptake.
• Endogenous: High Thyroglobulin; High uptake (e.g., Graves).
• High T3/T4 and low TSH are present in both.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: Contrast the metabolic feedback loop response during the hyperthyroid phase of de Quervain thyroiditis with that seen in multinodular goiter.
back:
• de Quervain: TSH suppressed due to leaking preformed hormone; Gland is non-hyperfunctioning.
• Multinodular Goiter: TSH suppressed due to autonomous follicular hyperfunction.
• Both present with high circulating T4.

category: Enumerate causes of hypo and hyperthyroidism along with levels of thyroid hormones
front: List the hormones produced by thyroid follicular cells and identify which has a higher affinity for target cell nuclear receptors.
back:
• Thyroxine (T4) and Triiodothyronine (T3).
• Triiodothyronine (T3) has 10x higher affinity.
• T4 serves as a buffer and is converted to T3 peripherally.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The histopathological hallmark that distinguishes a parathyroid adenoma from primary hyperplasia is the presence of a rim of [___] parathyroid tissue separated by a fibrous capsule.
back:
• Compressed non-neoplastic
• Found at the periphery of the solitary nodule
• Distinguishes localized neoplasia from multiglandular, diffuse involvement typical of hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and a solitary tan-red nodule in the neck. Histology shows uniform chief cells and inconspicuous stromal fat. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Characterized by a solitary, encapsulated mass
• Usually functional, causing primary hyperparathyroidism
• Adjacent non-neoplastic glands are normal or shrunken due to feedback inhibition.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
coreConcept: Significance of Stromal Fat in Parathyroid Pathology
front: Explain the role of stromal fat content in the microscopic differentiation of normal parathyroid tissue from parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Normal glands contain ~30% fat after age 25
• Decreased or absent stromal fat indicates hypercellularity
• Helps distinguish hyperfunctional/neoplastic states from normal parenchyma where fat is abundant.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the typical gross distribution and glandular involvement of parathyroid adenoma with that of primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Almost always solitary; involves only one gland.
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement; classically all four glands are enlarged, though frequently asymmetric.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the appearance of 'Oxyphil cells' frequently observed in clusters within parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Larger than chief cells
• Abundant acidophilic (eosinophilic) granular cytoplasm
• Tightly packed with mitochondria
• Generally lack parathyroid hormone secretory granules.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In certain variants of parathyroid hyperplasia, the constituent cells contain abundant glycogen, giving them a characteristic [___] appearance in histologic sections.
back:
• Water-clear cell
• Represents a morphological variant of chief cell hyperplasia
• May involve the glands in a diffuse or multinodular pattern.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Histology of a resected parathyroid nodule reveals chief cells with bizarre, pleomorphic nuclei but no evidence of capsular or vascular invasion. Define this phenomenon.
back:
• Endocrine atypia
• Frequently seen in benign parathyroid adenomas
• Is NOT a criterion for malignancy
• Carcinoma is diagnosed strictly by invasion or metastasis.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the chromosomal mechanism leading to Cyclin D1 (CCND1) overexpression in a subset of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11
• CCND1 gene relocates adjacent to the PTH gene promoter
• Directs pathological overexpression of cyclin D1
• Drives autonomous follicular cell proliferation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the presence and nature of the fibrous capsule in parathyroid adenoma versus parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Demonstrates a well-defined, intact fibrous capsule encircling the nodule.
• Hyperplasia: Lacks a prominent peripheral capsule; nodules may be enveloped by delicate strands but lack true encapsulation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the specific transcription factor mutations found in ~35% of sporadic parathyroid tumors and associated with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1.
back:
• MEN1 (Menin)
• Inactivating mutation with loss of heterozygosity
• Acts as a tumor suppressor protein regulating cell cycle components.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia in hospitalized patients is [___], which often occurs due to the secretion of PTH-related protein (PTHrP).
back:
• Malignancy
• Mimics PTH action on bone and kidney
• Common in lung, breast, and renal carcinomas
• Leads to suppressed native PTH levels

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 52-year-old female presents with recurrent nephrolithiasis and bone pain. Labs reveal serum Calcium 11.5 mg/dL (Normal: 8.5-10.5) and an inappropriately elevated serum PTH. What is the most likely underlying pathology?
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism
• Most commonly caused by a solitary parathyroid adenoma (85-95%)
• Associated with "Stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans"
• May involve Cyclin D1 or MEN1 mutations

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the mechanism by which chronic renal failure leads to secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Inadequate phosphate excretion causes hyperphosphatemia
• Reduced 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity decreases active Vitamin D
• Both factors induce hypocalcemia
• Low calcium triggers compensatory parathyroid gland hyperplasia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the serum calcium and phosphate levels in a patient with an autonomous parathyroid adenoma versus a patient with chronic renal failure.
back:
• Autonomous Adenoma: High Calcium, Low Phosphate (due to phosphaturia)
• Chronic Renal Failure: Low or Normal Calcium, High Phosphate (retention)
• Both demonstrate elevated PTH levels
• Autonomous is primary; Renal is secondary

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the three endocrine organs classically involved in Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN-1).
back:
• Parathyroid (Hyperplasia or Adenoma)
• Pancreas (Islet cell tumors or Gastrinomas)
• Pituitary (Prolactinomas)
• Commonly known as the "3 Ps" syndrome

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1) is characterized by hypoparathyroidism and candidiasis due to a germline mutation in the [___] gene.
back:
• AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator)
• Leads to failure of central T-cell tolerance
• Results in autoimmune destruction of endocrine organs
• Specifically targets the parathyroid and adrenal glands

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient presents with carpopedal spasms and a positive Trousseau sign after neck surgery. What is the likely clinical diagnosis and the physiological basis?
back:
• Hypoparathyroidism leading to Hypocalcemia
• Caused by neuromuscular irritability (tetany)
• Often due to inadvertent surgical removal of parathyroid glands
• Also characterized by the Chvostek sign

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the mechanism of hypercalcemia associated with sarcoidosis and other granulomatous diseases.
back:
• Activated macrophages in granulomas express 1-alpha-hydroxylase
• Leads to unregulated conversion of Vitamin D to its active form
• Increases intestinal absorption of calcium
• Causes PTH-independent hypercalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the macroscopic and microscopic involvement of the parathyroid glands in primary hyperplasia versus a solitary adenoma.
back:
• Hyperplasia: All four glands involved; microscopic diffuse or nodular growth
• Adenoma: Solitary gland; characterized by a compressed rim of normal tissue
• Both lack significant stromal fat
• Both predominantly feature chief cells

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the skeletal manifestation of severe primary hyperparathyroidism characterized by peritrabecular fibrosis and cystic hemorrhage.
back:
• Osteitis fibrosa cystica (Von Recklinghausen disease)
• Results from excessive osteoclastic activity
• Leads to "Brown tumors" filled with vascularity and hemosiderin
• Often presents with "salt and pepper" skull appearance

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In parathyroid adenoma, a characteristic histologic feature used to distinguish it from the surrounding normal gland is a [___] of compressed, non-neoplastic parathyroid tissue.
back:
• A peripheral rim of compressed normal tissue.
• Often separated from the adenoma by a thin fibrous capsule.
• This feature is typically absent in cases of diffuse primary hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. Imaging shows a solitary 2cm mass at the inferior pole of the thyroid. Microscopic exam reveals monomorphic polygonal chief cells and inconspicuous stromal fat. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma.
• Hallmark features include a solitary, well-circumscribed, soft, tan-brown nodule.
• Associated non-neoplastic glands are typically normal in size or shrunken due to feedback inhibition.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of the CCDN1 gene rearrangement in the development of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Inversion on chromosome 11.
• Places the Cyclin D1 (CCDN1) gene adjacent to the PTH gene promoter.
• Resulting Cyclin D1 overexpression drives constitutive cell cycle progression and clonal expansion.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the microscopic boundary and glandular involvement of primary parathyroid hyperplasia versus parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement (all four glands); lacks a well-defined capsule separating it from normal parenchyma.
• Adenoma: Solitary nodule; characteristically demonstrates an intact fibrous capsule and a compressed rim of normal tissue.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the clinical significance of finding nuclear pleomorphism and bizarre nuclei ("endocrine atypia") within a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• It is a benign finding.
• Does not indicate malignancy or adenocarcinoma.
• Nuclear pleomorphism is common in benign endocrine neoplasms and is not a criterion for cancer.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The majority of both parathyroid adenomas and hyperplastic glands are predominantly composed of [___] cells.
back:
• Chief cells.
• These are polygonal cells with centrally placed, uniform nuclei and light to dark pink cytoplasm.
• They contain the secretory granules for parathyroid hormone (PTH).

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with chronic renal failure presents with secondary hyperparathyroidism. Describe the typical changes in stromal fat content seen in the parathyroid glands.
back:
• Stromal fat is significantly decreased or absent.
• Adipocytes are replaced by diffuse or multinodular chief cell hyperplasia.
• This occurs in response to chronic hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe how the loss of the MEN1 gene product, Menin, carrying carries out its biological function in parathyroid tumorigenesis.
back:
• MEN1 is a tumor-suppressor gene (11q13).
• Inactivation of both alleles (two-hit hypothesis) leads to uncontrolled cell growth.
• Menin normally regulates transcription and maintains genomic stability in parathyroid cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast parathyroid chief cells with oxyphil cells based on their organelle content and staining.
back:
• Chief cells: Polygonal, eosinophilic; rich in PTH secretory granules.
• Oxyphil cells: Larger; acidophilic cytoplasm; tightly packed with mitochondria; secretory granules are sparse or absent.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the specific histologic variant of parathyroid hyperplasia characterized by cells containing abundant intracytoplasmic glycogen and a vacuolated appearance.
back:
• Water-clear cell hyperplasia.
• A rare pattern of primary hyperplasia.
• Cells appear optically clear in routine H&E sections due to high glycogen content.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common underlying lesion responsible for primary hyperparathyroidism is a solitary [___].
back:
• Sporadic parathyroid adenoma (85–95% of cases)
• Characterized by a well-circumscribed, tan to reddish-brown nodule
• Composed mostly of uniform chief cells

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia, nephrolithiasis, and depressed serum phosphate. Identify the most likely diagnosis and the typical status of the non-adenomatous parathyroid glands.
back:
• Diagnosis: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
• Non-adenomatous glands: Usually normal or shrunken
• Mechanism: Feedback inhibition by elevated serum calcium levels

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of alpha-1-hydroxylase deficiency in the pathogenesis of secondary hyperparathyroidism in chronic renal failure.
back:
• Loss of renal mass reduces alpha-1-hydroxylase availability
• Leads to decreased active Vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D)
• Results in reduced intestinal calcium absorption and compensatory PTH elevation

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 60-year-old male with weight loss and a lung mass presents with acute mental confusion and a serum calcium of 14 mg/dL. Contrast the expected PTH levels in this patient with those found in primary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Malignancy (this case): Low/suppressed PTH (hypercalcemia often due to PTHrP)
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Inappropriately elevated/High PTH
• Malignancy is the most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Detail the therapeutic role of phosphate binders in the management of secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Bind dietary phosphate in the gut to prevent absorption
• Directly lower serum phosphate levels
• Mitigates the hypocalcemic drive that stimulates parathyroid hyperplasia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The 'hallmark' clinical manifestation of hypocalcemia, characterized by neuromuscular irritability and carpopedal spasm, is [___].
back:
• Tetany
• Elicited by Chvostek sign (facial nerve tapping)
• Elicited by Trousseau sign (blood pressure cuff occlusion)

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 10-year-old child presents with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and primary adrenal insufficiency. Identify the likely gene mutation and the associated parathyroid abnormality.
back:
• Gene: AIRE mutation (Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1)
• Abnormality: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
• Result: Destructive immune attack against parathyroid tissue

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with long-standing secondary hyperparathyroidism from renal failure suddenly develops hypercalcemia that does not resolve with standard treatment. Name this condition and its underlying mechanism.
back:
• Condition: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
• Mechanism: Parathyroid activity becomes autonomous and excessive
• Often requires surgical resection of the hyperplastic glands

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the renal effects of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) on calcium versus phosphate homeostasis.
back:
• Calcium: Increases renal tubular reabsorption (conserves free calcium)
• Phosphate: Increases urinary phosphate excretion (phosphaturia)
• Net effect: Elevation of serum calcium and lowering of phosphate

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the most frequent cause of acquired hypoparathyroidism.
back:
• Inadvertent surgical removal during thyroidectomy or radical neck dissection
• Can also occur via excision of parathyroids mistaken for lymph nodes
• Results in acute post-operative hypocalcemic tetany

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia in the outpatient setting is [___].
back:
* Primary hyperparathyroidism
* Most often caused by a solitary parathyroid adenoma (85% to 95% of cases).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and recent-onset depression. Labs show a serum calcium of 11.8 mg/dL and an inappropriately elevated PTH. Identify the most likely underlying diagnosis.
back:
* Primary hyperparathyroidism
* Typically resulting from an autonomous overproduction of PTH by a solitary parathyroid adenoma.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the sequence by which chronic renal failure triggers secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
* Hyperphosphatemia directly depresses serum calcium levels
* Reduced renal alpha-1-hydroxylase activity decreases active Vitamin D levels
* Persistent hypocalcemia causes compensatory parathyroid gland overactivity.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Distinguish between Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Hypercalcemia of Malignancy based on serum PTH and PTH-related peptide (PTHrP) levels.
back:
* Primary HP: Elevated PTH; low to undetectable PTHrP
* Malignancy: Suppressed PTH; markedly elevated PTHrP in approximately 80% of cases.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate the three primary lesions of the parathyroid glands that underlie hyperfunction in primary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
* Adenoma (85% to 95%)
* Primary Hyperplasia (5% to 10%)
* Parathyroid Carcinoma (~1%).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A clonal molecular rearrangement relocating the [___] gene adjacent to the PTH gene promoter is found in 10% to 20% of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
* Cyclin D1 (CCND1)
* This pericentric inversion on chromosome 11 leads to excessive cellular proliferation.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient presents with circumoral numbness and carpopedal spasms following a radical neck dissection. Identify the likely cause of these symptoms and the biochemical hallmark.
back:
* Acquired hypoparathyroidism
* Caused by inadvertent surgical removal of parathyroid glands; characterized by hypocalcemia and low PTH.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the role of loss-of-function mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor (CASR) gene in the pathogenesis of Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia.
back:
* Mutations reduce the parathyroid's sensitivity to extracellular calcium
* Higher calcium levels are required to suppress PTH secretion
* Results in autonomous PTH production and increased renal calcium resorption.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast serum phosphate and calcium levels between Primary and Secondary (Renal-related) Hyperparathyroidism.
back:
* Primary: Hypercalcemia and Hypophosphatemia
* Secondary: Hypocalcemia (or normocalcemia) and Hyperphosphatemia (due to renal retention).

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the skeletal triad associated with severe, symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism (Von Recklinghausen disease of bone).
back:
* Osteoporosis
* Brown tumors (hemorrhagic cystic masses)
* Osteitis fibrosa cystica.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In the histological examination of parathyroid adenomas, the primary cell type responsible for parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion is the [___].
back:
• Chief cells.
• Polygonal cells with central, round, uniform nuclei.
• Light to dark pink cytoplasm containing secretory granules.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia. Surgical exploration reveals a solitary, 2-gram, tan-colored nodule in the left inferior gland, while the other three glands appear shrunken. Identify the underlying pathology.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma.
• Characterized by solitary involvement.
• High calcium levels cause feedback inhibition and atrophy of the remaining non-neoplastic glands.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role and significance of "endocrine atypia" in the nuclei of parathyroid adenoma cells.
back:
• Refers to pleomorphic and bizarre nuclear shapes.
• Commonly seen in benign endocrine neoplasms.
• It is NOT a criterion for malignancy or rapid growth.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast parathyroid adenoma with parathyroid hyperplasia regarding gland involvement and the presence of a peripheral rim of normal tissue.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary gland; features a compressed rim of normal parathyroid tissue outside the capsule.
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement; usually lacks a distinct capsule and normal rim.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the typical stromal fat content found in parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma compared to a normal adult gland.
back:
• Significantly decreased or inconspicuous stromal fat.
• Normal glands contain roughly 30% fat.
• Absence of fat distinguishes hypercellular lesions from normal parenchyma.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The rare variants of parathyroid adenomas composed entirely of larger cells with abundant, mitochondria-rich, acidophilic cytoplasm are known as [___].
back:
• Oxyphil adenomas.
• Cells have granular eosinophilic cytoplasm.
• Secretory granules are sparse or absent.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with MEN-1 syndrome undergoes neck exploration. Histology reveals diffuse chief cell proliferation in all four parathyroid glands with asymmetric enlargement. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
• Primary Parathyroid Hyperplasia.
• Multiglandular involvement is characteristic of familial syndromes like MEN-1 and MEN-2.
• May appear in diffuse or multinodular patterns.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the histological appearance of the "water-clear cell" variant of parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Constituent cells contain abundant intracytoplasmic glycogen.
• Imparts a clear appearance to the cytoplasm in sections.
• Represents a morphological variant of multiglandular hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the diagnostic requirements for parathyroid carcinoma versus adenoma regarding the capsule and mitotic activity.
back:
• Carcinoma: Thick fibrous capsule; frequent mitoses; requires evidence of local invasion or metastasis.
• Adenoma: Delicate capsule; mitotic figures are extremely rare; non-invasive.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: State the common macroscopic features of the cut surface of a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Soft and well-circumscribed.
• Tan to reddish-brown in color.
• Larger lesions may show hemorrhage, fibrosis, or cystic change.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, accounting for the vast majority of cases, is a solitary sporadic [___].
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma
• Usually presents as a well-circumscribed, soft, tan-brown nodule
• Microscopically composed primarily of uniform chief cells
• Demonstrates a peripheral rim of compressed normal parathyroid tissue

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 55-year-old female presents with incidental hypercalcemia (11.2 mg/dL) and hypophosphatemia. Serum PTH is inappropriately elevated. Identify the most likely diagnosis and the most common genetic cell-cycle driver associated with this sporadic condition.
back:
• Diagnosis: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
• Genetic Driver: Overexpression of Cyclin D1 (CCND1)
• Mechanism: Often involves a pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11
• Leads to unchecked cellular proliferation within the parathyroid

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the mechanism through which chronic renal failure induces secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Hyperphosphatemia: Reduced renal excretion directly depresses serum ionized calcium levels
• Vitamin D deficiency: Loss of renal alpha-1-hydroxylase reduces active calcitriol synthesis
• Compensatory stimulation: Chronic hypocalcemia triggers massive, reactive PTH oversecretion

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the PTH levels and typical clinical settings found in Primary Hyperparathyroidism versus Hypercalcemia of Malignancy.
back:
• Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Serum PTH is inappropriately high/normal; usually an asymptomatic incidental finding
• Malignancy: Serum PTH is suppressed (low); hypercalcemia is severe and symptomatic
• Malignancy Mechanism: Often mediated by PTH-related peptide (PTHrP) secretion

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List the classic skeletal manifestations seen in severe, untreated primary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Osteitis fibrosa cystica (Von Recklinghausen disease of bone)
• Brown tumors (fibrovascular tissue with hemorrhage and giant cells)
• Dissecting osteitis (osteoclasts boring into medullary bone trabeculae)
• Generalized osteoporosis

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: In the classic triad of hyperparathyroidism, the clinical feature described as "[___]" refers to the formation of nephrolithiasis and obstructive uropathy.
back:
• Renal stones
• Caused by hypercalciuria (excess filtered calcium load)
• Can lead to chronic renal insufficiency or nephrocalcinosis
• Often consists of calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Following a total thyroidectomy, a patient presents with circumoral paresthesias and a positive Trousseau sign. Identify the diagnosis and the underlying electrolyte derangement.
back:
• Diagnosis: Acquired (Iatrogenic) Hypoparathyroidism
• Electrolyte: Hypocalcemia
• Result: Neuromuscular irritability and tetany
• Cause: Inadvertent removal or surgical injury to parathyroid glands

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the mechanism of hormone resistance in Pseudohypoparathyroidism and its effect on serum PTH levels.
back:
• Mechanism: End-organ resistance to PTH due to defective post-receptor G-protein signaling
• PTH Levels: Paradoxically high (elevated) circulating PTH
• Biochemical profile: Hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia despite excessive PTH
• Association: Often presents with skeletal and developmental anomalies

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the morphologic glandular involvement between a parathyroid adenoma and primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Usually involves only one gland; remaining glands are atrophic
• Hyperplasia: Typically involves all four glands (multiglandular involvement)
• Adenoma: Features a peripheral rim of normal tissue
• Hyperplasia: Shows diffuse or multinodular growth lacking a true capsule

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Enumerate three causes of hypercalcemia associated with suppressed (low) serum parathyroid hormone.
back:
• Hypercalcemia of malignancy (PTHrP-mediated)
• Vitamin D toxicity
• Sarcoidosis (extra-renal conversion to active Vitamin D)
• Thiazide diuretic use

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia identified on routine blood chemistry is [___].
back:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism.
• Usually results from a solitary parathyroid adenoma (~85-95%).
• Often detected incidentally during outpatient electrolyte screening.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 60-year-old female presents with a fractured femur and nephrolithiasis. Labs show hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. Identify the likely underlying parathyroid lesion.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma.
• Typically a solitary, encapsulated tan-to-reddish-brown nodule composed of uniform chief cells.
• Feedback inhibition usually causes the remaining glands to appear normal or shrunken.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain how chronic renal failure induces secondary hyperparathyroidism via the Vitamin D pathway.
back:
• Renal failure reduces alpha-1-hydroxylase activity.
• This leads to decreased synthesis of active Vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D).
• Impaired intestinal calcium absorption results in hypocalcemia, triggering compensatory PTH secretion.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient presents with hypercalcemia, weight loss, and a large neck mass. Contrast the criteria for diagnosing parathyroid carcinoma versus a benign adenoma in this scenario.
back:
• Parathyroid Carcinoma: Requires clinical evidence of local tissue invasion or distant metastasis.
• Parathyroid Adenoma: Solitary, circumscribed nodule lacking invasion; cytologic atypia (endocrine atypia) is insufficient to prove malignancy.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Specify the therapeutic mechanism by which phosphate binders assist in treating secondary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Binders decrease the prevailing hyperphosphatemia associated with renal failure.
• Reducing phosphate prevents the direct depression of ionized calcium levels.
• This minimizes the persistent stimulatory trigger for parathyroid hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The hallmark of hypocalcemia is [___], which presents as neuromuscular irritability ranging from paresthesias to life-threatening laryngospasm.
back:
• Tetany.
• Evidenced clinically by Chvostek sign (facial twitch) or Trousseau sign (carpal spasm).
• Results from decreased serum ionized calcium levels.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 12-year-old presents with dental hypoplasia, cataracts, and a positive Trousseau sign. He has a history of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. Identify the gene mutation responsible.
back:
• AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene mutation.
• Part of Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1).
• Leads to failure of central T-cell tolerance and autoimmune parathyroid destruction.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the pathogenesis of 'Brown Tumors' observed in severe, symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• PTH-induced bone resorption causes microfractures and secondary hemorrhage.
• These elicit an influx of macrophages and reparative fibrous tissue.
• The brown color results from intense vascularity and hemosiderin deposition.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the PTH and calcium levels in secondary hyperparathyroidism with those found in tertiary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Secondary: High PTH with low or normal serum calcium.
• Tertiary: Persistently high PTH with autonomous hypercalcemia, typically occurring after correction of chronic renal failure.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: List three major non-parathyroid causes of hypercalcemia associated with low PTH levels.
back:
• Malignancy (PTHrP secretion or osteolytic metastases).
• Vitamin D toxicity.
• Granulomatous diseases (e.g., Sarcoidosis).
• Thiazide diuretics.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
coreConcept: Diagnostic Microscopic Feature of Parathyroid Adenoma
front: In the microscopic evaluation of a parathyroid adenoma, stromal [___] is characteristically inconspicuous or absent within the tumor, distinguishing it from normal gland parenchyma.
back:
• Adipose tissue (fat).
• Normal glands contain roughly 30% fat.
• Its absence is a key indicator of neoplastic proliferation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and a solitary hot nodule on sestamibi scan. If the diagnosis is a parathyroid adenoma, describe the expected histopathologic state of the remaining three glands.
back:
• Atrophic or normal in size.
• Occurs due to feedback inhibition of PTH by elevated serum calcium levels.
• This distinguishes solitary adenoma from multiglandular hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the molecular mechanism involving the CCDN1 gene that leads to the development of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Pericentromeric inversion of chromosome 11.
• Relocation of CCDN1 adjacent to the PTH gene promoter.
• Resultant overexpression of Cyclin D1 drives autonomous cell proliferation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the microscopic boundary features of a parathyroid adenoma with those of primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Features a well-defined capsule and a rim of compressed non-neoplastic tissue.
• Hyperplasia: Lacks a true capsule and peripheral compressed rim; typically involves multiple glands.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the only two reliable histopathologic criteria for a definitive diagnosis of parathyroid carcinoma.
back:
• Invasion of surrounding soft tissues/structures.
• Demonstrated distant metastasis.
• Cytologic atypia and mitoses are unreliable for determining malignancy.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The most common cell type found in parathyroid adenomas, characterized by uniform polygonal shapes and centrally placed nuclei, is the [___] cell.
back:
• Chief cell.
• These cells contain secretory granules of Parathyroid Hormone (PTH).
• They represent the primary functional unit of the gland.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with a history of recurrent peptic ulcers (Zollinger-Ellison) and a pituitary lesion presents with hypercalcemia. Histopathologic examination of the parathyroid is most likely to reveal [___].
back:
• Primary Hyperplasia.
• This suggests MEN-1 (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1).
• In MEN syndromes, parathyroid involvement is classically multiglandular.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the clinical significance of finding 'endocrine atypia' (bizarre, pleomorphic nuclei) within a parathyroid lesion.
back:
• It is a benign finding.
• Frequently seen in adenomas.
• It does not indicate malignancy or aggressive behavior.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
coreConcept: Histologic Cell Types of the Parathyroid
front: Contrast the cytoplasmic characteristics of parathyroid chief cells with those of oxyphil cells.
back:
• Chief cells: Light to dark pink cytoplasm; contains PTH granules.
• Oxyphil cells: Abundant, brightly acidophilic (eosinophilic) cytoplasm; packed with mitochondria.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: State the histopathologic components that characterize a 'Brown tumor' of bone in severe hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Influx of macrophages.
• Extensive hemorrhage and microfractures.
• Abundant hemosiderin deposition.
• Reactive fibrovascular tissue replacement.

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: The most common underlying cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, accounting for 85% to 95% of cases, is a solitary [___].
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma
• Presents as a well-circumscribed, soft, tan nodule
• Results in autonomous overproduction of PTH and hypercalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A 50-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and osteoporosis. Molecular analysis of a parathyroid lesion reveals a pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11, placing the PTH promoter next to the gene for [___].
back:
• Cyclin D1 (CCND1)
• Overexpression drives cell cycle progression
• Key oncogenic driver in 10%–20% of sporadic parathyroid adenomas

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Explain the mechanistic basis for low serum Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) levels observed in humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy.
back:
• Tumors secrete Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP)
• PTHrP mimics PTH action on bone and kidneys
• Resultant hypercalcemia causes feedback inhibition of endogenous PTH production

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A patient with end-stage renal disease presents with elevated PTH and low serum calcium. Contrast this with the lab profile expected in a patient with a solitary parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma (Primary): High PTH, High Calcium, Low Phosphate
• Renal Failure (Secondary): High PTH, Low/Normal Calcium, High Phosphate
• Primary is autonomous; Secondary is compensatory to hypocalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the metabolic management steps used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism in chronic renal failure to prevent bone disease.
back:
• Dietary vitamin D supplementation
• Use of phosphate binders to lower serum phosphate
• These steps break the compensatory loop stimulating the parathyroid glands

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: During a physical examination for suspected hypoparathyroidism, the [___] sign is elicited by tapping the facial nerve to induce muscle twitching.
back:
• Chvostek sign
• Indicates neuromuscular irritability
• Diagnostic clinical feature of hypocalcemia

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: A child with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and ectodermal dystrophy presents with seizures. Laboratory tests confirm hypocalcemia and low PTH. This condition likely stems from a mutation in the [___] gene.
back:
• AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene
• Diagnosis: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APS-1)
• Leads to autoimmune destruction of parathyroid glands

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Describe the specific mechanism of bone resorption known as 'dissecting osteitis' found in severe primary hyperparathyroidism.
back:
• Osteoclasts tunnel centrally along the length of trabeculae
• Gives medullary bone a 'railroad track' appearance
• Marrow is replaced by fibrovascular tissue

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Contrast the physiological triggers for the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the posterior pituitary versus PTH release from parathyroid glands.
back:
• ADH: Triggered by increased plasma osmotic pressure or decreased blood pressure
• PTH: Triggered exclusively by a decrease in serum free (ionized) calcium

category: Enumerate causes of hypercalcemia, hyper and hypoparathyroidism
front: Identify the three classic morphologic components of 'osteitis fibrosa cystica' (von Recklinghausen disease of bone).
back:
• Increased osteoclast activity (dissecting osteitis)
• Peritrabecular fibrosis
• Cystic brown tumors (fibrous tissue with hemorrhage and hemosiderin)

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In a parathyroid adenoma, the neoplastic cells are typically demarcated from a peripheral rim of compressed normal parathyroid tissue by a thin [___].
back:
• Fibrous capsule
• Distinguishes adenoma from primary hyperplasia
• The rim of normal tissue typically contains visible stromal fat cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 50-year-old female with primary hyperparathyroidism undergoes neck exploration. Only the right superior gland is enlarged (3g), while the others are normal. State the most likely histopathological diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Typically a solitary, uniglandular process
• Non-neoplastic glands are often shrunken or normal due to feedback inhibition.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the molecular mechanism involving the CCDN1 (Cyclin D1) gene inversion in the pathogenesis of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Relocates CCDN1 adjacent to the PTH gene promoter
• Leads to PTH-driven overexpression of Cyclin D1 protein
• Overexpression stimulates excessive cellular proliferation and cell cycle progression.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the macroscopic distribution of glandular involvement in primary parathyroid hyperplasia versus a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement (classically all four glands), though involvement can be asymmetric.
• Adenoma: Almost exclusively solitary/uniglandular.
• Hyperplasia lacks a discrete capsule between nodules and normal tissue.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the appearance of stromal fat within the hypercellular areas of parathyroid adenomas and primary hyperplasia compared to normal glands.
back:
• Inconspicuous or absent in both adenoma and hyperplasia
• Normal adult glands contain ~30-40% stromal fat
• Depletion of fat is a key marker of cellular overgrowth.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The most common cell type populating both parathyroid adenomas and primary hyperplasia is the [___] cell.
back:
• Chief cell
• Polygonal cells with central, uniform nuclei and PTH secretory granules
• May coexist with clusters of larger, acidophilic oxyphil cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A parathyroid mass shows uniform chief cells with focal 'endocrine atypia.' However, tumor nests are identified invading the adjacent thyroid parenchyma. Identify the diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Carcinoma
• Diagnosis requires evidence of local invasion or metastasis
• Cytologic atypia alone is insufficient to distinguish carcinoma from adenoma.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the histopathological response of the parathyroid glands to the chronic hypocalcemia seen in end-stage renal disease.
back:
• Secondary Hyperparathyroidism
• Manifests as diffuse or multinodular chief cell hyperplasia
• Characterized by decreased stromal fat and increased parenchymal mass.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the cytoplasmic features of chief cells and oxyphil cells found within parathyroid neoplasms.
back:
• Chief cells: Light/dark pink cytoplasm containing PTH granules.
• Oxyphil cells: Larger with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm due to packed mitochondria.
• Neoplasms composed purely of oxyphil cells are rare variants.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the significance of finding enlarged, pleomorphic, and bizarre nuclei in a well-circumscribed parathyroid tumor.
back:
• 'Endocrine atypia'
• Frequently seen in benign adenomas
• Not an indicator of malignancy or clinical aggressiveness.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The microscopic hallmark that distinguishes a parathyroid adenoma from surrounding tissue is a [___] of compressed, non-neoplastic parathyroid parenchyma.
back:
• Rim of compressed normal tissue
• Often separated from the tumor by a delicate fibrous capsule

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female with renal stones and high serum calcium shows a solitary 3g reddish-tan nodule on a sestamibi scan. Microscopy reveals uniform polygonal chief cells. Name the diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid adenoma
• Solitary involvement with suppressed (atrophic) adjacent glands is diagnostic

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the physiological reason for the atrophy of non-neoplastic parathyroid glands in a patient with a functional parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma secretes excessive PTH leading to hypercalcemia
• High serum calcium exerts negative feedback on normal glands
• Feedback inhibition suppresses cellular activity and size

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the macroscopic distribution of parathyroid glandular enlargement in primary hyperplasia versus a typical adenoma.
back:
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement (usually all four glands, though often asymmetric)
• Adenoma: Solitary nodule involving only one gland

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the histologic variant of parathyroid hyperplasia where cells contain abundant cytoplasmic glycogen, resulting in a transparent appearance.
back:
• Water-clear cell hyperplasia
• Characterized by large, vacuolated cells and chief cell proliferation

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In both parathyroid adenoma and hyperplasia, the amount of [___] within the gland is characteristically inconspicuous or decreased compared to normal parenchyma.
back:
• Stromal fat (adipose tissue)
• Loss of intracellular/stromal fat is a reliable indicator of hypercellularity

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 40-year-old male with MEN-1 syndrome presents with hypercalcemia. Histology of the resected glands shows diffuse chief cell proliferation across all four glands. State the diagnosis.
back:
• Primary parathyroid hyperplasia
• Typically associated with familial syndromes like MEN-1 or MEN-2A

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain why 'endocrine atypia' (pleomorphic, bizarre nuclei) is insufficient to diagnose malignancy in a parathyroid chief cell lesion.
back:
• Pleomorphism is common in benign adenomas
• Malignancy requires capsular invasion, vascular invasion, or distant metastasis

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the typical weight and gross appearance of a parathyroid adenoma with a parathyroid carcinoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Soft, reddish-brown, usually <5g, circumscribed
• Carcinoma: Hard, gray-white, irregular, often >10g, invasive

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the predominant cell type found in both parathyroid adenomas and the most common form of parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Chief cells
• Small, polygonal cells with central nuclei and light to dark pink cytoplasm

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A characteristic histologic feature helping distinguish a parathyroid adenoma from primary hyperplasia is the presence of a rim of [___] parathyroid tissue external to the tumor capsule.
back:
• Compressed non-neoplastic tissue
• Often separated by a thin fibrous capsule
• Serves as a key diagnostic clue for solitary adenoma

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and a solitary 2cm neck mass. Histology reveals uniform chief cells in a nodular pattern with minimal stromal fat. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Solitary, well-circumscribed nodule
• Predominantly composed of chief cells
• Significant reduction in intraglandular adipose tissue

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the significance of stromal adipose tissue when evaluating parathyroid hyperplasia or adenoma on a biopsy.
back:
• Adipose tissue is inconspicuous or absent within hyperplastic/neoplastic areas
• Normal adult glands contain approximately 30% stromal fat
• Loss of fat indicates hypercellularity

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the gross and microscopic glandular involvement pattern between primary parathyroid hyperplasia and parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Usually solitary; involves one gland; contains a compressed rim of normal tissue
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement; all four glands enlarged (often asymmetric); lacks a compressed rim

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Specify the most reliable histologic criteria used to diagnose parathyroid carcinoma, as cytologic anaplasia is often unreliable.
back:
• Invasion of surrounding tissues/capsule
• Vascular invasion
• Presence of distant metastases
• Often enclosed by a dense fibrous capsule

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The hallmark of all localized parathyroid adenomas is the presence of a(n) [___] encircling the tumor, separating it from adjacent parenchyma.
back:
• Well-formed, intact fibrous capsule
• Essential for defining the lesion as a discrete neoplasm
• Distinguishes it from diffuse hyperplasia

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: During surgery for primary hyperparathyroidism, the surgeon identifies one enlarged gland (2.5g) and three normal-sized glands. Predict the most likely histological finding in the enlarged gland.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Solitary involvement is typical for adenoma
• Normal glands indicate functional suppression by high serum calcium

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the histomorphology and origin of 'Oxyphil cells' frequently observed in parathyroid neoplasms.
back:
• Large cells with abundant, granular eosinophilic cytoplasm
• Packed with mitochondria
• Derived from chief cells
• Can form 'Oxyphil Adenomas'

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the parathyroid morphology seen in Primary Hyperparathyroidism due to a single-gene defect versus Secondary Hyperparathyroidism due to renal failure.
back:
• Primary: Often solitary adenoma (monoclonal) or multi-gland hyperplasia
• Secondary: Diffuse, often symmetric, chief cell hyperplasia across all four glands as a compensatory response

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the primary cell type populating the majority of parathyroid adenomas and its typical nuclear features.
back:
• Chief cells
• Polygonal cells with round, uniform, centrally placed nuclei
• Contain secretory granules of PTH
• May show 'endocrine atypia' (bizarre nuclei) even in benign cases

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
