front: Parathyroid adenomas are microscopically composed primarily of uniform, polygonal [___] cells containing small, centrally placed nuclei.
back:
• Chief cells
• Occasionally contains nests of larger oxyphil cells
• Cells are typically arrayed in sheets or cords

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
coreConcept: Morphologic Differentiation of Adenoma vs. Hyperplasia
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia. Surgery reveals a solitary 2-gram reddish-brown nodule on the right inferior gland, while the other three glands are shrunken. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Solitary involvement is characteristic
• Shrunken/normal size of other glands results from feedback inhibition by high calcium

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of Cyclin D1 (CCND1) overexpression in sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Pericentromeric inversion of chromosome 11
• Relocates CCND1 (11q) adjacent to the PTH gene promoter (11p)
• PTH-regulatory elements drive excessive Cyclin D1 synthesis, stimulating unchecked cell proliferation

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the gross glandular involvement of primary parathyroid hyperplasia with that of a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Almost always a solitary, encapsulated nodule involving one gland.
• Hyperplasia: Typically a multiglandular process involving all four glands, though often asymmetrically.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the term for the pleomorphic and bizarre nuclei found in parathyroid adenomas that is NOT an indicator of malignancy.
back:
• Endocrine atypia
• Does not signify carcinoma
• Diagnosis of carcinoma requires local invasion or metastasis

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In both parathyroid adenoma and hyperplasia, a hallmark microscopic feature is that [___] fat is inconspicuous or absent within the lesional tissue.
back:
• Stromal fat
• Contrast with normal adult glands, where fat comprises up to 30% of the tissue
• Absence of fat indicates hypercellularity/neoplasia

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
coreConcept: Capsular and Peripheral Features of Adenomas
front: A patient undergoes resection of an enlarged parathyroid gland. Histology shows a chief cell nodule separated by a fibrous capsule from a narrow, peripheral rim of compressed normal parathyroid tissue. What is the diagnosis?
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• The 'compressed rim' of non-neoplastic tissue is a classic diagnostic feature
• This rim is usually absent in primary hyperplasia

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Which two criteria are the only reliable indicators for the definitive diagnosis of parathyroid carcinoma over adenoma?
back:
• 1. Local invasion of surrounding tissues
• 2. Documentation of distant metastasis
• Note: Nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic activity are unreliable in this tissue

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the microscopic appearance of 'Chief cell hyperplasia' with 'Water-clear cell hyperplasia' in the parathyroid glands.
back:
• Chief cell hyperplasia: Most common; uniform polygonal cells in diffuse or multinodular patterns.
• Water-clear cell hyperplasia: Cells contain abundant intracytoplasmic glycogen, creating a transparent appearance.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: State the most common tumor suppressor gene mutated in roughly 30% to 35% of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• MEN1 gene (encodes menin)
• Located on chromosome 11q13
• Associated with loss of heterozygosity of the second allele

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A common molecular driver in sporadic parathyroid adenomas involves the inversion of chromosome 11, placing the [___] gene under the control of the PTH promoter.
back:
• Cyclin D1 (CCDN1)
• Leads to protein overexpression
• Acts as a major cell cycle regulator promoting cellular proliferation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with incidental hypercalcemia. Scintigraphy shows a solitary 'hot' spot. Histopathology reveals a tan nodule with a thin fibrous capsule and uniform chief cells. Diagnosis?
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism (85-95%)
• Typically presents as a solitary, encapsulated, and functional mass.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the morphologic state of the non-neoplastic parathyroid glands in a patient with a solitary functioning adenoma.
back:
• Glands are normal in size or shrunken (atrophic)
• Feedback inhibition occurs due to elevated serum calcium
• Contributes to distinguishing adenoma from hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the macroscopic gland involvement in parathyroid adenoma versus primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary gland involvement; other glands atrophic.
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement; classically all four glands are enlarged (though sometimes asymmetrically).

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: State the clinical and pathological significance of 'endocrine atypia' (nuclear pleomorphism) when seen in parathyroid chief cells.
back:
• It is not a criterion for malignancy
• Frequently observed in benign adenomas
• Manifests as bizarre, enlarged, or pleomorphic nuclei.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The presence of a rim of [___] parathyroid tissue at the periphery of a solitary nodule is a classic histopathological clue for diagnosing an adenoma.
back:
• Compressed, non-neoplastic
• Separated from the tumor by a fibrous capsule
• Helps differentiate adenoma from diffuse hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with MEN-1 syndrome presents with hypercalcemia. Histology of the resected parathyroid glands shows multiglandular enlargement with decreased stromal fat and diffuse chief cell proliferation. Name the lesion.
back:
• Parathyroid Hyperplasia
• Common in familial syndromes (MEN-1, MEN-2A)
• Characterized by a lack of a distinct capsule between hyperplastic and normal tissue.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain how stromal fat content changes within a parathyroid gland involved by hyperplasia or adenoma compared to a normal adult gland.
back:
• Stromal fat is markedly decreased or inconspicuous
• Normal adult glands contain roughly 30% fat
• Adipose tissue is replaced by proliferating chief cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the cytoplasmic features and contents of parathyroid chief cells with those of oxyphil cells.
back:
• Chief cells: Pale/pink cytoplasm; contain PTH secretory granules.
• Oxyphil cells: Larger; intensely eosinophilic (acidophilic); packed with mitochondria; few or no secretory granules.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: List the three definitive histopathological criteria required to diagnose parathyroid carcinoma and exclude a large adenoma.
back:
• Invasion of surrounding neck structures/soft tissue
• Vascular invasion (beyond the capsule)
• Documented regional or distant metastasis.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Histologically, the most striking feature of parathyroid adenomas and hyperplasias that distinguishes them from normal parathyroid tissue is the marked reduction or absence of [___].
back:
• Stromal fat.
• Normal glands contain ~30% adipose tissue; hyperactive neoplastic or hyperplastic glands displace this fat with sheets of chief cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. A radionuclide scan identifies a single localized focus of increased uptake. Surgeon removes a 1g tan, encapsulated nodule. Histology shows uniform polygonal cells with central nuclei. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma.
• Characterized by a solitary, circumscribed mass of chief cells.
• Remaining glands are usually normal or atrophic due to feedback inhibition.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of the CCDN1 gene rearrangement in the pathogenesis of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11.
• Relocates the Cyclin D1 gene next to the PTH promoter.
• Drives overexpression of Cyclin D1 protein, leading to unchecked cell cycle progression.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the macroscopic gland involvement in Parathyroid Adenoma versus Primary Parathyroid Hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary nodule; only one gland is enlarged.
• Hyperplasia: Multi-glandular process; all four glands typically enlarged (though involvement can be asymmetric).

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the diagnostic significance of finding a 'rim of compressed non-neoplastic parathyroid tissue' outside a fibrous capsule.
back:
• It is a hallmark of Parathyroid Adenoma.
• Helps distinguish adenomas from hyperplasia, where this distinct boundary and adjacent atrophy are absent.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Parathyroid adenomas are most commonly composed of [___] cells, but uncommonly they consist entirely of mitochondria-rich, acidophilic [___] cells.
back:
• Chief cells (most common).
• Oxyphil cells (less common; known as oxyphil adenomas).

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 32-year-old male with a history of recurrent nephrolithiasis and a pituitary prolactinoma is found to have multi-glandular parathyroid enlargement. Which germline mutation is associated with this presentation?
back:
• MEN1 mutation (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1).
• Involves loss of the tumor suppressor protein menin.
• Characterized by the '3 Ps': Parathyroid (hyperplasia), Pancreas, and Pituitary.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Briefly explain why 'endocrine atypia' is not considered a criterion for malignancy in parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Endocrine atypia refers to pleomorphic, bizarre, or enlarged nuclei.
• It is commonly seen in benign endocrine adenomas.
• Malignancy requires evidence of invasion or metastasis.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Distinguish between the microscopic features of primary and secondary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Primary: Often chief cell or 'water-clear' cell patterns; seen in autonomous PTH production.
• Secondary: Compensatory hyperplasia of chief cells; typically results from chronic renal failure or vitamin D deficiency.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: What are the two definitive histologic requirements for a diagnosis of parathyroid carcinoma?
back:
• Local invasion of surrounding tissues.
• Distant metastasis.
• Cytologic features alone (like pleomorphism) are insufficient to distinguish it from adenoma.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The diagnostic hallmark of a parathyroid adenoma on histopathology is the presence of a rim of [___] parathyroid tissue at the periphery of the tumor.
back:
• Compressed non-neoplastic parenchyma
• Separated from the adenoma by a delicate fibrous capsule
• Helps distinguish it from primary hyperplasia where this rim is absent.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 50-year-old female with hypercalcemia undergoes surgery. A single tan-red nodule is excised; the other three parathyroid glands appear shrunken. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Solitary involvement is characteristic (85-95% of cases)
• Other glands are shrunken due to feedback inhibition from elevated serum calcium.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of the CCDN1 gene rearrangement in the pathogenesis of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• A pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11
• Relocates Cyclin D1 (CCDN1) adjacent to the PTH gene promoter
• Leads to overexpression of Cyclin D1, driving autonomous cell cycle progression.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the glandular involvement of primary parathyroid hyperplasia with that of a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary, discrete nodule involving only one gland.
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular process, classically involving all four glands, though often asymmetrically.
• Hyperplastic glands lack the peripheral rim of compressed normal tissue.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the predominant cell type and its arrangement in a typical parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Uniform, monomorphic polygonal chief cells
• Small, centrally placed nuclei with light to dark pink cytoplasm
• Arrayed in sheets, cords, or small follicles.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In both parathyroid adenoma and hyperplasia, the amount of stromal [___] is characteristically inconspicuous compared to the normal gland.
back:
• Adipose tissue (Fat)
• Normal adult glands contain up to 30% fat
• Neoplastic or hyperplastic proliferation replaces these fat stores with chief cells.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with MEN-1 syndrome presents with primary hyperparathyroidism. Neck exploration reveals all four glands are enlarged. This microscopic pattern is consistent with [___].
back:
• Primary Parathyroid Hyperplasia
• Strongly associated with familial syndromes like MEN-1 and MEN-2A
• Usually presents as diffuse or nodular chief cell hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the microscopic appearance of 'oxyphil cells' and 'water-clear cells' in parathyroid lesions.
back:
• Oxyphil cells: Larger than chief cells, acidophilic granular cytoplasm (mitochondria-rich).
• Water-clear cells: Chief cells containing abundant intracytoplasmic glycogen, seen in specific hyperplasia variants.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the diagnostic criteria for parathyroid carcinoma versus parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Circumscribed, uniform cells; lack of invasion.
• Carcinoma: Requires invasion of surrounding tissues (thyroid, neck soft tissue) or documented metastasis.
• Cytologic detail and 'endocrine atypia' are unreliable for malignancy.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Define 'endocrine atypia' as it appears in parathyroid adenoma histology.
back:
• Presence of bizarre, pleomorphic, or monstrous nuclei
• Found even in benign adenomas
• Does not indicate malignancy on its own; requires evidence of invasion.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A characteristic histologic feature of a parathyroid adenoma that helps distinguish it from primary hyperplasia is the presence of a rim of [___] at the edge of the lesion.
back:
• Compressed, non-neoplastic parathyroid tissue
• Usually separated from the tumor by a delicate fibrous capsule
• Helps confirm the solitary nature of the neoplastic process

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. A sestamibi scan reveals solitary uptake in the left superior gland. Upon surgical excision, the most likely finding regarding stromal fat within the lesion is [___].
back:
• Stromal fat is inconspicuous or absent
• Neoplastic chief cells replace the normal 30% fat content
• Useful marker to differentiate from normal parathyroid parenchyma

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the significance of "endocrine atypia" when evaluating the nuclear features of a suspected parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Refers to bizarre, pleomorphic nuclei found within benign adenomas
• Does not indicate malignancy or anaplastic transformation
• Mitotic figures remain rare in these cases

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the glandular involvement pattern of Primary Parathyroid Hyperplasia with that of a typical Parathyroid Adenoma.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary gland involvement; remaining glands are often shrunken/atrophic
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular (all four glands) involvement; often asymmetric and may include islands of oxyphils

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the two most common molecular defects involved in the pathogenesis of sporadic parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Cyclin D1 (CCDN1) gene inversions: Leading to protein overexpression
• MEN1 mutations: Inactivating mutations of the tumor suppressor gene (found in ~35%)

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In Primary Parathyroid Hyperplasia, the most common microscopic growth pattern observed is [___].
back:
• Chief cell hyperplasia
• Can manifest as a diffuse or multinodular pattern
• Adipose tissue is decreased within the hyperplastic areas

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A surgeon removes an enlarged parathyroid gland weighing 15 grams that is adherent to the surrounding neck structures. Histology shows uniform cells within a dense fibrous capsule. The definitive diagnosis of carcinoma in this case requires [___].
back:
• Evidence of invasion into surrounding tissues
• Clinically documented metastases
• Note: Cytologic pleomorphism and capsular entrapment are unreliable for diagnosing malignancy here

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of the CCDN1 pericentromeric inversion in the development of parathyroid adenomas.
back:
• Relocates the Cyclin D1 gene adjacent to the PTH gene promoter
• PTH promoter triggers constitutive Cyclin D1 overexpression
• Overexpression acts as a mitogen to drive cell cycle progression

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the typical gross appearance of a Parathyroid Adenoma with the glands in Primary Hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Solitary, soft, tan-to-reddish brown nodule with a thin capsule
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular enlargement; combined weight usually exceeds 1 gram but often less than massive adenomas

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Name the cell type characterized by abundant acidophilic cytoplasm and mitochondria that can be seen in both parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma variants.
back:
• Oxyphil cells
• Found in small nests in hyperplasia
• Can comprise the entire population in rare 'Oxyphil Adenomas'

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Approximately 10-20% of sporadic parathyroid adenomas exhibit a chromosomal inversion that places the [___] gene under the control of the PTH promoter.
back:
• **Cyclin D1** (CCDN1)
• Results in protein overexpression
• Functions as a major cell cycle regulator driving neoplastic proliferation.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia. Imaging reveals a solitary, 2 cm, soft, tan-colored mass at the inferior pole of the right thyroid lobe. Identify the most likely histopathological diagnosis.
back:
• **Parathyroid Adenoma**
• Usually solitary and encapsulated
• Accounts for 85-95% of primary hyperparathyroidism cases.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Describe the appearance and relationship of the "non-neoplastic" parathyroid tissue located immediately adjacent to a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• **Compressed rim** of normal tissue
• Often separated from the adenoma by a delicate fibrous capsule
• Other glands are usually shrunken/atrophic due to hypercalcemia feedback.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the pattern of glandular involvement seen in primary parathyroid hyperplasia with that found in a solitary parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• **Hyperplasia:** Multiglandular involvement (classically all four glands, though often asymmetric).
• **Adenoma:** Solitary involvement; remaining glands are suppressed and normal or small in size.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Interpret the clinical significance of finding nuclear pleomorphism and "bizarre" nuclei (endocrine atypia) within a well-circumscribed parathyroid mass.
back:
• It is **not** a criterion for malignancy
• Termed "endocrine atypia"
• Malignancy requires evidence of capsular/vascular invasion or distant metastasis.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In the histological assessment of parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia, [___] is characteristically inconspicuous or absent compared to the ~30% volume found in a normal adult gland.
back:
• **Stromal fat** (adipose tissue)
• Loss of fat is a key marker of hypercellularity
• Helps distinguish hyperfunctional tissue from normal parenchyma.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with a germline mutation in the *MEN1* gene presents with elevated serum calcium. Identify the specific histopathological pattern of parathyroid growth expected.
back:
• **Primary Hyperplasia**
• Multiglandular and often nodular
• Usually the earliest manifestation of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of total glandular weight in the differential diagnosis of primary parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Combined weight of all glands is usually **< 1.0 gram**
• Distinguishes hyperplasia from large parathyroid carcinomas (often >10g)
• Individual glands in hyperplasia may only be subtly enlarged.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the histological features of "Chief cell" hyperplasia with the rarer "Water-clear cell" hyperplasia.
back:
• **Chief cell:** Polygonal cells with light/dark pink cytoplasm containing PTH granules.
• **Water-clear cell:** Cells contain abundant cytoplasmic **glycogen**, appearing transparent.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the definitive histological feature required to diagnose a parathyroid carcinoma rather than a large adenoma.
back:
• **Invasion** of surrounding tissues or blood vessels
• **Metastasis** to distant sites or regional lymph nodes
• Mass size often exceeds 10g.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The histological distinction of a parathyroid adenoma from the surrounding normal gland is primarily marked by a delicate fibrous capsule and a rim of [___] parathyroid tissue.
back:
• Compressed, non-neoplastic tissue.
• This rim is usually atrophic due to feedback inhibition from hypercalcemia.
• Absence of stromal fat within the adenoma itself.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 52-year-old female presents with recurrent renal stones and high serum calcium. Surgical exploration reveals one enlarged gland (2g) and three small, shrunken glands. Identify the most likely underlying lesion and the state of the non-enlarged glands.
back:
• Diagnosis: Parathyroid Adenoma.
• State of other glands: Atrophic/Suppressed.
• Mechanism: High calcium from the adenoma suppresses PTH in normal glands.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the role of stromal adipose tissue (fat) as a diagnostic marker in parathyroid hyperplasia.
back:
• Normal glands contain ~30% stromal fat.
• In hyperplasia, fat is markedly reduced or absent within the proliferating areas.
• This reduction confirms increased parenchymal cell mass.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the typical number of glands involved in parathyroid hyperplasia versus those involved in a solitary adenoma.
back:
• Hyperplasia: Multiglandular involvement (classically all four glands, though often asymmetrically).
• Adenoma: Monoglandular involvement (solitary nodule).
• Hyperplasia is common in familial syndromes like MEN-1.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Define 'endocrine atypia' in the context of parathyroid adenoma microscopy.
back:
• Refers to enlarged, pleomorphic, or bizarre nuclei.
• It is a benign finding in parathyroid and other endocrine tissues.
• Does not indicate malignancy/carcinoma.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The predominant cell type constituting both parathyroid adenomas and hyperplasia is the [___].
back:
• Chief cell.
• Polygonal cells with central nuclei and pale-to-dark pink cytoplasm.
• Organized in sheets, cords, or small follicles.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A patient with MEN-1 syndrome presents with primary hyperparathyroidism. Histology of the resected glands shows a combined weight of 1.2g and nodules of chief cells lacking a distinct capsule between hyperplastic and normal tissue. Identify the lesion.
back:
• Parathyroid Hyperplasia.
• Diffuse or nodular chief cell proliferation.
• Characteristically associated with MEN-1 and MEN-2A syndromes.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the definitive histological criteria required to diagnose parathyroid carcinoma as opposed to an adenoma with nuclear atypia.
back:
• Requires evidence of local tissue invasion (capsular/vascular).
• Or documented metastasis.
• Cytological pleomorphism alone is insufficient for a diagnosis of malignancy.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the cytoplasmic characteristics of oxyphil cells with chief cells in the parathyroid gland.
back:
• Oxyphil cells: Larger, acidophilic, granular cytoplasm packed with mitochondria.
• Chief cells: Smaller, uniform, containing PTH secretory granules.
• Oxyphils increase with age and can form rare 'oxyphil adenomas'.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Which specific architectural arrangement is characteristically absent in parathyroid adenomas but present in the normal gland?
back:
• Intraselular/Stromal fat.
• Normal glands have prominent adipocytes interspersed between cells.
• Adenomas are composed of solid, nearly fat-free cellular sheets.

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: The most common molecular alteration in sporadic parathyroid adenomas, involving a pericentromeric inversion on chromosome 11, leads to the overexpression of the cell cycle regulator [___].
back:
• Cyclin D1 (CCDN1)
• Promotes unchecked cellular proliferation
• Seen in 10%–20% of sporadic adenomas

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 55-year-old female presents with hypercalcemia and a solitary 2-cm tan parathyroid mass. Upon surgical exploration, the remaining three glands are shrunken and atrophic. Name the diagnosis.
back:
• Parathyroid Adenoma
• Solitary, encapsulated nature
• Feedback inhibition from hypercalcemia causes atrophy of non-neoplastic glands

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the histopathological feature that distinguishes a parathyroid adenoma from the surrounding non-neoplastic parathyroid tissue in a biopsy specimen.
back:
• Presence of a well-defined fibrous capsule
• A peripheral rim of compressed, non-neoplastic parathyroid parenchyma
• Monomorphism of neoplastic chief cells

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: During neck exploration for hypercalcemia, a patient is found to have a 1-gram nodule on the right superior gland, while the other three appear grossly normal. Contrast the expected histologic state of those three glands if the diagnosis is adenoma versus hyperplasia.
back:
• Adenoma: Other glands are shrunken/atrophic due to feedback inhibition
• Hyperplasia: All glands are typically involved, though often asymmetrically

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Identify the primary cell type found in both parathyroid adenomas and hyperplastic glands, characterized by a polygonal shape and centrally placed nuclei.
back:
• Chief cells
• Contain secretory granules of PTH
• Uniform (monomorphic) in adenomas

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: In primary parathyroid hyperplasia, the combined weight of all four affected glands typically rarely exceeds [___].
back:
• 1.0 gram
• Total weight is often less than this despite multiglandular involvement

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: A 40-year-old with a family history of MEN-1 presents with hypercalcemia. Histology reveals diffuse chief cell growth and absent stromal fat across all four parathyroid glands. Identify the lesion.
back:
• Parathyroid Hyperplasia
• Multiglandular involvement is hallmark of MEN-1
• Diffuse or multinodular growth pattern

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Explain the diagnostic criteria required to differentiate a widely invasive parathyroid carcinoma from an adenoma exhibiting 'endocrine atypia' and high cellularity.
back:
• Invasion of surrounding tissues
• Distant metastasis
• Cytologic atypia/mitoses are unreliable for malignancy in parathyroid tissue

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Contrast the microscopic distribution of stromal adipose tissue in a normal adult parathyroid gland versus a parathyroid adenoma.
back:
• Normal: Adipose tissue comprises up to 30-40% of the gland
• Adenoma: Stromal fat is inconspicuous or absent within the neoplastic nodule

category: Describe the histopathological features of parathyroid hyperplasia and adenoma
front: Name the secondary cell type found in parathyroid adenomas that is larger than chief cells and contains abundant mitochondria-rich eosinophilic cytoplasm.
back:
• Oxyphil cells
• Often found in small nests or as a pure oxyphil adenoma
• Distinctly acidophilic cytoplasm
